knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Constrained QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic objective over a coordinatewise box, allowing absent lower or upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) in \(\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}\), lower bounds \(\ell\in(\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\})^n\), and upper bounds \(u\in(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\})^n\) satisfying \(\ell_i\le u_i\) for every \(i\), a convex bound-constrained quadratic program is
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c
\quad\text{subject to}\quad \ell\le x\le u.
\]
The inequalities are componentwise, and absent lower or upper bounds are represented by \(-\infty\) or \(+\infty\), respectively. The feasible set is the closed convex box \([\ell,u]=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ell\le x\le u\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex bound-constrained QP minimizes a quadratic function with a positive-semidefinite quadratic matrix over componentwise lower and upper bounds, with infinite endpoints representing absent bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
\(\ell\in(\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\})^n\), \(u\in(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\})^n\), and \(\ell_i\le u_i\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c:\ell\le x\le u\}\) is a convex quadratic program over a closed convex box.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic programming over an affine equality set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), an equality-constrained quadratic program is
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b.
\]
It is convex when \(Q\succeq0\). Feasibility means \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\); no full-row-rank assumption on \(A\) is part of the definition. The feasible region is the affine set \(\{x:Ax=b\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-constrained QP minimizes a quadratic objective on an affine set defined by linear equations.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
\(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c:Ax=b\}\) is a convex equality-constrained quadratic program.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Equality Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix representation of the equality block in a mixed-constraint QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a decision vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), an explicit linear equality block is represented by \(Ax=b\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e}\). Equivalently, with the affine residual \(r_e(x)=Ax-b\), the equality block is
\[
r_e(x)=0.
\]
Rows of \(A\) need not be linearly independent, although feasibility requires \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\). In a mixed QP this block remains explicit rather than being absorbed into the objective or converted into paired inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit equalities are stored as a matrix equation Ax=b, equivalently as a vanishing affine residual.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e}\).
\(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\) when feasibility is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\iff r_e(x):=Ax-b=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Inequality Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix representation of the one-sided inequality block in a mixed QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), an explicit linear inequality block is represented componentwise by \(Gx\le h\), where \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i\times n}\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i}\). With affine residual \(r_i(x)=Gx-h\), the same block is
\[
r_i(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i}_{-}.
\]
A two-sided scalar constraint may be encoded by two rows, while an equality should ordinarily remain in a separate equality block. The inequality feasible set is a closed convex polyhedron, possibly empty or unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit inequalities are stored as Gx≤h, equivalently by requiring an affine residual to lie in the nonpositive orthant.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i\times n}\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Gx\le h\iff r_i(x):=Gx-h\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i}_{-}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General quadratic-objective models having only explicit linear inequality constraints; convexity is not assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quadratic program with only inequality constraints has the form
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\;c^Tx+\frac12x^TGx
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax\ge b,
\]
where \(G\) and \(c\) are constant problem data. In an active-set representation, \(\widehat A_k\) is the matrix of working constraints at \(x_k\), and the columns of \(Z_k\) form a basis for the vectors orthogonal to the rows of \(\widehat A_k\), equivalently \(\operatorname{range}(Z_k)=\ker(\widehat A_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality-constrained quadratic program minimizes a quadratic objective subject to explicit linear inequalities. Its active-set representation records the current working constraints in A-hat and uses Z as a basis for their null space. The definition does not require convexity.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb R^n
G\in\mathbb R^{n\times n},\ c\in\mathbb R^n\text{ are constant problem data}
Ax\ge b
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{QP}:\ \min_x\ c^Tx+\tfrac12x^TGx\ \text{s.t.}\ Ax\ge b,\qquad \operatorname{range}(Z_k)=\ker(\widehat A_k).

children.title: Mixed-Constraint QP Structure
children.top_down_role: Structural interaction between equality blocks and inequality blocks within a single explicit QP representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Constraint QP Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical convex QP with separate equality and inequality blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A convex QP with explicit mixed linear constraints has the canonical representation
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\qquad Gx\le h,
\]
where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). The equality and inequality rows are stored separately because their multipliers have different domains: equality multipliers are unrestricted, whereas inequality multipliers are nonnegative under the displayed sign convention. Bounds are included by choosing rows of \(G\) from signed coordinate vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-constraint QP combines a convex quadratic objective with separate linear equality and one-sided inequality blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
\(A,G\) have \(n\) columns and compatible right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set is \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\), a convex polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Affine-Image QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic programming with bounds imposed on an affine image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) in \(\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(d\in\mathbb{R}^m\), lower bounds \(\ell\in(\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\})^m\), and upper bounds \(u\in(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\})^m\) satisfying \(\ell_i\le u_i\) for every \(i\), a two-sided affine-image QP is
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x
\quad\text{subject to}\quad \ell\le Ax+d\le u.
\]
Equal finite endpoints encode equalities, while \(-\infty\) and \(+\infty\) encode absent lower and upper sides, respectively. With \(a(x)=Ax+d\), the feasible region is \(a^{-1}([\ell,u])\), a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This convex QP constrains every component of an affine image Ax+d between lower and upper bounds; equal finite endpoints encode equalities and infinite endpoints encode absent sides.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
\(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
\(\ell\in(\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\})^m\), \(u\in(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\})^m\), and \(\ell_i\le u_i\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With \(a(x)=Ax+d\), the feasible set \(\{x:\ell\le a(x)\le u\}=a^{-1}([\ell,u])\) is closed and convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-plus-Indicator Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite extended-value representation of a convex constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty closed convex set encoding the QP constraints, and define its indicator by \(\delta_C(x)=0\) for \(x\in C\) and \(\delta_C(x)=+\infty\) otherwise. Then
\[
\min_{x\in C}\;\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c
\quad\equiv\quad
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c+\delta_C(x).
\]
For \(Q\succeq0\), this is the sum of a differentiable convex quadratic and a proper closed convex function, the standard composite form for proximal splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained convex QP equals unconstrained minimization of its quadratic objective plus the feasible-set indicator.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
\(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}(f(x)+\delta_C(x))\).

notation.meaning: extended-value indicator of the feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Inclusion Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order optimality representation for a convex QP over a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c\) with \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). A point \(x^\star\in C\) solves \(\min_{x\in C}f(x)\) if and only if
\[
0\in Qx^\star+q+N_C(x^\star),
\]
where \(N_C(x)=\{v:\langle v,y-x\rangle\le0\ \text{for every }y\in C\}\) for \(x\in C\), and \(N_C(x)=\varnothing\) otherwise. Thus QP optimality is a monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point minimizes a convex QP exactly when the negative quadratic gradient belongs to the feasible set’s normal cone.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
\(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\iff0\in Qx^\star+q+N_C(x^\star)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Monotone-Inclusion Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator form separating the affine quadratic gradient from the constraint normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the convex QP \(\min_{x\in C}\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c\), define the affine operator \(F(x)=Qx+q\) and the set-valued operator \(T=F+N_C\). If \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) and \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, then \(F\) is monotone and
\[
0\in T(x^\star)=Qx^\star+q+N_C(x^\star)
\]
is equivalent to primal optimality. This representation exposes an affine single-valued part and a normal-cone part suitable for forward-backward or related operator splittings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex QP optimality is the zero of a monotone operator formed from an affine gradient plus a normal cone.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
\(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=Q(\cdot)+q\) is monotone and \(x^\star\) is optimal exactly when \(0\in(F+N_C)(x^\star)\).

notation.meaning: normal-cone operator of the feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Saddle Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-concave saddle representation of a mixed linear-constraint QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the convex QP with \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), define
\[
L(x,y,z)=\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c+y^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)+z^{\mathsf T}(Gx-h),
\qquad z\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i}_{+}.
\]
Its Lagrangian saddle problem is
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e},\ z\ge0}L(x,y,z).
\]
When a primal-dual saddle point \((x^\star,y^\star,z^\star)\) exists, it satisfies \(L(x^\star,y,z)\le L(x^\star,y^\star,z^\star)\le L(x,y^\star,z^\star)\) for every admissible \(x,y,z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixed convex QP becomes a convex-concave saddle problem using unrestricted equality multipliers and nonnegative inequality multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
The primal constraint convention is \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A primal-dual solution is a saddle point of \(L\) over \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e}\), and \(z\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i}_{+}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Quadratic Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit dual of an equality-constrained QP with positive-definite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_x\;\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,
\]
where \(Q\succ0\). Minimizing its Lagrangian over \(x\) gives \(x(y)=-Q^{-1}(q+A^{\mathsf T}y)\) and the concave dual QP
\[
\max_{y\in\mathbb{R}^m}\;c-b^{\mathsf T}y-\frac12(q+A^{\mathsf T}y)^{\mathsf T}Q^{-1}(q+A^{\mathsf T}y).
\]
Equivalently, after discarding constants, it minimizes \(\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}AQ^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}y+(b+AQ^{-1}q)^{\mathsf T}y\). If the affine primal set is nonempty, the primal and dual optimal values coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the primal variable from an equality-constrained QP produces a quadratic dual in the unrestricted equality multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
\(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed primal and dual QPs have equal optimal values, and \(x^\star=-Q^{-1}(q+A^{\mathsf T}y^\star)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual KKT Operator Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone operator encoding stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity for a mixed convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), and \(z\ge0\), set \(w=(x,y,z)\). The KKT system is the zero inclusion
\[
0\in\mathcal{T}(w):=
\begin{pmatrix}Q&A^{\mathsf T}&G^{\mathsf T}\\-A&0&0\\-G&0&0\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}
+
\begin{pmatrix}q\\b\\h\end{pmatrix}
+
\begin{pmatrix}0\\0\\N_{\mathbb{R}^{m_i}_{+}}(z)\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(Q\succeq0\), the affine matrix operator is monotone: its symmetric part is \(\operatorname{diag}(Q,0,0)\). The three block rows encode stationarity, equality feasibility, and inequality feasibility with complementary slackness, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixed-QP KKT conditions form one monotone zero inclusion in the primal vector and equality and inequality multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
The constraints use the convention \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), and \(z\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\mathcal{T}(x,y,z)\) is equivalent to the primal-dual KKT conditions for the convex QP.

notation.meaning: normal cone to the nonnegative multiplier orthant

knowledge_statements.title: Separable QP Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines objective and feasible-set separability for a convex block QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), where \(x_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\). A convex QP has separable components when it can be written as \[\min_{x_i\in C_i}\ \sum_{i=1}^m\left(\tfrac12x_i^{\mathsf T}P_i x_i+q_i^{\mathsf T}x_i+r_i\right),\] where \(P_i\in\mathbb S_+^{n_i}\) and each \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is a nonempty closed convex polyhedron. In this representation, \(P=\operatorname{diag}(P_1,\ldots,P_m)\), \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\), and every displayed objective or constraint component involves only one variable block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex QP is separable in a given block representation when its Hessian is block diagonal and its polyhedral feasible set is a Cartesian product of block feasible sets.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge1\) and \(n_i\ge1\) for every \(i\).
\(P_i\succeq0\) and each \(C_i\) is a nonempty closed convex polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{diag}(P_1,\ldots,P_m)\) and \(C=\prod_{i=1}^m C_i\).

notation.meaning: polyhedral feasible set for block i

children.title: Block-Structured QP Systems
children.top_down_role: Variable, Hessian, and constraint partitions expressed through compatible block organization.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Structured QP Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents a QP and its optimality system using conformal variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-constrained convex QP \[\min_x\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\] partition \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\) and write \(P=[P_{ij}]_{i,j=1}^m\) and \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_m]\). Its primal-dual optimality equations have the block system \[\begin{bmatrix}P_{11}&\cdots&P_{1m}&A_1^{\mathsf T}\\ \vdots&\ddots&\vdots&\vdots\\ P_{m1}&\cdots&P_{mm}&A_m^{\mathsf T}\\ A_1&\cdots&A_m&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\ \vdots\\ x_m\\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-q_1\\ \vdots\\ -q_m\\ b\end{bmatrix}.\] The nonzero off-diagonal blocks explicitly identify cross-block interactions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning variables exposes the QP Hessian and KKT equations as a block system whose off-diagonal blocks encode interactions.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
The displayed block partitions are dimensionally conformal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The QP optimality equations admit the displayed block KKT representation.

notation.meaning: Hessian block coupling variable blocks i and j
constraint columns associated with block i

children.title: Cross-Block Coupling Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural features that preserve, weaken, or destroy decomposition across QP blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Block Coupling Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies cross-block coupling in a fixed block representation of a QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a QP with variable blocks \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\), Hessian blocks \(P_{ij}\), and a fixed row representation of its linear constraints. In this representation, distinct blocks \(i\) and \(j\) are structurally uncoupled when \(P_{ij}=0\) and no displayed constraint row has nonzero coefficients in both blocks. The representation is block separable when this condition holds for every \(i\ne j\), so that its constraint rows can be grouped into block-local systems and its feasible set is the Cartesian product of the resulting block feasible sets. A nonzero \(P_{ij}\) or a displayed constraint row involving both blocks is a cross-block coupling in that representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a fixed QP representation, blocks are structurally uncoupled when neither an off-diagonal Hessian block nor a displayed constraint row joins them.
assumptions_latex: The objective and linear constraints have a fixed dimensionally conformal block representation.
Constraint incidence is assessed from the displayed rows, without removing or reformulating redundant constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed representation is block separable when \(P_{ij}=0\) for all \(i\ne j\) and every constraint row is supported on at most one variable block.

notation.meaning: Hessian block coupling variable blocks i and j

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus-Coupled QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a separable local QP coupled solely through consensus equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A consensus-coupled convex QP is a problem of the form \[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z}\ \sum_{i=1}^m\left(\tfrac12x_i^{\mathsf T}P_i x_i+q_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\right)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i=z\ \ (i=1,\ldots,m),\quad x_i\in C_i,\] where \(P_i\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and each \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed and convex. More generally, linear consensus may be written \(E_i x_i=z\) when the images share a common dimension. Removing the consensus equalities leaves independent local QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consensus QP has separable local quadratic objectives and sets, linked only by equalities requiring local variables or their images to agree.
assumptions_latex: \(P_i\succeq0\) for every agent.
Each \(C_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The only cross-block coupling is \(x_i=z\), or its linear-image form \(E_i x_i=z\).

children.title: Sequence-Structured QP Models
children.top_down_role: Stage-indexed variables, local interactions, and endpoint structure in ordered QP models.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequence-Structured QP Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines finite-horizon QPs whose terms have bounded temporal interaction range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(x_0,\ldots,x_T)\), with \(x_t\in\mathbb R^d\). A QP is sequence-structured with interaction radius \(r\) when every quadratic term involving \(x_s\) and \(x_t\) satisfies \(|s-t|\le r\), and every constraint row depends only on variables from some window \((x_t,\ldots,x_{t+r})\). Thus it admits the form \[\min_x\ \tfrac12\sum_{|s-t|\le r}x_s^{\mathsf T}Q_{st}x_t+\sum_{t=0}^Tq_t^{\mathsf T}x_t\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad Gx\le h,\] with temporally local row supports in \(A\) and \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence-structured QP orders variables by time and restricts every objective interaction and constraint to a bounded temporal window.
assumptions_latex: \(T\ge0\), \(d\ge1\), and \(0\le r\le T\).
The assembled quadratic form is convex when convexity is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All objective and constraint interactions occur within temporal distance \(r\).

notation.meaning: decision vector at sequence position t
quadratic interaction block between positions s and t

children.title: Banded QP Matrices

knowledge_statements.title: Banded QP Matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines block-banded Hessians and temporally local constraint matrices under sequence ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the ordering \(x=(x_0,\ldots,x_T)\), a symmetric block matrix \(P=[P_{st}]_{s,t=0}^T\) has block half-bandwidth at most \(r\) when \(P_{st}=0\) for every \(|s-t|>r\). Its block half-bandwidth equals \(r\) when this bound is attained, except that the zero matrix may be assigned bandwidth zero by convention. A constraint matrix has temporally local row support of radius \(r\) when every row is supported on variable blocks contained in some consecutive window \(x_t,\ldots,x_{\min\{t+r,T\}}\). A QP has banded sequence matrices when its Hessian and constraint matrices satisfy these respective conditions under the same variable ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under sequence ordering, a QP has banded sequence matrices when its Hessian vanishes beyond a fixed block diagonal band and every constraint row uses a bounded consecutive window of variable blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le r\le T\).
All matrix blocks conform to the fixed sequence partition \(x=(x_0,\ldots,x_T)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{st}=0\) whenever \(|s-t|>r\), and every constraint row has support in a consecutive window of at most \(r+1\) variable blocks.

notation.meaning: Hessian block at sequence positions s and t
Hessian half-bandwidth bound and constraint-support radius

children.title: Sequence-to-Bandwidth Correspondence
children.top_down_role: How local sequence couplings induce banded or block-banded QP algebra.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequence-to-Bandwidth Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates bounded temporal interactions to block bandwidth after chronological ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Order the variables of a sequence-structured QP as \(x=(x_0,
\ldots,x_T)\). If every quadratic interaction joins positions \(s,t\) with \(|s-t|\le r\), then its Hessian satisfies \(P_{st}=0\) for \(|s-t|>r\) and hence has block half-bandwidth at most \(r\). Conversely, a block-banded Hessian of half-bandwidth \(r\) contains no quadratic interaction beyond temporal distance \(r\). If each constraint row is supported on at most \(r+1\) consecutive positions, the constraint matrix has the corresponding block-banded row structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chronological ordering converts a temporal interaction radius of r into block half-bandwidth at most r, and bandedness excludes longer-range quadratic interactions.
assumptions_latex: Variables are ordered chronologically by sequence position.
Matrix blocks use the same partition as the sequence model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Temporal radius \(r\) is equivalent to Hessian block half-bandwidth at most \(r\).

notation.meaning: temporal interaction radius and resulting bandwidth bound
Hessian block joining positions s and t

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Pattern Parametric QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a parameterized QP whose matrix sparsity pattern remains invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta\in\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p\). A fixed-pattern parametric QP is a family \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}P(\theta)x+q(\theta)^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(\theta)x=b(\theta),\quad G(\theta)x\le h(\theta),\] for which the dimensions and structural nonzero patterns of \(P(\theta)\), \(A(\theta)\), and \(G(\theta)\) are independent of \(\theta\). Numerical values and right-hand sides may vary with \(\theta\). In the convex family, \(P(\theta)\succeq0\) for every admissible parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-pattern parametric QP changes numerical data with a parameter while preserving dimensions and the structural nonzero locations of all matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is nonempty.
Matrix dimensions are constant over \(\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structural sparsity patterns of \(P(\theta)\), \(A(\theta)\), and \(G(\theta)\) do not depend on \(\theta\).

children.title: Box Projection
children.top_down_role: Projection geometry for finite lower and upper bounds on individual coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Box Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the Euclidean projector onto a closed axis-aligned box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,n\}\), where \(-\infty<\ell_i\le u_i<+\infty\). For every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), the Euclidean projection \(\Pi_B(v)=\arg\min_{x\in B}\tfrac12\|x-v\|_2^2\) is unique and is computed componentwise by \[\bigl(\Pi_B(v)\bigr)_i=\min\{u_i,\max\{\ell_i,v_i\}\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\] Thus box projection requires only independent scalar clipping operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Euclidean projection onto a finite box clips each coordinate independently to its lower and upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(v\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(-\infty<\ell_i\le u_i<+\infty\) for every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(\Pi_B(v)\bigr)_i=\min\{u_i,\max\{\ell_i,v_i\}\}\).

children.title: Orthant Projection
children.top_down_role: Projection geometry for coordinatewise sign restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthant Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives coordinatewise Euclidean projection onto nonnegative and signed orthants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sign vector \(s\in\{-1,1\}^n\), define the closed orthant \(O_s=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:s_i x_i\ge0\text{ for all }i\}\). Its Euclidean projector is unique and satisfies \[\bigl(\Pi_{O_s}(v)\bigr)_i=s_i\max\{s_i v_i,0\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\] In particular, for the nonnegative orthant \(\mathbb R_+^n\), \(\Pi_{\mathbb R_+^n}(v)=(\max\{v_i,0\})_{i=1}^n\), while projection onto the nonpositive orthant is componentwise minimum with zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto an orthant independently replaces every coordinate having the forbidden sign by zero and leaves all other coordinates unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(v\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(\Pi_{O_s}(v)\bigr)_i=s_i\max\{s_i v_i,0\}\).

notation.meaning: orthant determined by sign vector s

children.title: Infinite-Bound Specializations
children.top_down_role: Transitions from two-sided boxes to one-sided or unrestricted coordinate regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Bound Specializations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends coordinatewise box projection to one-sided and absent bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\}\), where \(\ell_i\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\), \(u_i\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and \(\ell_i\le u_i\). For every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), the Euclidean projection is coordinatewise and satisfies \[\bigl(\Pi_B(v)\bigr)_i=\begin{cases}\min\{u_i,\max\{\ell_i,v_i\}\},&\ell_i\in\mathbb R,\ u_i\in\mathbb R,\\ \min\{u_i,v_i\},&\ell_i=-\infty,\ u_i\in\mathbb R,\\ \max\{\ell_i,v_i\},&\ell_i\in\mathbb R,\ u_i=+\infty,\\ v_i,&\ell_i=-\infty,\ u_i=+\infty.\end{cases}\] Thus each missing bound removes its corresponding clipping operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With one infinite bound, box projection applies only the remaining finite clip; with both bounds infinite, it leaves the coordinate unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(v\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(\ell_i\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\), \(u_i\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and \(\ell_i\le u_i\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each coordinate of \(\Pi_B(v)\) is obtained by applying exactly its finite lower and upper bounds.

notation.meaning: closed axis-aligned box with possibly infinite bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Space Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the Euclidean projector onto a nonempty affine equality set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}\) be nonempty. For every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), the Euclidean projection onto \(C\) is \[\Pi_C(v)=v-A^{\mathsf T}(AA^{\mathsf T})^{\dagger}(Av-b),\] where the expression is valid without a row-rank assumption. If \(A\) has full row rank, then \((AA^{\mathsf T})^{\dagger}=(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\). The projected point satisfies \(A\Pi_C(v)=b\), and the displacement \(v-\Pi_C(v)\) lies in \(\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a nonempty affine equality set corrects the point along the row space using the pseudoinverse of the constraint Gram matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(v\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(C=\{x:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_C(v)=v-A^{\mathsf T}(AA^{\mathsf T})^{\dagger}(Av-b)\).

children.title: Simplex Projection
children.top_down_role: Projection onto nonnegative vectors subject to a fixed total-mass constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection onto a scaled probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(b>0\), let \(\Delta_b=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:x\geq0,\ \mathbf 1^Tx=b\}\). Its Euclidean projection is uniquely given by
\[P_{\Delta_b}(v)_i=\max\{v_i-\tau,0\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n,\]
where \(\tau\in\mathbb{R}\) is the unique threshold satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^n\max\{v_i-\tau,0\}=b\). Equivalently, if \(v_{(1)}\geq\cdots\geq v_{(n)}\), then \(\rho=\max\{j:v_{(j)}-(\sum_{i=1}^jv_{(i)}-b)/j>0\}\) and \(\tau=(\sum_{i=1}^{\rho}v_{(i)}-b)/\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simplex projection subtracts a common threshold and truncates at zero; the threshold is selected so the projected coordinates sum to the prescribed budget.
assumptions_latex: \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\Delta_b}(v)_i=\max\{v_i-\tau,0\}\) with \(\sum_iP_{\Delta_b}(v)_i=b\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative simplex of total mass b

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the threshold representation of simplex projection.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and content kind fit the simplex-projection leaf, and the threshold formula is mathematically standard, but no inspectable citation supports either the threshold or sorting characterization.

children.title: Budget-Set Projection
children.top_down_role: Projection onto resource-budget regions with inequality-based aggregate limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Budget-Set Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection onto a nonnegative inequality-budget set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(b\geq0\), define \(B_b=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:x\geq0,\ \mathbf 1^Tx\leq b\}\). Let \(v_+=\max\{v,0\}\) componentwise. If \(\mathbf 1^Tv_+\leq b\), then \(P_{B_b}(v)=v_+\). Otherwise,
\[P_{B_b}(v)_i=\max\{v_i-\tau,0\},\]
where the unique \(\tau>0\) satisfies \(\sum_i\max\{v_i-\tau,0\}=b\). Thus projection either clips negative coordinates or reduces to projection onto the active simplex boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection first clips negative entries. If the budget is then exceeded, a common positive threshold is subtracted until the budget constraint is active.
assumptions_latex: \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\)
\(b\geq0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{B_b}(v)=v_+\) when \(\mathbf 1^Tv_+\leq b\), and otherwise \(P_{B_b}(v)_i=\max\{v_i-\tau,0\}\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the budget set

children.title: Weighted Budget Geometry
children.top_down_role: Projection regimes in which coordinates consume unequal portions of an aggregate budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Budget Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection onto a positively weighted nonnegative budget set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\), \(b\geq0\), and \(B_{w,b}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:x\geq0,\ w^Tx\leq b\}\). For \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), its Euclidean projection satisfies
\[P_{B_{w,b}}(v)_i=\max\{v_i-\lambda w_i,0\}.\]
If \(w^Tv_+\leq b\), then \(\lambda=0\); otherwise \(\lambda>0\) is the unique solution of \(\sum_iw_i\max\{v_i-\lambda w_i,0\}=b\). The active coordinates change only at breakpoints \(v_i/w_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted budget projection subtracts a multiplier times each coordinate’s weight, truncating at zero; the multiplier makes the weighted budget active when necessary.
assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\)
\(b\geq0\)
\(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{B_{w,b}}(v)_i=\max\{v_i-\lambda w_i,0\}\) with complementary budget activity.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports weighted budget projection or its breakpoint characterization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits weighted budget geometry, but no citation supports the multiplier formula, uniqueness assertion, or breakpoint characterization.

knowledge_statements.title: General Polyhedral Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT characterization of Euclidean projection onto a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b,\ Ex=d\}\) be nonempty and closed. For every \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the projection \(x^*=P_C(v)\) is the unique minimizer of \(\tfrac12\|x-v\|_2^2\) over \(C\). It is equivalently characterized by the existence of multipliers \(\lambda\geq0\) and \(\nu\) such that
\[x^*-v+A^T\lambda+E^T\nu=0,\quad Ax^*\leq b,\quad Ex^*=d,\quad \lambda_i(Ax^*-b)_i=0\ \text{for all }i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a nonempty polyhedron is a strictly convex quadratic program whose unique solution is characterized by primal feasibility, stationarity, dual feasibility, and complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\{x:Ax\leq b,\ Ex=d\}\neq\varnothing\)
\(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*=P_C(v)\) if and only if the displayed primal-dual KKT system holds.
review_flags: The supplied polyhedral-set locator does not directly certify the projection KKT characterization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A KKT representation is appropriate for this leaf and is standard for polyhedral projection, but no source directly supports it; the dimensions of A, E, b, d, lambda, and nu are also not introduced explicitly.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Cauchy-Point Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First projected-arc minimizer for a bound- or convex-constrained quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a closed convex set \(C\), a feasible point \(x\in C\), and \(q(z)=\tfrac12z^THz+c^Tz\) with symmetric \(H\), set \(g=Hx+c\) and define the projected arc \(z(t)=P_C(x-tg)\) for \(t\geq0\). A projected Cauchy point is any
\[x_C=z(t_C),\qquad t_C\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\leq t\leq\bar t}q(z(t)),\]
where \(\bar t>0\) is a prescribed search horizon; a classical breakpoint variant selects the first local minimizer encountered along the piecewise-affine arc. Output \(x_C\), or stop at \(x\) when \(g=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected Cauchy point minimizes the quadratic model along the feasible arc obtained by projecting points on the negative-gradient ray.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex
\(x\in C\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_C=P_C(x-t_Cg)\) minimizes the model over the prescribed projected arc.
review_flags: Projected Cauchy-point conventions vary, and no directly supporting locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate content kind, but the record blends a general closed-convex projected arc with a piecewise-affine breakpoint variant that applies only under additional polyhedral structure. A source is needed to fix the intended Cauchy-point convention and hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Free-Variable Subspace Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic correction restricted to variables not fixed by the current active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx\) and a feasible iterate \(x\), choose a free index set \(F\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and hold \(x_{F^c}\) fixed. Compute
\[p_F\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u}\left\{g_F^Tu+\tfrac12u^TH_{FF}u:\ A_Fu=0\right\},\qquad p_{F^c}=0,\]
where \(g=Hx+c\) and \(A_Fu=0\) represents equality or currently active linear constraints retained during the correction. Select the largest admissible \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), optionally shortened by a descent line search, and output \(x^+=x+\alpha p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After identifying fixed variables, minimize the quadratic over the remaining feasible subspace, then truncate or line-search the correction to retain feasibility and descent.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is feasible
The reduced subproblem has a minimizer
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^+=x+\alpha p\) is obtained from a reduced quadratic minimization with \(p_{F^c}=0\).

notation.meaning: principal Hessian block on free indices
active-constraint matrix restricted to free indices

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Step Projected Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-step projected gradient for a convex quadratic over a convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx\), where \(H\succeq0\), and let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Choose \(x_0\in C\) and a constant \(\alpha\in(0,2/\lambda_{\max}(H))\) when \(H\neq0\). Iterate
\[x_{k+1}=P_C\bigl(x_k-\alpha(Hx_k+c)\bigr).\]
Stop when \(\|x_k-P_C(x_k-\alpha(Hx_k+c))\|/\alpha\leq\varepsilon\), and output \(x_k\). If the solution set is nonempty, the iterates converge to a minimizer of \(q\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly take a constant negative-gradient step and project onto the feasible set; a step below twice the reciprocal Lipschitz constant ensures convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex
\(H\succeq0\) and the constrained minimizer set is nonempty
\(0<\alpha<2/\lambda_{\max}(H)\) when \(H\neq0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha(Hx_k+c))\) converges to a constrained minimizer.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the fixed-step convergence range.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits fixed-step projected gradient and states the convex quadratic setting clearly, but the convergence claim and step interval require a direct authoritative citation.

children.title: Line-Search Projected Gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Projected Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone Armijo backtracking applied to a projected-gradient direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given differentiable \(f\), a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), and \(x_k\in C\), choose \(\gamma_k\in[\gamma_{\min},\gamma_{\max}]\) and form \(y_k=P_C(x_k-\gamma_k\nabla f(x_k))\), \(d_k=y_k-x_k\). Starting with \(t=1\), replace \(t\leftarrow\beta t\) until
\[f(x_k+td_k)\leq f(x_k)+\sigma t\nabla f(x_k)^Td_k,\]
where \(\beta,\sigma\in(0,1)\). Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+td_k\). Stop and output \(x_k\) when \(\|d_k\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project a trial gradient step, then backtrack along the feasible segment to that projection until monotone Armijo decrease is achieved.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex
\(f\) is continuously differentiable
\(0<\gamma_{\min}\leq\gamma_k\leq\gamma_{\max}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted feasible iterate satisfies the monotone Armijo inequality.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this line-search projected-gradient formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm correctly targets line-search projected gradient and distinguishes segment search from projected-arc search, but no citation supports the formulation or acceptance rule.

children.title: Nonmonotone Projected Gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Projected Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected gradient allowing bounded temporary objective increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\in C\), choose \(\gamma_k>0\), set \(y_k=P_C(x_k-\gamma_k\nabla f(x_k))\), and let \(d_k=y_k-x_k\). For a memory length \(M\geq1\), define \(F_k=\max\{f(x_j):\max(0,k-M+1)\leq j\leq k\}\). Backtrack \(t\leftarrow\beta t\) from \(t=1\) until
\[f(x_k+td_k)\leq F_k+\sigma t\nabla f(x_k)^Td_k.\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+td_k\), and stop when \(\|d_k\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected-gradient step is accepted relative to the largest recent objective value, permitting temporary increases while retaining a finite-memory decrease condition.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex
\(f\) is continuously differentiable
\(M\geq1\) and \(\beta,\sigma\in(0,1)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted iterate satisfies a finite-memory nonmonotone Armijo condition.

notation.meaning: maximum objective value in the current memory window

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-memory nonmonotone algorithm fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but the reference-value rule and projected Armijo test lack a supporting citation.

when \(s_k^Ty_k>0\), and otherwise use a safeguarded fallback. Stop when \(\|d_k\|\leq\varepsilon\).

abla f(x_k)-

children.title: Safeguarded Spectral Steps
children.top_down_role: Bounds, resets, and acceptance controls used around spectral step estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguarded Spectral Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounding and fallback conditions for spectral projected-gradient steplengths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix constants \(0<\alpha_{\min}\leq\alpha_{\max}<\infty\) and a fallback \(\alpha_{\mathrm{fb}}\in[\alpha_{\min},\alpha_{\max}]\). From a raw spectral quotient \(\widehat\alpha_k\), define \[\alpha_k=\begin{cases}\min\{\alpha_{\max},\max\{\alpha_{\min},\widehat\alpha_k\}\},&\widehat\alpha_k\text{ is finite and positive},\\ \alpha_{\mathrm{fb}},&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] Thus every accepted steplength satisfies \(\alpha_{\min}\leq\alpha_k\leq\alpha_{\max}\), including iterations with zero, nonpositive, or numerically unusable curvature denominators. The projected update \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_k\nabla f(x_k))\) is consequently well-defined whenever the projection is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip every valid spectral step to fixed positive bounds and replace invalid curvature quotients by a prescribed bounded fallback.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(0<\alpha_{\min}\leq\alpha_{\max}<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k\in[\alpha_{\min},\alpha_{\max}]\) and \(x_{k+1}\in C\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded clipping and fallback condition is internally correct and fits the leaf, but the particular safeguard convention lacks a cited source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Projected Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected-gradient QP iteration in a uniformly positive-definite changing metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\in C\). At iteration \(k\), select a symmetric positive-definite metric \(H_k\) and steplength \(\alpha_k>0\), and compute \[x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in C}\left\{\nabla f(x_k)^{\mathsf T}(z-x_k)+\frac{1}{2\alpha_k}(z-x_k)^{\mathsf T}H_k(z-x_k)\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(x_{k+1}=P_C^{H_k}(x_k-\alpha_kH_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k))\). Require uniform metric bounds \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\) for constants \(0<m\leq M<\infty\). Stop when \(\|H_k(x_k-x_{k+1})/\alpha_k\|\) meets the chosen tolerance; otherwise return the last feasible iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, take and project a gradient step in a uniformly bounded positive-definite metric.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(Q\succeq0\).
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\) and \(\alpha_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The subproblem has a unique solution \(x_{k+1}\in C\).

notation.meaning: projection onto the feasible set in the metric induced by the metric matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The metric projection subproblem, equivalent projection formula, and uniqueness claim are correct under the stated assumptions, but the algorithm and residual convention have no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Nesterov-Type Projected Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accelerated projected-gradient scheme for a smooth convex QP over a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in C\), set \(x_{-1}=x_0\) and \(t_0=1\), and choose \(0<\alpha\leq1/L\). For \(k\geq0\), compute \[t_{k+1}=\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2}}{2},\qquad y_k=x_k+\frac{t_k-1}{t_{k+1}}(x_k-x_{k-1}),\qquad x_{k+1}=P_C(y_k-\alpha\nabla f(y_k)).\] Stop when a prescribed projected-gradient residual or iteration limit is reached, and output the latest feasible point \(x_{k+1}\). For this convex smooth problem, the standard estimate-sequence guarantee gives objective residual of order \(O(k^{-2})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extrapolate consecutive feasible iterates, take a gradient step at the extrapolated point, and project to obtain accelerated objective convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) is convex and has \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
A minimizer \(x^\star\in C\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\in C\) for all \(k\), and \(f(x_k)-f(x^\star)=O(k^{-2})\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated projected FISTA/Nesterov iteration and O(k^{-2}) objective-rate role fit the leaf, but the precise indexing and rate claim require an authoritative source and locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Restarted Accelerated Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-value restart of accelerated projected gradient for convex QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run the accelerated projected iteration with state \((x_{k-1},x_k,t_k)\). Form its extrapolated point and projected trial \(z_{k+1}=P_C(y_k-\alpha\nabla f(y_k))\). If \(f(z_{k+1})\leq f(x_k)\), accept \(x_{k+1}=z_{k+1}\) and retain the accelerated parameter update. Otherwise restart by setting \(t_k=1\), \(y_k=x_k\), and recomputing \[x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha\nabla f(x_k)).\] Continue until the projected-gradient residual meets tolerance, then output \(x_{k+1}\). This convention prevents acceptance of an objective-increasing inertial trial while preserving feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept an accelerated projected trial only when it does not increase the objective; otherwise reset momentum and take an ordinary projected step.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(0<\alpha\leq1/L\).
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted iterate lies in \(C\) and satisfies \(f(x_{k+1})\leq f(x_k)\).

notation.meaning: acceleration parameter reset to one on restart
Euclidean projection onto the feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The function-value restart rule is coherent and ensures the stated monotonicity with the fallback step, but restart conventions vary and this version has no cited support.

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguarded Inertial Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracked inertial projection with a sufficient-decrease acceptance safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_{k-1},x_k\in C\), choose an initial \(\beta_k\in[0,\bar\beta]\), form \(y_k=x_k+\beta_k(x_k-x_{k-1})\), and compute \(z_k=P_C(y_k-\alpha\nabla f(y_k))\). Accept \(x_{k+1}=z_k\) only if \[f(z_k)\leq f(x_k)-\sigma\|z_k-x_k\|^2.\] If the test fails, reduce \(\beta_k\) and retry; the terminal fallback \(\beta_k=0\) uses the ordinary projected-gradient step. Stop when the projected-gradient residual is below tolerance and output the accepted feasible iterate. Choose \(\sigma\) no larger than the descent constant of the fallback step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack the momentum coefficient until the projected inertial trial gives sufficient decrease, with ordinary projected gradient as the fallback.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(0<\alpha<2/L\).
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(0\leq\beta_k\leq\bar\beta\) and \(\sigma\geq0\) permits acceptance of the fallback.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted iterate satisfies \(x_{k+1}\in C\) and \(f(x_{k+1})\leq f(x_k)-\sigma\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The safeguarded inertial algorithm is plausible, but the sufficient-decrease test, momentum backtracking, and fallback-acceptance condition require a source establishing the exact convention and descent constant.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Gradient Mapping Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projected-gradient mapping and its exact first-order optimality interpretation.

For \(\alpha>0\), define the projected-gradient mapping of differentiable \(f\) on \(C\) by \[G_\alpha(x)= rac{1}{\alpha} igl(x-P_C(x-\alpha
abla f(x)) igr),\qquad x\in C.\] The projection variational inequality implies \(G_\alpha(x)=0\) if and only if \(x=P_C(x-\alpha
abla f(x))\), which is equivalent to \[0\in
abla f(x)+N_C(x).\] Hence a zero mapping is precisely a first-order stationary point; when \(f\) and \(C\) are convex, it is precisely a global minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected-gradient mapping is the scaled displacement to a projected gradient step; its zeros are exactly constrained stationary points and, convexly, minimizers.

\(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Face Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification of the optimal polyhedral face under strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be polyhedral, let \(x^\star\) minimize a convex differentiable \(f\) over \(C\), and let \(F^\star\) be the minimal face of \(C\) containing \(x^\star\). Suppose \(-\nabla f(x^\star)\in\operatorname{ri}N_C(x^\star)\). If \(x_k\to x^\star\) and \[x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha_k\nabla f(x_k)),\qquad 0<\underline\alpha\leq\alpha_k\leq\overline\alpha<\infty,\] then there exists \(K\) such that \(x_k\in\operatorname{ri}F^\star\) for every \(k\geq K\). Thus the active constraints defining the optimal face are identified after finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedral feasible set, convergence plus strict complementarity makes projected gradient identify the optimal face after finitely many iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is polyhedral and \(f\) is convex and continuously differentiable near \(x^\star\).
\(-\nabla f(x^\star)\in\operatorname{ri}N_C(x^\star)\).
\(x_k\to x^\star\) with steplengths uniformly bounded above and away from zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\geq K:\ x_k\in\operatorname{ri}F^\star\).

notation.meaning: minimal feasible face containing the solution
normal cone of the feasible set at the solution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is appropriately a theorem, but finite identification of the relative interior of the minimal face under the stated varying-step assumptions is nontrivial and needs an authoritative theorem-level citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Transition to Reduced-Space Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced quadratic model after a polyhedral face has been identified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the identified face have affine hull \(\operatorname{aff}F=x_F+\operatorname{range}Z\), where the columns of \(Z\) are orthonormal. Writing \(x=x_F+Zp\) transforms the QP objective into \[\phi(p)=\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ)p+\bigl(Z^{\mathsf T}(Qx_F+c)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}p+f(x_F).\] Therefore minimizing \(f\) over \(F\) is equivalent to minimizing \(\phi(p)\) subject to \(x_F+Zp\in F\). Locally around a point in \(\operatorname{ri}F\), those face inequalities are inactive relative to the affine hull, so the local step is an unconstrained reduced-space quadratic minimization with Hessian \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameterizing an identified face by a null-space basis converts the original QP into a smaller quadratic problem on that face.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(Q\succeq0\).
\(F\) is an identified face and \(\operatorname{aff}F=x_F+\operatorname{range}Z\).
\(Z^{\mathsf T}Z=I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in F}f(x)=\min_{p:\,x_F+Zp\in F}\phi(p)\), with reduced Hessian \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\).

notation.meaning: reference point on the identified face
orthonormal basis for directions parallel to the face

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced quadratic expansion and equivalence are algebraically correct and the representation kind fits the leaf, but the claimed transition to local unconstrained face minimization lacks a cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Identification under Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict complementarity failure can prevent finite identification even for a one-dimensional strongly convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(C=[0,\infty)\) and \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\). The unique solution is \(x^\star=0\), but \(-\nabla f(x^\star)=0\) lies on the boundary, not the relative interior, of \(N_C(0)=(-\infty,0]\). For any \(x_0>0\) and fixed \(0<\alpha<1\), projected gradient gives \[x_{k+1}=P_C((1-\alpha)x_k)=(1-\alpha)x_k>0\] at every finite \(k\), although \(x_k\to0\). Hence the optimal active face \(\{0\}\) is never finitely identified. Degeneracy therefore invalidates finite-identification conclusions without additional assumptions or identification tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate boundary solution may be approached forever from the interior, so the correct active face need not be identified finitely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k=(1-\alpha)^kx_0>0\) for every finite \(k\), while \(x_k\to x^\star=0\).

notation.meaning: normal cone at the optimal boundary point
Euclidean projection onto the nonnegative half-line

knowledge_statements.title: General Convex QP Rate Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global sublinear objective bound for fixed-step projected gradient on a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha\nabla f(x_k))\) with \(0<\alpha\leq1/L\), and let \(x^\star\) be any minimizer. Then for every integer \(k\geq1\), \[f(x_k)-f(x^\star)\leq\frac{\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{2\alpha k}.\] Consequently, projected gradient requires at most \(\left\lceil\|x_0-x^\star\|^2/(2\alpha\varepsilon)\right\rceil\) iterations, each using one gradient evaluation and one Euclidean projection, to obtain objective residual at most \(\varepsilon>0\). This bound does not require positive definiteness of the QP Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex QP, fixed-step projected gradient achieves objective error of order one over the iteration count.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(Q\succeq0\) and \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
A minimizer \(x^\star\in C\) exists and \(0<\alpha\leq1/L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_k)-f(x^\star)\leq\|x_0-x^\star\|^2/(2\alpha k)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Linear-Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global distance contraction for projected gradient with a positive-definite quadratic Hessian, including the equal-eigenvalue one-step case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\mu I\preceq Q\preceq LI\) with \(0<\mu\leq L\), and choose \(\alpha=2/(L+\mu)\). For the iteration \(x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-\alpha(Qx_k+c))\) and the unique constrained minimizer \(x^\star\), nonexpansiveness of projection yields \[\|x_{k+1}-x^\star\|\leq\rho\|x_k-x^\star\|,\qquad \rho=\frac{L-\mu}{L+\mu}\in[0,1).\] Hence \(\|x_k-x^\star\|\leq\rho^k\|x_0-x^\star\|\). If \(L>\mu\), a sufficient condition for \(\|x_k-x^\star\|\leq\varepsilon\), where \(0<\varepsilon<\|x_0-x^\star\|\), is \[k\geq\left\lceil\frac{\log(\|x_0-x^\star\|/\varepsilon)}{\log(1/\rho)}\right\rceil.\] If \(L=\mu\), then \(\rho=0\) and \(x_1=x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive definiteness makes projected gradient globally contractive. When the eigenvalue bounds differ, convergence is geometric; when they coincide, the selected step reaches the constrained minimizer in one iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(\mu I\preceq Q\preceq LI\) and \(\mu>0\).
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_k-x^\star\|\leq((L-\mu)/(L+\mu))^k\|x_0-x^\star\|\), with \(x_1=x^\star\) when \(L=\mu\).

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Error-Bound Linear Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear convergence of projected gradient under a polyhedral error bound on the initial sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) with \(Q\succeq0\), and define \(T_\alpha(x)=P_C(x-\alpha\nabla f(x))\), where \(0<\alpha<2/\|Q\|_2\). Suppose \(X^*=\arg\min_{x\in C}f(x)\neq\varnothing\) and, on the initial sublevel set, \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\leq\kappa\|x-T_\alpha(x)\|\). Then the iteration \(x^{k+1}=T_\alpha(x^k)\) admits constants \(M<\infty\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x^k,X^*)\leq M\rho^k\) and \(f(x^k)-f^*\leq M\rho^{2k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected-gradient residual error bound converts the usual descent estimate into geometric convergence of solution distance and quadratic objective error.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty polyhedron and \(Q\succeq0\).
\(X^*\neq\varnothing\) and the displayed residual error bound holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x^k,X^*)\leq M\rho^k\) and \(f(x^k)-f^*\leq M\rho^{2k}\) for some \(M<\infty\), \(\rho\in(0,1)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Identified-Face Local Rate Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local rate after finite identification of an optimal polyhedral face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be polyhedral and let \(x^*\) solve \(\min_{x\in C}\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), where \(Q\succeq0\). Let \(F\) be a face containing \(x^*\), with tangent space \(T=\operatorname{span}(F-F)\). Assume projected-gradient iterates identify \(F\): there is \(K\) such that \(x^k\in F\) for every \(k\geq K\). If \(d^\top Qd\geq\mu\|d\|^2\) for all \(d\in T\) and some \(\mu>0\), then for every admissible fixed stepsize there exist \(M<\infty\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that \(\|x^k-x^*\|\leq M\rho^{k-K}\) for \(k\geq K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once the optimal face is identified, positive curvature on its tangent space yields local geometric convergence even if the full Hessian is singular.
assumptions_latex: The projected-gradient iterates identify the face \(F\) after finitely many iterations.
\(Q\) is uniformly positive on \(T=\operatorname{span}(F-F)\).
The fixed stepsize lies in the stable interval for the restriction to \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x^k-x^*\|\leq M\rho^{k-K}\) for all \(k\geq K\), with \(M<\infty\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\).

notation.meaning: Tangent space parallel to the face.

children.title: Semidefinite Curvature Regime
children.top_down_role: Projected-gradient behavior when the QP Hessian is positive semidefinite without global positive definiteness.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Curvature Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature classification for a convex quadratic program with a positive-semidefinite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), where \(Q\succeq0\). Then \(f\) is convex, and its quadratic curvature along a nonzero feasible chord \(d=y-x\), with \(x,y\in C\), is \(d^\top Qd\). If \(D=(C-C)\setminus\{0\}\neq\varnothing\), a positive uniform curvature modulus on feasible chords exists exactly when \(\inf_{d\in D}d^\top Qd/\|d\|^2>0\). When this infimum is zero, there is a sequence of nonzero feasible chords whose curvature ratios converge to zero, so positive-semidefinite curvature does not provide a positive uniform feasible curvature modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite Hessian makes the QP convex, while the infimum of the curvature ratio over nonzero feasible chords determines whether feasible curvature is uniformly positive or can approach zero.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex.
\(Q\succeq0\).
\(D=(C-C)\setminus\{0\}\neq\varnothing\) when the curvature infimum is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive feasible curvature modulus exists if and only if \(\inf_{d\in D}d^\top Qd/\|d\|^2>0\); if the infimum is zero, feasible-chord curvature ratios approach zero along a sequence.

notation.meaning: Set of nonzero feasible chord directions.
A positive uniform feasible curvature modulus.

children.title: Flat Feasible Directions
children.top_down_role: Feasible directions carrying zero quadratic curvature and their effect on solution geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Flat Feasible Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible directions carrying zero quadratic curvature at a point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(x\in C\), and let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) with \(Q\succeq0\). A nonzero vector \(d\) is a flat feasible direction at \(x\) if \(x+td\in C\) for every sufficiently small \(t\geq0\) and \(d^\top Qd=0\). Because \(Q\succeq0\), the curvature condition is equivalent to \(Qd=0\), and along the feasible ray \(f(x+td)=f(x)+t\nabla f(x)^\top d\). It is objective-flat when additionally \(\nabla f(x)^\top d=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat feasible direction lies in the Hessian nullspace and follows a feasible ray; the objective is affine, and possibly constant, along it.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\).
\(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\neq0\), \(x+td\in C\) locally, and \(Qd=0\); objective-flatness additionally requires \(\nabla f(x)^\top d=0\).

children.title: Loss of Strong-Curvature Rates
children.top_down_role: Boundary separating strong-curvature rate guarantees from semidefinite behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Strong-Curvature Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of contraction toward a distinguished optimizer when nullspace curvature is allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x_1,x_2)=\tfrac12x_1^2\) on \(C=\mathbb R^2\), whose Hessian is \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\). For projected gradient with \(0<\alpha<2\), \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha\nabla f(x^k)\) gives \(x_1^{k+1}=(1-\alpha)x_1^k\) and \(x_2^{k+1}=x_2^k\). Thus the objective and distance to the solution set \(X^*=\{(0,t):t\in\mathbb R\}\) decrease geometrically, but convergence to the distinguished optimizer \((0,0)\) fails whenever \(x_2^0\neq0\). Hence positive-semidefinite curvature alone cannot imply a contraction in full-space distance to an arbitrary optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nullspace component remains unchanged under gradient steps, so semidefinite curvature cannot guarantee geometric convergence to a selected optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x_1,x_2)=\tfrac12x_1^2\) and \(C=\mathbb R^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(x_2^0\neq0\), then \(x^k\not\to(0,0)\), despite geometric decay of \(f(x^k)-f^*\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: directly checkable two-dimensional quadratic counterexample

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Coordinate Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cyclic coordinate minimization for a box-constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), where \(Q\succeq0\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(C=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\) be a nonempty box. Initialize \(x^0\in C\) and select coordinates \(i_k\) cyclically. At iteration \(k\), set \(g_{i_k}=(Qx^k+c)_{i_k}\). If \(Q_{i_k i_k}>0\), set \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}=P_{[\ell_{i_k},u_{i_k}]}(x_{i_k}^k-g_{i_k}/Q_{i_k i_k})\). If \(Q_{i_k i_k}=0\), choose \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}\) from the minimizers of the resulting affine coordinate restriction over \([\ell_{i_k},u_{i_k}]\). Set \(x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\) for every \(j\neq i_k\). Stop when all bound-constrained coordinate optimality residuals are within tolerance, and output the final feasible iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cyclic primal coordinate descent exactly minimizes the convex quadratic over one box-constrained coordinate at a time and leaves all other coordinates unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(C=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\neq\varnothing\).
\(x^0\in C\), and the coordinate schedule is cyclic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update satisfies \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{t\in[\ell_{i_k},u_{i_k}]}f(x^k+(t-x_{i_k}^k)e_{i_k})\) and preserves feasibility.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the coordinate interval.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Coordinate Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or proximal block updates for a product-constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), where \(Q\succeq0\), partition the coordinates into blocks \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\), and let \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\), where every \(C_j\) is nonempty, closed, and convex. Initialize \(x^0\in C\). At iteration \(k\), select \(B=B_{j_k}\) and perform either an attained exact update \(x_B^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{z\in C_B}f(z,x_{-B}^k)\), or the proximal update \(x_B^{k+1}=P_{C_B}^{H_B}(x_B^k-H_B^{-1}\nabla_Bf(x^k))\), where \(H_B\succ0\) and \(H_B\succeq Q_{BB}\). Set \(x_{-B}^{k+1}=x_{-B}^k\). Select blocks essentially cyclically and stop when the assembled block projected-gradient residual is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block coordinate method updates a selected group of variables by attained exact minimization or by a curvature-majorized metric projection while preserving product-set feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\).
\(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\), with every \(C_j\) nonempty, closed, and convex.
Every block is selected essentially cyclically.
For a proximal update, \(H_B\succ0\) and \(H_B\succeq Q_{BB}\); for an exact update, the block minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update is feasible and satisfies \(f(x^{k+1})\leq f(x^k)\).

notation.meaning: Projection onto the selected block set in the metric induced by H_B.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Coordinate Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random exact coordinate minimization with full-support independent sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), where \(Q\succeq0\), and let \(C=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\neq\varnothing\), with finite bounds \(\ell_i\leq u_i\). Initialize \(x^0\in C\), choose probabilities \(p_i>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\), and sample the indices \(i_k\) independently with \(\mathbb P(i_k=i)=p_i\). Replace coordinate \(i_k\) by an exact minimizer of \(t\mapsto f(x^k+(t-x_{i_k}^k)e_{i_k})\) over \([\ell_{i_k},u_{i_k}]\), leaving every other coordinate unchanged. Stop after a prescribed sampling budget or when an estimated projected-coordinate residual is below tolerance. If the sampling process is instead continued indefinitely, every coordinate is sampled infinitely often almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized coordinate descent independently samples every coordinate with positive probability and exactly minimizes the QP along the sampled box-constrained coordinate; under an infinite run, every coordinate is sampled infinitely often almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\).
\(C=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\neq\varnothing\), with finite interval bounds.
The sampled indices are independent and identically distributed with probabilities \(p_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every update is feasible and satisfies \(f(x^{k+1})\leq f(x^k)\) almost surely; if sampling continues indefinitely, every coordinate is sampled infinitely often almost surely.

notation.meaning: Random coordinate sampled at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Frank-Wolfe QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-free conditional-gradient iteration for a convex QP over a compact polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonempty compact polytope \(C\), \(Q\succeq0\), and \(x^0\in C\), compute \(g^k=Qx^k+c\) and a linear-minimization atom \(s^k\in\arg\min_{s\in C}\langle g^k,s\rangle\). Define \(d^k=s^k-x^k\) and the gap \(G_k=\langle g^k,x^k-s^k\rangle\). If \(G_k\leq\varepsilon\), stop and output \(x^k\). Otherwise choose \(\gamma_k\in\arg\min_{0\leq\gamma\leq1}f(x^k+\gamma d^k)\), available by clipped one-dimensional quadratic minimization, and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\gamma_kd^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Frank–Wolfe repeatedly solves a linear problem over the polytope, moves toward its minimizing atom, and stops using the conditional-gradient gap.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty compact polytope.
\(Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is feasible, and termination with \(G_k\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(f(x^k)-f^*\leq\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Conditional Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set mass transfer from an away atom to a linear-minimization atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a compact polytope and let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), where \(Q\succeq0\). Maintain \(x^k=\sum_{a\in A_k}\lambda_a^ka\), with \(\lambda_a^k>0\) and \(\sum_{a\in A_k}\lambda_a^k=1\). Compute \(s^k\in\arg\min_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x^k),s\rangle\) and \(v^k\in\arg\max_{v\in A_k}\langle\nabla f(x^k),v\rangle\). Use \(d^k=s^k-v^k\) and choose \(\gamma_k\in\arg\min_{0\leq\gamma\leq\lambda_{v^k}^k}f(x^k+\gamma d^k)\). Set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\gamma_kd^k\), increase the coefficient of \(s^k\) by \(\gamma_k\), decrease the coefficient of \(v^k\) by \(\gamma_k\), combine these changes if the atoms coincide, and remove zero coefficients. Stop when the Frank–Wolfe gap is within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise conditional gradient preserves a convex active-set representation by transferring weight from the worst active atom to a linear-minimization atom.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a compact polytope and \(Q\succeq0\).
Each iterate has a maintained positive convex decomposition over \(A_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update satisfies \(x^{k+1}\in C\); if \(s^k\neq v^k\) and \(\gamma_k=\lambda_{v^k}^k\), the updated coefficient of \(v^k\) is zero.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Drop Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Step-size conditions under which away or pairwise updates delete an active atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=\sum_{a\in A}\lambda_aa\) with positive coefficients. For an away direction \(d=x-v\) with \(0<\lambda_v<1\), feasibility requires \(0\leq\gamma\leq\lambda_v/(1-\lambda_v)\); choosing the upper endpoint makes the updated coefficient of \(v\) equal to zero. For a pairwise direction \(d=s-v\), feasibility requires \(0\leq\gamma\leq\lambda_v\), and choosing \(\gamma=\lambda_v\) likewise deletes \(v\). Such maximal steps are drop steps. They reduce active-set cardinality unless the toward atom \(s\) is newly introduced during the same pairwise update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An away or pairwise step drops an atom exactly when it exhausts that atom’s maximal transferable convex weight.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is represented by a positive convex combination of active atoms.
The chosen step reaches the corresponding maximal feasible endpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated coefficient of \(v\) is zero, so \(v\) can be removed from the active representation.

notation.meaning: Current coefficient of the atom being removed.

knowledge_statements.title: Fully Corrective Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fully corrective conditional gradient for a convex quadratic over a compact atom hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\top}Qx+c^{\top}x\), where \(Q\succeq0\), and let \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\) be compact. Initialize \(x^0\in C\) with a finite active set \(S_0\subset\mathcal A\) satisfying \(x^0\in\operatorname{conv}(S_0)\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(s_k\in\arg\min_{s\in\mathcal A}\langle Qx^k+c,s\rangle\), set \(S_{k+1}=S_k\cup\{s_k\}\), and compute \[x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in\operatorname{conv}(S_{k+1})}f(x).\] Zero-weight atoms may be deleted. Stop when \(\langle Qx^k+c,x^k-s_k\rangle\leq\varepsilon\), and output \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a linear-oracle atom, then reoptimize the quadratic over the convex hull of every active atom; terminate when the conditional-gradient gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\).
\(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) minimizes \(f\) over the enlarged active hull, and the stated stopping test gives an \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate.

notation.meaning: finite active atom set at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Gradient Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal suboptimality certificate for differentiable convex QPs on compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\top}Qx+c^{\top}x\) with \(Q\succeq0\). For \(x\in C\), define \[g_{\mathrm{FW}}(x)=\max_{s\in C}\langle\nabla f(x),x-s\rangle=\langle Qx+c,x-s_x\rangle,\] where \(s_x\in\arg\min_{s\in C}\langle Qx+c,s\rangle\). Then \(g_{\mathrm{FW}}(x)\geq0\), and for every minimizer \(x^\star\in\arg\min_C f\), \[0\leq f(x)-f(x^\star)\leq g_{\mathrm{FW}}(x).\] Thus \(g_{\mathrm{FW}}(x)\leq\varepsilon\) is a directly verifiable certificate of \(\varepsilon\)-optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Frank–Wolfe linearization gap is nonnegative and upper-bounds primal suboptimality, so a gap at most epsilon certifies epsilon-optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\).
\(C\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-\min_{z\in C}f(z)\leq g_{\mathrm{FW}}(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient ascent on the smooth equality-constrained convex-QP dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^{\top}Qx+c^{\top}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), with \(Q\succ0\). Define \(x(y)=-Q^{-1}(c+A^{\top}y)\) and the concave dual function \(d(y)=-\tfrac12(c+A^{\top}y)^{\top}Q^{-1}(c+A^{\top}y)-b^{\top}y\). Initialize \(y^0\in\mathbb R^m\) and iterate \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_k\nabla d(y^k)=y^k+\alpha_k(Ax(y^k)-b).\] For the fixed-step form, choose \(0<\alpha_k=\alpha<2/L\), where \(L=\lambda_{\max}(AQ^{-1}A^{\top})\). Stop using a prescribed dual-gradient or primal-residual tolerance and output \(y^k\) with \(x(y^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply gradient ascent to the smooth quadratic dual; its gradient is the primal equality residual and admits a spectral fixed-step bound.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succ0\).
The equality-constrained QP is feasible.
\(0<\alpha<2/\lambda_{\max}(AQ^{-1}A^{\top})\) for the fixed-step iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha(Ax(y^k)-b)\) is gradient ascent on \(d\).
