knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Dual Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nesterov acceleration applied to the smooth concave dual of an equality-constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the dual-QP definitions \(x(y)=-Q^{-1}(c+A^{\top}y)\), \(d(y)=-\tfrac12(c+A^{\top}y)^{\top}Q^{-1}(c+A^{\top}y)-b^{\top}y\), and \(L=\lambda_{\max}(AQ^{-1}A^{\top})>0\), initialize \(y^0=z^0\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(t_0=1\). For \(k\geq0\), compute \[y^{k+1}=z^k+L^{-1}(Ax(z^k)-b),\qquad t_{k+1}=\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2}}2,\] \[z^{k+1}=y^{k+1}+\frac{t_k-1}{t_{k+1}}(y^{k+1}-y^k).\] Stop at a prescribed dual-gradient, residual, or iteration tolerance and return \(y^{k+1}\) with \(x(y^{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a Lipschitz-scaled dual-gradient step followed by Nesterov extrapolation, while recovering primal iterates from the current multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succ0\) and the equality-constrained QP is feasible.
\(L=\lambda_{\max}(AQ^{-1}A^{\top})>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recurrence is accelerated gradient ascent on the concave quadratic dual \(d\).

children.title: Dual Coordinate QP Methods
children.top_down_role: Dual first-order methods organized around coordinate or coordinate-block selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Coordinate QP Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cyclic or selected-coordinate ascent for an unconstrained concave quadratic dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-constrained QP with \(Q\succ0\), set \(H=AQ^{-1}A^{\top}\), \(x(y)=-Q^{-1}(c+A^{\top}y)\), and \(r(y)=Ax(y)-b=\nabla d(y)\). Initialize \(y^0\in\mathbb R^m\). At iteration \(k\), select an index \(i_k\) satisfying \(H_{i_ki_k}>0\), and update only that coordinate by \[y_{i_k}^{k+1}=y_{i_k}^k+\frac{r_{i_k}(y^k)}{H_{i_ki_k}},\qquad y_j^{k+1}=y_j^k\quad(j\neq i_k).\] This is the exact maximizer of \(d\) along coordinate \(i_k\). Stop when a chosen norm of \(r(y^k)\) is below tolerance, and output \(y^k\) and \(x(y^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select one dual coordinate and maximize the concave quadratic exactly along it; the update divides its current constraint residual by coordinate curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succ0\).
Each selected coordinate satisfies \(H_{ii}>0\).
The coordinate-selection rule visits every relevant coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_{i}^{k+1}=y_i^k+r_i(y^k)/H_{ii}\) exactly maximizes \(d\) with all other coordinates fixed.

notation.meaning: dual gradient and primal equality residual

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, and the sign and curvature normalization in the exact coordinate-ascent update are correct. A source with a specific coordinate-ascent or quadratic-dual locator is required.

children.title: Multiplier QP Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier QP Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact augmented-Lagrangian multiplier iteration for an equality-constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\top}Qx+c^{\top}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), with \(Q\succeq0\), and choose \(\rho>0\). Initialize \(y^0\in\mathbb R^m\). At iteration \(k\), compute \[x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\left\{f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax-b\rVert^2\right\},\] then update \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b).\] Stop when the primal residual and an appropriate stationarity residual satisfy prescribed tolerances, and output \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\). If \(Q+\rho A^{\top}A\succ0\), the primal subproblem has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the quadratic augmented Lagrangian exactly, then update equality multipliers by the scaled primal residual.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) and the equality-constrained QP is feasible.
Each augmented-Lagrangian subproblem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b)\) is the method-of-multipliers update.

notation.meaning: positive penalty and multiplier stepsize parameter

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-to-Multiplier Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-update correspondence between dual coordinate ascent and coordinatewise multiplier steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q\succ0\), let \(H=AQ^{-1}A^{\top}\), \(x(y)=-Q^{-1}(c+A^{\top}y)\), and \(r(y)=Ax(y)-b\). Holding \(y_j\) fixed for \(j\neq i\), the dual coordinate restriction is a concave scalar quadratic with derivative \(r_i(y)\) and curvature \(-H_{ii}\). Hence, when \(H_{ii}>0\), its exact coordinate maximizer satisfies \[y_i^+=y_i+\rho_i r_i(y),\qquad \rho_i=H_{ii}^{-1}.\] Thus exact dual coordinate ascent is precisely a coordinatewise multiplier residual update with the curvature-normalized stepsize \(\rho_i\); conversely, this multiplier update performs exact line maximization of the quadratic dual along coordinate \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact dual coordinate step equals a multiplier residual update whose stepsize is the reciprocal diagonal dual curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succ0\).
The selected row satisfies \(H_{ii}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_i^+=y_i+H_{ii}^{-1}(a_i^{\top}x(y)-b_i)\) is both exact coordinate ascent and a coordinate multiplier update.

notation.meaning: ith equality residual and dual partial derivative

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Point Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent and implicit-inclusion forms of proximal-point iteration for QP optimality operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\tfrac12x^{\top}Qx+c^{\top}x+\delta_C(x)\), where \(Q\succeq0\) and \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex. Its optimality operator is \(T=\partial F=Q(\cdot)+c+N_C\), which is maximal monotone. For \(\lambda_k>0\), the proximal-point update has the equivalent forms \[x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_kF}(x^k)=J_{\lambda_kT}(x^k),\] \[0\in T(x^{k+1})+\lambda_k^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k).\] Therefore the QP proximal step is simultaneously a regularized QP, a resolvent evaluation, and an implicit Euler step for the inclusion \(0\in T(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex-QP proximal step is equivalently a regularized quadratic program, a resolvent evaluation, and an implicit step for the optimality inclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\).
\(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(\lambda_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_kF}(x^k)=J_{\lambda_k\partial F}(x^k)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the relation leaf, and the proximal, resolvent, regularized-QP, and implicit-inclusion forms are consistent under the stated finite-dimensional convex assumptions. No authoritative monotone-operator or proximal-point source locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Method-of-Multipliers Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact method of multipliers as proximal-point ascent on the concave dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d(y)=\inf_x\{f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\}\) be the concave dual function of a feasible convex equality-constrained problem. For \(\rho>0\), suppose \(x^{k+1}\) exactly minimizes \(f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax-b\rangle+\tfrac\rho2\lVert Ax-b\rVert^2\), and set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-b)\). Then \[y^{k+1}\in\arg\max_y\left\{d(y)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\lVert y-y^k\rVert^2\right\}=\operatorname{prox}_{\rho(-d)}(y^k).\] Thus an exact augmented-Lagrangian multiplier step is a proximal-point step for minimizing the convex function \(-d\), equivalently proximal ascent on \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact augmented-Lagrangian multiplier updates coincide with proximal-point iterations on the negative dual objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and the equality-constrained problem admits strong duality.
The augmented-Lagrangian subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\rho(-d)}(y^k)\).

children.title: Douglas-Rachford Relations

knowledge_statements.title: Douglas-Rachford Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Douglas–Rachford splitting represented through resolvents and reflected resolvents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be maximal monotone operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let \(\gamma>0\), and define \(J_{\gamma A}=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}\) and \(R_{\gamma A}=2J_{\gamma A}-I\), with analogous definitions for \(B\). The Douglas–Rachford operator for \(0\in A(x)+B(x)\) is \[T_{\mathrm{DR}}=\tfrac12(I+R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A})=I-J_{\gamma A}+J_{\gamma B}(2J_{\gamma A}-I).\] The iteration is \(z^{k+1}=T_{\mathrm{DR}}z^k\), and its shadow iterate is \(x^k=J_{\gamma A}z^k\). Every fixed point \(z^\star\) yields a solution \(x^\star=J_{\gamma A}z^\star\) of the inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Douglas–Rachford averages the identity with two successive reflected resolvents; resolving a fixed point through the first operator produces a solution.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are maximal monotone.
The inclusion has a solution when solution recovery is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{DR}}=\tfrac12(I+R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A})\), and \(z^\star=T_{\mathrm{DR}}z^\star\) implies \(J_{\gamma A}z^\star\in\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the Douglas-Rachford relation leaf. The averaged reflected-resolvent formula, equivalent resolvent expansion, and fixed-point shadow recovery are coherent, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Peaceman-Rachford Relations
children.top_down_role: Connections between Peaceman-Rachford splitting and related reflected-operator constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Peaceman-Rachford Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Peaceman–Rachford splitting as the unaveraged composition of reflected resolvents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be maximal monotone operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and let \(\gamma>0\). With \(J_{\gamma A}=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}\) and \(R_{\gamma A}=2J_{\gamma A}-I\), the Peaceman–Rachford operator is \[T_{\mathrm{PR}}=R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A}.\] Hence its iteration \(z^{k+1}=T_{\mathrm{PR}}z^k\) uses the same two reflected-resolvent composition as Douglas–Rachford but without averaging with the identity. Moreover, \[T_{\mathrm{DR}}=\tfrac12(I+T_{\mathrm{PR}}).\] If \(z^\star\) is a fixed point of \(T_{\mathrm{PR}}\), then \(x^\star=J_{\gamma A}z^\star\) solves \(0\in A(x^\star)+B(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Peaceman–Rachford applies two reflected resolvents without averaging; Douglas–Rachford is the half-average of this map with the identity.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are maximal monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{PR}}=R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A}\) and \(T_{\mathrm{DR}}=\tfrac12(I+T_{\mathrm{PR}})\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the Peaceman-Rachford relation leaf. The unaveraged reflected-resolvent composition and its relationship to Douglas-Rachford are correctly distinguished, but an authoritative source with a specific locator is missing.

children.title: Relaxation Boundary Between Splittings
children.top_down_role: How relaxation choices distinguish or connect the two reflected splitting families.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Boundary Between Splittings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Averaging parameter separating standard relaxed Douglas–Rachford from unaveraged Peaceman–Rachford.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A}\) for maximal monotone \(A,B\), and define the relaxed fixed-point map \[T_\alpha=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha S.\] Then \(\alpha=\tfrac12\) gives Douglas–Rachford, while \(\alpha=1\) gives Peaceman–Rachford. Because \(S\) is nonexpansive, \(T_\alpha\) is averaged for \(0<\alpha<1\), the regime in which standard averaged-operator fixed-point convergence applies. At the boundary \(\alpha=1\), averagedness is lost in general: for \(A=N_{\{0\}}\) and \(B=0\) on \(\mathbb R\), \(S=-I\), so Peaceman–Rachford alternates \(z^{k+1}=-z^k\) unless \(z^0=0\), whereas every \(0<\alpha<1\) yields \(z^{k+1}=(1-2\alpha)z^k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation below one makes the reflected-resolvent composition averaged; at one, Peaceman–Rachford may cycle, as the explicit reflection example shows.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are maximal monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Standard averagedness holds for \(0<\alpha<1\), but can fail at the Peaceman–Rachford boundary \(\alpha=1\).

notation.meaning: composition of the two reflected resolvents
normal cone to the singleton zero

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role exactly fits the terminal container. The averagedness regime, the Peaceman-Rachford boundary, and the explicit cycling example are internally correct, but the record supplies no authoritative source locator for the relaxation result or boundary phenomenon.

children.title: Monotone-Operator Splitting Foundations
children.top_down_role: Operator-level structure supporting the splitting families used for convex QP.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone-Operator Splitting Foundations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality-inclusion representation for finite-dimensional convex quadratic composites.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(h_1,h_2:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, convex functions whose sum represents a convex QP, with a relative-interior qualification ensuring the subdifferential sum rule. Define \(A=\partial h_1\) and \(B=\partial h_2\). Then \(A\) and \(B\) are maximally monotone, and
\[x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}\{h_1(x)+h_2(x)\}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in(A+B)(x^\star).\]
For \(\gamma>0\), their resolvents satisfy \(J_{\gamma A}=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h_1}\) and \(J_{\gamma B}=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h_2}\), furnishing directly computable building blocks for proximal and Douglas–Rachford QP methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex QP can be written as a zero of a sum of maximal monotone subdifferentials, whose resolvents are proximal maps.
assumptions_latex: \(h_1\) and \(h_2\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h_1)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h_2)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}(h_1+h_2)=\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\), with \(J_{\gamma A}=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h_1}\) and \(J_{\gamma B}=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h_2}\).

notation.meaning: Set of points x satisfying zero in A(x).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically standard and fits the foundations leaf, but no cited source with an inspectable locator supports the maximal-monotonicity, sum-rule, and resolvent claims.

children.title: Fixed-Point Interpretation of Splittings
children.top_down_role: Fixed-point viewpoints that organize common QP splitting constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Interpretation of Splittings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Douglas–Rachford fixed points and their QP solution shadows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A,B:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone, let \(\gamma>0\), and set \(R_{\gamma A}=2J_{\gamma A}-I\) and \(T=\tfrac12(I+R_{\gamma B}R_{\gamma A})\). For any \(z\in H\), put \(x=J_{\gamma A}z\). Then
\[z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=J_{\gamma B}(2x-z),\]
and either condition implies \(0\in(A+B)(x)\). Conversely, if \(0\in(A+B)(x)\) and \(a\in A(x)\), \(-a\in B(x)\), then \(z=x+\gamma a\) belongs to \(\operatorname{Fix}T\). Thus the QP solution is the resolvent shadow of a splitting fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Douglas–Rachford fixed points encode QP solutions through a resolvent shadow, and every decomposable solution generates a fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are maximally monotone on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_{\gamma A}(\operatorname{Fix}T)\subseteq\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\), with the stated converse construction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-point and resolvent-shadow formulation is coherent and the property kind fits the leaf, but the exact equivalence and converse construction have no supporting citation or locator.

children.title: Primal Proximal-Point QP
children.top_down_role: Proximal-point QP formulations centered on primal variables and primal geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Proximal-Point QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal-point iteration for a constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(Q\in\mathbb{S}_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a nonempty closed convex polyhedral set \(C\), \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and parameters \(\gamma_k>0\), define \(h(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\delta_C(x)\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute
\[x^{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\frac{1}{2\gamma_k}\lVert x-x^k\rVert^2\right\}=J_{\gamma_k\partial h}(x^k).\]
Stop when \(r^{k+1}=(x^k-x^{k+1})/\gamma_k\) satisfies a prescribed residual tolerance, and return \(x^{k+1}\); otherwise continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each primal proximal-point step solves a strongly convex regularized QP and stops when its inclusion residual is sufficiently small.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) and \(C\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and polyhedral.
\(\gamma_k>0\) for every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^{k+1}\in\partial h(x^{k+1})\), so the stopping residual directly measures primal stationarity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and residual identity are internally consistent and appropriate for the primal proximal-point leaf, but no source supports the update and stationarity interpretation.

children.title: Dual Proximal-Point QP
children.top_down_role: Proximal-point QP formulations centered on dual variables or multiplier geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Proximal-Point QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal-point iteration on the Fenchel dual QP objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the primal convex QP be \(\min_x f(x)+g(Kx)\), where \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex quadratic or polyhedral functions and strong Fenchel duality holds. Define the dual minimization objective
\[d(y)=f^*(-K^\top y)+g^*(y).\]
Given \(y^0\in\operatorname{dom}d\) and \(\sigma_k>0\), compute
\[y^{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y}\left\{d(y)+\frac{1}{2\sigma_k}\lVert y-y^k\rVert^2\right\}=J_{\sigma_k\partial d}(y^k).\]
Stop when \(s^{k+1}=(y^k-y^{k+1})/\sigma_k\) meets a prescribed tolerance, and return \(y^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual proximal-point method repeatedly minimizes the Fenchel dual objective plus a quadratic regularizer and monitors a dual stationarity residual.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex, and \(K\) is linear.
A qualification condition ensures strong Fenchel duality.
\(\sigma_k>0\) for every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s^{k+1}\in\partial d(y^{k+1})\), providing a verifiable dual-stationarity residual.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugates of f and g.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual proximal-point algorithm is plausible and correctly typed, but the dual formulation, update, and residual claim lack an authoritative citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Primal-Dual Proximal Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural links between primal proximal subproblems and their dual counterparts.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Proximal Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moreau correspondence between primal and conjugate proximal QP subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(h^*\) be its Fenchel conjugate. For every \(z\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\), define \(x=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(z)\) and \(y=(z-x)/\gamma\). Then
\[y=\operatorname{prox}_{h^*/\gamma}(z/\gamma),\qquad x+\gamma y=z,\qquad y\in\partial h(x),\qquad x\in\partial h^*(y).\]
Equivalently,
\[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(z)+\gamma\operatorname{prox}_{h^*/\gamma}(z/\gamma)=z.\]
When \(h\) is an extended-valued convex quadratic, both proximal evaluations are convex QPs and determine one another by this identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal proximal QP solution and its conjugate dual proximal solution are linked exactly by Moreau decomposition and subgradient inversion.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(z\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(z)+\gamma\operatorname{prox}_{h^*/\gamma}(z/\gamma)=z\).

notation.meaning: Proximal map of gamma times h.
Scaled primal proximal residual and conjugate proximal point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Moreau identity and subgradient correspondence are standard and the duality kind fits the leaf, but the record supplies no source or locator.

children.title: Preconditioned Proximal QP
children.top_down_role: Proximal QP variants using nonstandard metrics or problem-scaled regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Proximal QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-metric proximal-point iteration for a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\delta_C(x)\), with \(Q\succeq0\) and \(C\) nonempty, closed, and convex. Given \(x^0\) and symmetric matrices \(M_k\) satisfying \(mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI\) for constants \(0<m\leq M<\infty\), compute
\[x^{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\left\{h(x)+\tfrac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_{M_k}^2\right\}=(I+M_k^{-1}\partial h)^{-1}(x^k).\]
Stop when \(r^{k+1}=M_k(x^k-x^{k+1})\) meets a prescribed tolerance; otherwise update the metric and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite metric replaces scalar proximal regularization, producing a strongly convex preconditioned QP and a metric-scaled stationarity residual.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) and \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI\) uniformly in \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^{k+1}\in\partial h(x^{k+1})\), where \(r^{k+1}=M_k(x^k-x^{k+1})\).

notation.meaning: Metric norm given by the square root of v-transpose M_k v.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The variable-metric proximal update and metric-scaled residual are coherent and algorithmically appropriate, but they are unsupported by a cited source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Inexact Proximal QP
children.top_down_role: Proximal QP variants allowing controlled error in subproblem resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-controlled inexact proximal-point iteration for convex QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper closed convex extended-valued quadratic with \(\operatorname*{argmin}h\neq\varnothing\). Given \(x^0\), parameters \(\gamma_k\geq\underline\gamma>0\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\), choose \(x^{k+1}\) and an error \(e^{k+1}\) satisfying
\[e^{k+1}\in\partial h(x^{k+1})+\gamma_k^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k),\qquad \lVert e^{k+1}\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k.\]
Require \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\gamma_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\). Stop when the computable inclusion residual meets the requested tolerance; otherwise continue with the next inexact proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each proximal QP may be solved inexactly if its inclusion residual is controlled and the scaled errors are summable.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper, closed, convex, and has a minimizer.
\(\gamma_k\geq\underline\gamma>0\).
\(\sum_k\gamma_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted iterate satisfies an explicitly bounded perturbation of the exact proximal inclusion.

notation.meaning: Uniform positive lower bound on proximal parameters.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record states a specific absolute-residual inexactness model and scaled summability requirement. Those choices require authoritative sourcing before this algorithm variant can be accepted.

children.title: Metric-Error Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Interaction between chosen proximal metrics and admissible inexactness regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Error Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatible residual criterion for variable-metric inexact proximal steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a proper closed convex function \(h\), let variable metrics satisfy \(mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI\). An inexact metric-proximal step \(x^{k+1}\) is metric-error compatible if there exists \(e^{k+1}\) such that
\[e^{k+1}\in\partial h(x^{k+1})+M_k(x^{k+1}-x^k),\qquad \lVert e^{k+1}\rVert_{M_k^{-1}}\leq\varepsilon_k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty.\]
The dual metric is essential: \(\langle e^{k+1},x^{k+1}-x^k\rangle\) is then bounded in magnitude by \(\varepsilon_k\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert_{M_k}\), matching the geometry of the proximal regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-metric errors are compatible when measured in the dual metric and summably bounded, so error-work terms match the proximal geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI\) for fixed positive constants.
\(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lvert\langle e^{k+1},x^{k+1}-x^k\rangle\rvert\leq\varepsilon_k\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert_{M_k}\).

notation.meaning: Error norm dual to the primal M_k metric.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual-metric Cauchy-Schwarz bound is internally consistent and the condition kind fits the leaf, but the selected compatibility criterion and summability model have no supporting source.

children.title: Primal Douglas-Rachford QP
children.top_down_role: Douglas-Rachford QP constructions expressed through primal-space operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Douglas-Rachford QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Douglas–Rachford splitting of a quadratic objective and convex constraint indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_x f(x)+\delta_C(x)\), where \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), \(Q\succeq0\), and \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex. Given \(z^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\gamma>0\), iterate
\[x^k=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(z^k)=(I+\gamma Q)^{-1}(z^k-\gamma c),\]
\[w^k=P_C(2x^k-z^k),\qquad z^{k+1}=z^k+w^k-x^k.\]
Stop when \(\lVert w^k-x^k\rVert\) meets a prescribed fixed-point tolerance, and return the primal shadow \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal Douglas–Rachford alternates a linear-system quadratic proximal step with projection onto the feasible set and returns the proximal shadow.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) and \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is \(z^{k+1}=\tfrac12(I+R_{\gamma\delta_C}R_{\gamma f})z^k\), with output shadow \(x^k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal Douglas-Rachford steps and fixed-point form are consistent and correctly classified as an algorithm, but no citation supports the specialized QP formulation or stopping residual.

children.title: Dual Douglas-Rachford QP
children.top_down_role: Douglas-Rachford QP constructions expressed through dual-space operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Douglas-Rachford QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Douglas–Rachford splitting applied to the Fenchel dual QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal problem \(\min_x f(x)+g(x)\), assume proper closed convex \(f,g\) and strong Fenchel duality. Write its dual as
\[\min_y \phi(y)+\psi(y),\qquad \phi(y)=f^*(-y),\quad \psi(y)=g^*(y).\]
Given \(v^0\) and \(\sigma>0\), iterate
\[y^k=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma\phi}(v^k),\qquad q^k=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma\psi}(2y^k-v^k),\qquad v^{k+1}=v^k+q^k-y^k.\]
Stop when \(\lVert q^k-y^k\rVert\) meets a prescribed tolerance, and return the dual shadow \(y^k\). For quadratic-polyhedral \(f,g\), both proximal subproblems are convex QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual Douglas–Rachford applies the same reflected-proximal construction to the two terms of the Fenchel dual objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
A qualification condition ensures strong Fenchel duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^{k+1}=\tfrac12(I+R_{\sigma\psi}R_{\sigma\phi})v^k\), with dual output shadow \(y^k\).

notation.meaning: Sign-composed conjugate of the first primal term.
Conjugate of the second primal term.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual splitting is plausible for the stated Fenchel convention and fits the algorithm leaf, but the sign convention and proximal construction require an authoritative source with a precise locator.

children.title: Primal-Dual Douglas-Rachford Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural equivalences and variable mappings between primal-space and dual-space constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Douglas-Rachford Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT correspondence encoded by primal Douglas–Rachford fixed points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f,g\) be proper closed convex functions satisfying the subdifferential sum rule, let \(\gamma>0\), and define \(T=\tfrac12(I+R_{\gamma\partial g}R_{\gamma\partial f})\). If \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), set
\[x=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(z),\qquad y=(x-z)/\gamma.\]
Then
\[-y\in\partial f(x),\qquad y\in\partial g(x),\]
so \(x\) solves \(\min_x f(x)+g(x)\) and \(y\) solves \(\min_y f^*(-y)+g^*(y)\). Conversely, any primal-dual pair satisfying these inclusions generates the primal Douglas–Rachford fixed point \(z=x+\gamma(-y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Douglas–Rachford fixed point yields primal and dual optimal solutions satisfying Fenchel KKT conditions, and every such pair reconstructs a fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
The subdifferential sum rule and strong Fenchel duality hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\) corresponds to \(-y\in\partial f(x)\) and \(y\in\partial g(x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The signs in the stated KKT correspondence are internally consistent with the chosen shadow variable, and duality is the correct kind, but the full fixed-point correspondence lacks source support.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Douglas-Rachford QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxed Douglas–Rachford iteration with an admissible relaxation interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f,g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex quadratic or polyhedral functions with \(\operatorname*{argmin}(f+g)\neq\varnothing\). Given \(z^0\), \(\gamma>0\), and relaxation parameters \(\lambda_k\in[\underline\lambda,\overline\lambda]\subset(0,2)\), compute
\[x^k=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(z^k),\qquad w^k=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(2x^k-z^k),\]
\[z^{k+1}=z^k+\lambda_k(w^k-x^k).\]
Stop when \(\lVert w^k-x^k\rVert\) meets the fixed-point tolerance, and return \(x^k\). The choice \(\lambda_k=1\) recovers the standard Douglas–Rachford iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxed Douglas–Rachford scales the standard fixed-point displacement by a factor uniformly bounded inside the interval from zero to two.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex, and a minimizer exists.
\(0<\underline\lambda\leq\lambda_k\leq\overline\lambda<2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^{k+1}=z^k+\lambda_k(Tz^k-z^k)\), where \(T=\tfrac12(I+R_{\gamma\partial g}R_{\gamma\partial f})\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxed iteration is coherent and correctly classified as an algorithm, but the admissible relaxation interval and associated fixed-point interpretation are not supported by any cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the QP \(\min_{x\in C} f(x)\), introduce a copy \(z\) and write \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+\delta_C(z)\) subject to \(x-z=0\). Scaled ADMM initializes \(z^0,u^0\in\mathbb R^n\) and iterates
\[
x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\left\{f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-z^k+u^k\rVert^2\right\},\qquad z^{k+1}=\Pi_C(x^{k+1}+u^k),
\]
\[
u^{k+1}=u^k+x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}.
\]
It stops when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances for \(r^{k+1}=x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\) and \(s^{k+1}=\rho(z^{k+1}-z^k)\) are met, and returns \(z^{k+1}\).

children.top_down_role: Splitting architectures based on local variable copies linked by agreement constraints.

assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At convergence, \(x_i=z\) for every \(i\), and \(z\) minimizes \(\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(z)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Express \(\min_z\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(z)\) as \(\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_N,z}\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(x_i=z\) for every \(i\). Given \(z^0\) and \(u_i^0\), consensus ADMM computes in parallel
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x_i-z^k+u_i^k\rVert^2\right\},
\]
then
\[
z^{k+1}=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N(x_i^{k+1}+u_i^k),\qquad u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-z^{k+1}.
\]
The method returns \(z^{k+1}\) after all consensus and dual residuals meet their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local blocks optimize independently, then average their shifted variables into one global variable while dual updates enforce consensus.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Splitting

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The sharing problem
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_N}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)+g\left(\sum_{i=1}^N A_ix_i\right)\right\}
\]
has the equivalent split form
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_N,z_1,\ldots,z_N}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)+g\left(\sum_{i=1}^N z_i\right)\right\}
\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_ix_i-z_i=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,N).
\]
Consequently, two-block ADMM may group all \(x_i\) into one block and all \(z_i\) into the other; the \(x_i\)-minimizations are separable, while the \(z\)-minimization contains the shared aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Copy each block’s contribution to the aggregate, making local updates separable and confining global coupling to the copied-image block.

children.title: Consensus-Sharing Duality
children.top_down_role: Representation-level links between agreement coupling and shared-resource coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus-Sharing Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel duality between global-variable consensus and zero-sum sharing formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the consensus problem
\[
p^\star=\inf_{z\in\mathbb R^n}\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(z),
\]
introduce copies \(x_i=z\) and multipliers \(y_i\). Minimization of the Lagrangian over \(z\) is finite exactly when \(\sum_{i=1}^N y_i=0\), and minimization over each \(x_i\) yields \(-f_i^*(-y_i)\). Hence
\[
p^\star=\sup_{\sum_{i=1}^N y_i=0}\left\{-\sum_{i=1}^N f_i^*(-y_i)\right\}.
\]
Thus a primal consensus architecture is dual to a sharing architecture in which the dual blocks jointly satisfy a zero-sum aggregate constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fenchel dualization transforms equality of all primal copies into a zero-sum constraint shared by the dual blocks.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(\bigcap_{i=1}^N\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i)\neq\varnothing\).
The primal consensus value \(p^\star\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consensus coupling in the primal becomes the zero-sum sharing constraint \(\sum_i y_i=0\) in the dual.

children.title: Range-Space Splitting
children.top_down_role: Splitting organized around affine images, constraint ranges, or reduced range-space variables.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(A\) has full row rank.
\(q\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality-constrained QP is solved through the positive-definite range-space system \((AQ^{-1}A^\top)y=-b-AQ^{-1}q\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Schur-complement range-space reduction is standard for equality-constrained positive-definite QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical Schur-complement range-space reduction for an equality-constrained strictly convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\frac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x:Ax=b\right\},
\]
initialize no iteration and eliminate \(x\) from the KKT equations. Stationarity gives \(x=-Q^{-1}(q+A^\top y)\). Substitute this expression into \(Ax=b\), solve
\[
(AQ^{-1}A^\top)y=-b-AQ^{-1}q,
\]
and recover
\[
x=-Q^{-1}(q+A^\top y).
\]
Because \(Q\) is positive definite and \(A\) has full row rank, \(AQ^{-1}A^\top\) is positive definite. The algorithm outputs the recovered \(x\), together with \(y\) when a dual solution is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate the primal variable, solve a Schur-complement system in constraint space, and recover the unique primal QP solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space Splitting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Schur-complement calculation is standard and correct, but no cited source establishes that this direct KKT reduction is the intended “Range-Space Splitting” architecture in the local ADMM branch.

children.title: Dual Splitting
children.top_down_role: Splitting organized directly in multiplier or dual-variable space.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(q\in\mathbb R^n\).
The equality system \(Ax=b\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any maximizer \(y^\star\) of the displayed dual produces the primal optimizer \(x^\star=-Q^{-1}(q+A^\top y^\star)\).

notation.meaning: primal variable recovered from a dual point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: eliminating a strictly convex quadratic primal block gives its standard equality-constrained QP dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-space reduction obtained by eliminating the primal variable of an equality-constrained strictly convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the equality-constrained QP \(\min_x \tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), the Lagrangian is \(L(x,y)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x+y^\top(Ax-b)\). Eliminating \(x\) gives
\[
x(y)=-Q^{-1}(q+A^\top y)
\]
and the unconstrained concave dual
\[
\max_{y\in\mathbb R^m} d(y),\qquad d(y)=-\frac12(q+A^\top y)^\top Q^{-1}(q+A^\top y)-b^\top y.
\]
Thus a dual splitting or first-order method may operate entirely on \(y\), using \(\nabla d(y)=Ax(y)-b\), and recover the primal optimizer from its terminal dual point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate the strictly convex primal block, optimize the resulting concave quadratic over multipliers, and recover the primal solution algebraically.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Splitting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed equality-constrained QP dual is correct, but the record provides no source supporting its identification as the terminal container’s “Dual Splitting” rather than merely a dual representation.

children.title: Range-Space Dual Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which range-space formulations coincide with or differ from dual formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
The equality-constrained QP \(\min\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x:Ax=b\}\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The range-space multiplier is exactly the dual maximizer, and its Schur-complement equation is the dual stationarity equation.

notation.meaning: primal point induced by a multiplier

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the Schur-complement equation and stationarity of the equality-constrained QP dual coincide algebraically
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between the Schur-complement range-space solve and stationarity of the QP dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The dual gradient satisfies
\[
\nabla d(y)=Ax(y)-b=-AQ^{-1}(q+A^\top y)-b.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\nabla d(y)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(AQ^{-1}A^\top)y=-b-AQ^{-1}q.
\]
The right-hand equation is precisely the range-space Schur-complement system. Since \(S=AQ^{-1}A^\top\) is positive definite, it has a unique solution \(y^\star\); this same vector is the unique maximizer of the strictly concave dual objective. In both constructions the associated primal solution is
\[
x^\star=-Q^{-1}(q+A^\top y^\star).
\]
Thus range-space elimination and unconstrained dual solution are two representations of the same KKT reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The range-space Schur equation is exactly dual stationarity, so both approaches produce the same multiplier and recovered primal solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space Dual Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic correspondence between dual stationarity and the range-space Schur system is correct, but the nontrivial correspondence has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Over-Relaxed ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM variants using extrapolative relaxation beyond the unrelaxed setting.

knowledge_statements.title: Over-Relaxed ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extrapolating subregime of relaxed two-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In relaxed ADMM, replace \(Ax^{k+1}\) in the second-block and multiplier updates by
\[
\widehat a^{k+1}=\alpha Ax^{k+1}+(1-\alpha)(c-Bz^k).
\]
When \(1<\alpha<2\), the coefficient \(1-\alpha\) is negative, so \(\widehat a^{k+1}\) extrapolates from the previous feasible-side image \(c-Bz^k\) through the new image \(Ax^{k+1}\). This regime is over-relaxed ADMM. At any fixed point satisfying \(Ax+Bz=c\), the relaxed image equals \(Ax\), so over-relaxation changes the iteration but not its primal-dual fixed-point equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing the relaxation parameter strictly between one and two extrapolates the transmitted affine image without changing ADMM’s fixed-point equations.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions ensuring convergence of relaxed two-block ADMM hold.
The relaxation parameter satisfies \(1<\alpha<2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Over-relaxation extrapolates beyond \(Ax^{k+1}\) while preserving the standard relaxed-ADMM fixed points for \(1<\alpha<2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The classical relaxed two-block ADMM convergence range is
\[
0<\alpha<2.
\]
The subinterval \(0<\alpha<1\) is under-relaxation, \(\alpha=1\) is standard ADMM, and \(1<\alpha<2\) is over-relaxation. At \(\alpha=0\), the transmitted image becomes \(c-Bz^k\), so the relaxed primal residual used in the multiplier update is \(B(z^{k+1}-z^k)\) and the new \(x\)-image is not transmitted. At \(\alpha=2\), the averaged-operator argument underlying the general guarantee reaches its excluded endpoint. Values outside the open interval therefore require additional problem-specific analysis and have no uniform convex two-block convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General relaxed-ADMM theory uses the open interval from zero to two; zero stalls the new image, while two and beyond need extra assumptions.

children.title: Proximal ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM variants adding proximal regularization to one or more subproblems.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex, and the constraint \(Ax+Bz=c\) has a saddle point.
\(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(R\in\mathbb S_+^p\), and \(\rho>0\).
The proximal subproblems admit minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The added positive-semidefinite terms vanish at a fixed point and regularize the two ADMM subproblems without changing the original KKT solutions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: proximal ADMM adds positive-semidefinite squared-distance terms to the standard scaled ADMM subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block scaled proximal ADMM with fixed positive-semidefinite proximal metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), choose \(z^0,u^0\) and, when needed, \(x^0\). Proximal ADMM iterates
\[
x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x\left\{f(x)+\frac\rho2\lVert Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert x-x^k\rVert_P^2\right\},
\]
\[
z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_z\left\{g(z)+\frac\rho2\lVert Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\rVert^2+\frac12\lVert z-z^k\rVert_R^2\right\},
\]
\[
u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.
\]
It stops at prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances and returns the latest primal pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add positive-semidefinite proximal distances to both ADMM subproblems to regularize or simplify them while retaining the original fixed points.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal ADMM

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed fixed-metric proximal-ADMM updates are standard, but no authoritative source or locator supports this precise two-sided positive-semidefinite variant and its fixed-point claim.

children.title: Variable-Metric ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM variants whose subproblem geometry changes through iteration-dependent metrics.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are closed, proper, and convex.
A saddle point exists for \(\min\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\}\).
The penalty metrics satisfy \(0<\underline r I\preceq R_k\preceq \overline r I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^k,z^k,y^k)\) is the variable-metric ADMM sequence defined by the displayed updates.

notation.meaning: Symmetric positive-definite penalty metric at iteration k.
Squared seminorm induced by a positive-semidefinite matrix.
Unscaled multiplier for the coupling equality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unscaled two-block ADMM with an iteration-dependent quadratic penalty metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \((z^0,y^0)\) and symmetric positive-definite \(R_k\), compute
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax+Bz^k-c\rangle+\tfrac12\|Ax+Bz^k-c\|_{R_k}^2\right\},
\]
\[
z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_z\left\{g(z)+\langle y^k,Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c\rangle+\tfrac12\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c\|_{R_k}^2\right\},
\]
and then set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+R_k(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c)\). Stop when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances hold; output the latest primal pair and multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-metric ADMM replaces the scalar penalty by a uniformly positive-definite metric in both alternating subproblems and the multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric ADMM

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the terminal container and the displayed updates are internally consistent, but no inspectable citation supports this variable-metric ADMM formulation. In particular, the relation between uniform metric bounds, admissible metric variation, and any convergence interpretation remains unsupported.

children.title: Proximal-Metric Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Structural interaction between proximal regularization and metric selection.

assumptions_latex: \(R_k\succ0\) is the residual penalty metric.
\(S_k\succeq0\) and \(T_k\succeq0\) are intended proximal metrics for the two blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_{x,k}=A^\top R_kA+S_k\succeq0\) and \(H_{z,k}=B^\top R_kB+T_k\succeq0\), with strict positivity when unique quadratic subproblem minimizers are required.

notation.meaning: Added proximal metrics for the x and z blocks.
Effective quadratic metrics of the block subproblems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic compatibility of residual and proximal metrics in a two-block quadratic splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For residual term \(\tfrac12\|Ax+Bz-c\|_{R_k}^2\), adding proximal terms \(\tfrac12\|x-x^k\|_{S_k}^2\) and \(\tfrac12\|z-z^k\|_{T_k}^2\) is metric-compatible when \(R_k\succ0\), \(S_k\succeq0\), and \(T_k\succeq0\). The induced block curvatures are
\[
H_{x,k}=A^\top R_kA+S_k,
\qquad
H_{z,k}=B^\top R_kB+T_k.
\]
They must be positive semidefinite for convex subproblems and positive definite whenever the implementation requires unique block minimizers. Thus proximal regularization may supply curvature missing because \(A\) or \(B\) is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatibility requires positive-semidefinite proximal additions and effective block metrics that provide the curvature required by each ADMM subproblem.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Metric Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the compatibility leaf, but no source is supplied for the named condition. Moreover, the stated effective curvatures omit curvature contributed by the block objectives; positive definiteness of the displayed matrices is sufficient but is not generally necessary for unique minimizers when f or g supplies strict or strong convexity.

children.title: Inexact ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM variants permitting controlled subproblem error.

assumptions_latex: The exact two-block ADMM problem has a saddle point and solvable subproblems.
Approximate subproblem optimality residuals satisfy \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(\|e_x^k\|+\|e_z^k\|)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inexact updates have absolutely summable perturbations relative to exact ADMM.

notation.meaning: Optimality residuals of the approximate block solves.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block convex ADMM with summably inaccurate block minimizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \((z^0,y^0)\) and choose \(\rho>0\). At iteration \(k\), select \(x^{k+1}\) and \(z^{k+1}\) satisfying
\[
e_x^k\in\partial_x L_\rho(x^{k+1},z^k,y^k),
\qquad
e_z^k\in\partial_z L_\rho(x^{k+1},z^{k+1},y^k),
\]
where the residuals obey \(\sum_k(\|e_x^k\|+\|e_z^k\|)<\infty\). Update \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c)\). Stop when the outer primal and dual residuals meet their tolerances; output the latest iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact ADMM permits approximate block solves whose optimality residuals are absolutely summable, followed by the usual multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact ADMM

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and summable-error formulation are plausible, but no citation identifies the precise inexact-ADMM theorem or error criterion being used. A source is required to determine whether summability of these subgradient residuals, rather than another absolute or relative error condition, is sufficient under the stated hypotheses.

children.title: Matrix-Free ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM implementations using operator products instead of explicit matrix factorizations.

assumptions_latex: Each ADMM block subproblem is convex and admits a matrix-vector-product implementation.
Required proximal maps or projections are available without forming the system matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration can be executed using operator products and vector operations, without explicit matrix assembly or factorization.

notation.meaning: Inner stopping tolerance at outer iteration k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: An implementation regime based exclusively on forward and adjoint operator products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent \(A\), \(B\), and their adjoints as callable linear operators. Initialize \((z^0,y^0)\). At each outer iteration, solve the two ADMM block optimality systems iteratively using only evaluations of \(Av\), \(A^\top w\), \(Bv\), and \(B^\top w\), terminating each inner solve when its computable optimality residual is at most \(\eta_k\). Apply the usual multiplier update using \(r^{k+1}=Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c\). Stop on outer residual tolerances and return the latest iterates; no explicit assembled normal matrix or factorization is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix-free ADMM performs block solves and residual updates through forward and adjoint operator products, avoiding assembled normal matrices and direct factorizations.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free ADMM

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role matches the terminal container, but the record has no source for the matrix-free ADMM specification or for the relationship between the inner tolerances and valid outer updates. The availability of operator products alone also does not establish that every stated block solve can be performed without additional operators or proximal evaluations.

children.title: Krylov-Based ADMM Subsolves
children.top_down_role: Iterative linear-algebra regimes supporting matrix-free or inexact ADMM subproblems.

assumptions_latex: The ADMM block optimality system is \(H_k u=b_k\), where \(H_k\) is symmetric positive definite.
Products \(v\mapsto H_kv\) are available; when preconditioned conjugate gradient is used, its preconditioner is symmetric positive definite.
A positive inner residual tolerance \(\eta_k>0\) is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted inner iterate \(u_{k,j}\) satisfies \(\|b_k-H_ku_{k,j}\|\leq\eta_k\) before the corresponding ADMM outer update is performed.

notation.meaning: Symmetric positive-definite block-system operator at outer iteration k.
Conjugate-gradient inner iterate at outer iteration k and inner iteration j.
Positive inner residual tolerance at outer iteration k.
Linear-system residual at outer iteration k and inner iteration j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate-gradient solution of symmetric positive-definite ADMM block systems; no outer-convergence claim is made without a separate forcing rule.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Conjugate Gradient Method p. 75; 5.1.5 Convergence of the Conjugate Gradient Method p. 83
source_refs.source_title: Trust Region Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ADMM block equation \(H_ku=b_k\), initialize \(u_{k,0}\), form \(r_{k,0}=b_k-H_ku_{k,0}\), and apply conjugate gradient, or symmetric positive-definite preconditioned conjugate gradient, using products with \(H_k\). Generate mutually \(H_k\)-conjugate search directions and use the conjugate-gradient step lengths; equivalently, in exact arithmetic, each iterate minimizes the associated strictly convex quadratic over the current affine Krylov space. Terminate at the first \(j\) satisfying \(\|r_{k,j}\|\leq\eta_k\), accept \(u_{k,j}\) as the inexact ADMM block solution, and then perform the corresponding outer update. This inner-solve specification alone makes no outer-convergence assertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a symmetric positive-definite ADMM block system, conjugate gradients minimizes the associated quadratic over successive Krylov spaces and returns the first inner iterate whose linear residual meets the prescribed tolerance.

assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is closed, proper, and convex.
Every cyclic block subproblem has a selected minimizer.
The coupling constraint is \(\sum_{i=1}^pA_ix_i=c\) with \(p\geq3\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Gauss-Seidel sweep and multiplier update define direct multi-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct cyclic Gauss-Seidel extension of ADMM to at least three primal blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \((x_1^0,\ldots,x_p^0,y^0)\) and choose \(\rho>0\). For \(i=1,\ldots,p\), compute
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+\left\langle y^k,\sum_{j<i}A_jx_j^{k+1}+A_ix_i+\sum_{j>i}A_jx_j^k-c\right\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|\sum_{j<i}A_jx_j^{k+1}+A_ix_i+\sum_{j>i}A_jx_j^k-c\right\|^2\right\}.
\]
Then set \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(\sum_iA_ix_i^{k+1}-c)\). Stop on prescribed residual tolerances. This definition alone makes no convergence assertion for \(p\geq3\).

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are closed, proper, and convex, and \(K\) is linear.
The saddle problem \(\min_x\max_y f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-g^*(y)\) has a solution.
Step sizes satisfy \(\tau\sigma\|K\|^2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^k,y^k)\) is the PDHG sequence for the stated convex QP splitting.

notation.meaning: Proximal mapping of a convex function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard constant-step PDHG applied to a convex quadratic-program splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write the convex QP as \(\min_x f(x)+g(Kx)\), where the quadratic objective and simple primal constraints are included in \(f\). Initialize \((x^0,y^0)\), set \(\bar x^0=x^0\), and choose \(\tau,\sigma>0\) with \(\tau\sigma\|K\|^2<1\). Iterate
\[
y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma g^*}(y^k+\sigma K\bar x^k),
\qquad
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau f}(x^k-\tau K^\top y^{k+1}),
\]
\[
\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+(x^{k+1}-x^k).
\]
Stop using prescribed primal-dual residual tolerances and return the latest or ergodically averaged primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PDHG alternates a dual proximal step, a primal proximal step containing the quadratic objective, and primal extrapolation under a coupled step-size bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Hybrid Gradient for QP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the PDHG-for-QP leaf, and the update order and strict step-size bound describe a standard PDHG variant. No citation supports the exact saddle formulation, update convention, QP specialization, or stated output alternatives.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(\gamma\)-strongly convex for some \(\gamma>0\), while \(g\) is closed, proper, and convex.
The initial step sizes satisfy \(\tau_0\sigma_0\|K\|^2<1\).

notation.meaning: Strong-convexity modulus of the primal term.
Iteration-dependent primal and dual step sizes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly convex primal acceleration with coupled variable step sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \((x^0,y^0)\), set \(\bar x^0=x^0\), and choose \(\tau_0,\sigma_0>0\) with \(\tau_0\sigma_0\|K\|^2<1\). For \(k\geq0\), compute
\[
y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma_k g^*}(y^k+\sigma_kK\bar x^k),
\qquad
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau_k f}(x^k-\tau_kK^\top y^{k+1}).
\]
Set \(\theta_k=(1+2\gamma\tau_k)^{-1/2}\), \(\tau_{k+1}=\theta_k\tau_k\), \(\sigma_{k+1}=\sigma_k/\theta_k\), and \(\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta_k(x^{k+1}-x^k)\). Stop on prescribed primal-dual residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the primal term is strongly convex, accelerated PDHG couples decreasing primal steps, increasing dual steps, and scaled extrapolation.

Selected terminal or averaged inner iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

reset extrapolation by \(\bar x_{s+1}^0=x_{s+1}^0\), and optionally update the step sizes according to the fixed restart rule. Stop when the restart-point residual or gap satisfies its tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\,z\in\mathbb{R}^m} f(x)+g(z)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Bz=c,

children.title: Saddle-Point Existence Regime
children.top_down_role: ADMM applicability organized around the existence of an appropriate primal-dual saddle point.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are closed, proper, and convex.
The Lagrangian is \(L(x,z,y)=f(x)+g(z)+\langle y,Ax+Bz-c\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A saddle point exists exactly when there is \((x^*,z^*,y^*)\) satisfying the displayed saddle inequalities.

notation.meaning: Lagrangian of the equality-coupled splitting problem.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Lagrangian saddle-point existence for equality-coupled convex splitting.

source_refs.locator: 2.12.2 Saddle Point of a Function p. 75
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Global Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The saddle-point existence regime holds when there is \((x^*,z^*,y^*)\) such that
\[
L(x^*,z^*,y)\leq L(x^*,z^*,y^*)\leq L(x,z,y^*)
\]
for every \((x,z,y)\) in the ambient primal-dual space. For the equality-coupled convex problem, this is equivalently expressed by
\[
Ax^*+Bz^*=c,
\qquad
0\in\partial f(x^*)+A^\top y^*,
\qquad
0\in\partial g(z^*)+B^\top y^*.
\]
Thus the regime requires a primal feasible optimizer and a multiplier satisfying both block stationarity inclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A saddle point exists when a feasible primal pair and multiplier satisfy both block stationarity inclusions, equivalently the global Lagrangian saddle inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Existence Regime

children.title: Primal Solution Existence Regime
children.top_down_role: Coverage determined by attainment of the primal QP solution set.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Solution Existence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient finite-dimensional attainment regime for the convex QP used in ADMM splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\inf_{x\in F} f(x)\), where \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\), \(P\succeq0\), and \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\in C\}\) for a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^m\). If \(F\neq\varnothing\), the optimal value is finite, and \(f\) is level-bounded on \(F\), meaning that \(\{x\in F:f(x)\leq\alpha\}\) is bounded for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), then the QP attains its minimum: \(X^\star=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible convex QP has a primal optimizer when its finite objective is level-bounded over the closed feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(F\neq\varnothing\) and the primal value is finite.
\(f\) is level-bounded on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^\star\neq\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional level-boundedness attainment condition is mathematically plausible and fits the condition container, but no cited source or inspectable locator supports it.

children.title: Dual Solution Existence Regime
children.top_down_role: Coverage determined by attainment of a compatible dual solution set.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Solution Existence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-interior qualification ensuring dual attainment for the set-constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(P\succeq0\), and consider \(\inf_x\{f(x)+\delta_C(Ax)\}\), where \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty, closed, and convex. If the primal value \(p^\star\) is finite and there exists \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ax_0\in\operatorname{ri}C\), then the dual \(\sup_y\{-f^*(-A^{\mathsf T}y)-\sigma_C(y)\}\) attains its optimum at some \(y^\star\), and \(d^\star=p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-interior feasible point and finite primal value ensure strong duality and attainment of the Fenchel dual.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(p^\star\in\mathbb R\).
\(Ax_0\in\operatorname{ri}C\) for some \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y^\star\neq\varnothing\) and \(d^\star=p^\star\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-interior qualification and stated Fenchel dual are plausible, but the strong-duality and dual-attainment conclusion requires an authoritative, specifically located source.

children.title: Existence-Gap Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where primal or dual attainment fails to furnish the saddle structure required by standard convergence coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: Existence-Gap Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between separate primal or dual existence and the saddle-point hypothesis required by standard ADMM theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the Lagrangian \(L(x,z,y)=f(x)+\delta_C(z)+y^{\mathsf T}(Ax-z)\), a saddle point \((x^\star,z^\star,y^\star)\) exists if and only if the primal and dual optima are both attained and their finite values agree. Thus primal attainment alone does not establish the ADMM saddle-point hypothesis; neither does equality \(p^\star=d^\star\) without dual attainment. If \(X^\star=\varnothing\), \(Y^\star=\varnothing\), or \(p^\star>d^\star\), no primal-dual saddle point exists and the standard saddle-based ADMM convergence conclusion is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ADMM’s saddle-point premise fails if either optimum is unattained or a positive duality gap remains.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(\delta_C\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(L\) is the Lagrangian of the constraint \(Ax-z=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\operatorname{Sad}(L)
eq\varnothing\iff X^\star
eq\varnothing,\ Y^\star
eq\varnothing,\ p^\star=d^\star\in\mathbb R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the asserted equivalence among saddle-point existence, bilateral attainment, and zero finite duality gap has no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Solvability Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete well-posedness conditions for the two exact minimizations in QP ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the splitting \(Ax-z=0\) with penalty \(\rho>0\), the ADMM updates are \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x+\tfrac\rho2\|Ax-z^k+u^k\|^2\}\) and \(z^{k+1}=\Pi_C(Ax^{k+1}+u^k)\). If \(P+\rho A^{\mathsf T}A\succ0\), equivalently \(\ker P\cap\ker A=\{0\}\), the first update has a unique solution for every finite \((z^k,u^k)\). If \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, the projection update also exists uniquely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both ADMM subproblems are uniquely solvable when the augmented quadratic is positive definite and the constraint set is nonempty, closed, and convex.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(\rho>0\).
\(\ker P\cap\ker A=\{0\}\).
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) and \(z^{k+1}\) exist uniquely for every finite \((z^k,u^k)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-definiteness/nullspace equivalence and projection solvability claims are precise and appropriate as a condition, but no inspectable source is cited.
