children.title: Rank-Deficient QP Coverage
children.top_down_role: ADMM convergence coverage when constraint or system matrices lack full rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient QP Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank deficiency compatible with exact QP ADMM when the augmented Hessian remains nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Neither \(P\) nor \(A\) must be full rank for the QP ADMM update. For \(P\succeq0\) and \(\rho>0\), \(P+\rho A^{\mathsf T}A\succ0\) holds exactly when \(\ker P\cap\ker A=\{0\}\). Hence a singular quadratic Hessian or rank-deficient constraint map is covered whenever their null spaces have trivial intersection. Under this condition the primal quadratic subproblem is uniquely solvable, so rank deficiency alone does not invalidate the standard exact-subproblem ADMM iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singular QP matrices are admissible when the Hessian and constraint map have no common nonzero null direction.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(\rho>0\).
\(\ker P\cap\ker A=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P+\rho A^{\mathsf T}A\succ0\), even if \(P\) or \(A\) is rank deficient.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nullspace criterion is mathematically plausible and the property kind fits, but its claimed coverage by standard exact-subproblem ADMM lacks cited evidence.

children.title: Nonunique-Solution QP Coverage
children.top_down_role: ADMM convergence coverage when primal or dual solution sets contain multiple points.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique-Solution QP Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence claims retained when the optimal set is non-singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the convex QP splitting has a saddle point and every ADMM subproblem is solved exactly. Uniqueness of the primal optimizer is not required for feasibility-residual convergence or optimal-value convergence. If the primal iterates are bounded, every cluster point satisfying the limiting constraint is a primal optimizer. However, these conclusions do not by themselves imply convergence of the entire sequence \((x^k)\) to one member of a non-singleton solution set; such iterate convergence requires an additional uniqueness, injectivity, or regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ADMM residual and value convergence can survive nonunique optima, although the complete primal-iterate sequence need not select one optimizer.
assumptions_latex: The QP is convex and its primal-dual Lagrangian has a saddle point.
ADMM subproblems are solved exactly.
The primal-iterate sequence is bounded when cluster points are asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^k\to0\) and objective values approach \(p^\star\), while full convergence of \(x^k\) is not implied by nonempty \(X^\star\) alone.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the container, but the residual, objective-value, cluster-point, and absence-of-full-iterate-convergence claims require a theorem source establishing the precise hypotheses.

children.title: Rank-Deficiency-Induced Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Situations in which algebraic rank loss contributes to nonunique iterates, multipliers, or solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficiency-Induced Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-nullspace mechanism producing an affine family of QP optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^\star\) minimize \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax\in C\), with \(P\succeq0\). If a nonzero direction \(d\) satisfies \(Pd=0\), \(Ad=0\), and \(q^{\mathsf T}d=0\), then \(A(x^\star+td)=Ax^\star\) and \(f(x^\star+td)=f(x^\star)\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\). Consequently the entire affine line \(\{x^\star+td:t\in\mathbb R\}\) consists of primal optimizers, so the solution is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero direction invisible to both the quadratic curvature and constraints, and orthogonal to the linear cost, creates infinitely many optimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(x^\star\) is primal optimal.
\(q^{\mathsf T}d=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star+td\in X^\star\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The common-null-direction mechanism is internally consistent and fits the property container, but the record supplies no source with a specific locator.

children.title: Primal Residual Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence behavior of residuals measuring split-constraint consistency.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Residual Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard exact two-block ADMM feasibility conclusion for the QP splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply exact two-block ADMM with fixed \(\rho>0\) to \(\min_{x,z}\{f(x)+\delta_C(z):Ax-z=0\}\), where \(f\) and \(\delta_C\) are proper, closed, and convex. If the unaugmented Lagrangian has a saddle point and both update subproblems attain their minima at every iteration, then the primal residual \(r^{k}=Ax^{k}-z^{k}\) converges to zero. Thus asymptotic feasibility holds even when the primal optimizer is not unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a saddle point and exactly solvable subproblems, the ADMM constraint violation converges to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(\delta_C\) are proper, closed, and convex.
A primal-dual saddle point exists.
ADMM uses fixed \(\rho>0\) and exact attained updates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind and residual conclusion fit the leaf, but the exact ADMM convergence theorem and its sufficient hypotheses are unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Dual Residual Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence behavior of residuals measuring dual-side stationarity change.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Residual Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard exact two-block ADMM stationarity-residual conclusion for the QP splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under exact two-block ADMM for \(\min_{x,z}\{f(x)+\delta_C(z):Ax-z=0\}\), define the dual residual by \(s^{k}=\rho A^{\mathsf T}(z^{k}-z^{k-1})\). If \(f\) and \(\delta_C\) are proper, closed, and convex, the Lagrangian has a saddle point, the penalty \(\rho>0\) is fixed, and both subproblems attain their exact minima, then \(s^k\to0\). This residual measures the stationarity discrepancy induced by the change in the split variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard exact ADMM assumptions, the stationarity residual generated by consecutive split-variable iterates converges to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(\delta_C\) are proper, closed, and convex.
A primal-dual saddle point exists.
ADMM uses fixed \(\rho>0\) and exact attained updates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the leaf, but the dual-residual convention and convergence conclusion require an authoritative theorem locator for this splitting and sign convention.

children.title: Residual Convergence Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Regimes in which primal and dual residuals decay at materially different scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Convergence Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual convergence does not supply a balanced relative rate or scale-independent comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conclusions \(\|r^k\|_2\to0\) and \(\|s^k\|_2\to0\) do not imply that their ratio is bounded above or below. Indeed, vanishing nonnegative sequences may satisfy \(a_k=k^{-1}\) and \(b_k=k^{-2}\), for which \(a_k/b_k=k\to\infty\). Moreover, \(r^k=Ax^k-z^k\) and \(s^k=\rho A^{\mathsf T}(z^k-z^{k-1})\) have different scaling dependencies. Therefore separate residual convergence alone cannot justify a universal residual-balance constant or a penalty-update rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both residuals may vanish at very different relative rates, so convergence alone neither balances them nor validates residual-based penalty adaptation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No constant \(M\geq1\) satisfying \(M^{-1}\leq\|r^k\|_2/\|s^k\|_2\leq M\) eventually follows from separate convergence alone.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical warning that separate convergence does not imply comparable rates is sound and fits a failure boundary, but the ADMM-specific scaling and penalty-rule claims need cited support.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Value Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal-value convergence for exact two-block ADMM applied to the convex QP splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider exact two-block ADMM for \(\min_{x,z}\{f(x)+\delta_C(z):Ax-z=0\}\), with fixed \(\rho>0\). Suppose \(f\) and \(\delta_C\) are proper, closed, and convex, both subproblems attain their minima, and a primal-dual saddle point exists with finite value \(p^\star\). Then the split objective values converge to the optimum: \(f(x^k)+\delta_C(z^k)\to p^\star\). When each projection update yields \(z^k\in C\), this reduces to \(f(x^k)\to p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard exact ADMM assumptions, the QP objective values converge to the finite primal optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(\delta_C\) are proper, closed, and convex.
A saddle point with finite value \(p^\star\) exists.
Fixed-penalty ADMM subproblems are solved exactly and attain their minima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^k)+\delta_C(z^k)\to p^\star\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits, but convergence of the particular nonergodic split-objective sequence under exactly these assumptions requires an authoritative, specifically located theorem.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Iterate Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient full-iterate convergence regime using injectivity of the QP constraint map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply exact fixed-penalty ADMM to \(\min_{x,z}\{f(x)+\delta_C(z):Ax-z=0\}\). Suppose the functions are proper, closed, and convex, a saddle point exists, the subproblems attain their minima, and \(A\) has full column rank. Standard ADMM convergence gives \(z^k\to z^\star\), \(y^k\to y^\star\), and \(Ax^k-z^k\to0\). Hence \(Ax^k\to z^\star\); injectivity of \(A\) then yields \(x^k\to x^\star\), where \((x^\star,z^\star,y^\star)\) is a primal-dual saddle point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard ADMM limits plus a full-column-rank constraint map imply convergence of both primal variables and the dual iterate to a saddle point.
assumptions_latex: The split objective functions are proper, closed, and convex and possess a saddle point.
ADMM uses fixed positive penalty and exact attained updates.
\(A\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^k,z^k,y^k)\to(x^\star,z^\star,y^\star)\in\operatorname{Sad}(L)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the iterate-convergence container, but convergence of both the split and dual iterates under the stated assumptions—and the resulting full primal convergence—must be checked against a specifically located ADMM theorem.

children.title: Ergodic ADMM Rates
children.top_down_role: Rate guarantees attached to averaged ADMM iterates or averaged residual quantities.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, convex functions, and the problem \(\min\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\}\) has a saddle point.
Two-block ADMM is run with fixed penalty \(\rho>0\), exact subproblem solutions, and unrelaxed updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G(\bar x^N,\bar z^N)=O(N^{-1})\) and \(\|A\bar x^N+B\bar z^N-c\|=O(N^{-1})\).

notation.meaning: Cesaro averages of the first N ADMM primal iterates
primal-dual saddle-gap functional relative to any fixed saddle point

review_flags: Exact source theorem and constants are not supplied; an ADMM ergodic-rate source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard two-block convex ADMM with fixed penalty and Cesaro averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any saddle point \((x^\star,z^\star,y^\star)\), define \((\bar x^N,\bar z^N)=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^N(x^k,z^k)\). There exists a finite constant \(C\), determined by the initial primal-dual distance, \(\rho\), and the chosen saddle point but independent of \(N\), such that the primal-dual saddle gap and feasibility residual satisfy \[\mathcal G(\bar x^N,\bar z^N)\leq \frac{C}{N},\qquad \|A\bar x^N+B\bar z^N-c\|\leq \frac{C}{N}.\] Thus ADMM attains an \(O(1/N)\) certificate for averaged iterates without requiring strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For standard convex two-block ADMM, Cesaro-averaged iterates have objective saddle gap and constraint violation of order one over the iteration count.
knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic ADMM Rates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the simultaneous O(1/N) saddle-gap and feasibility claims. The functional G is not defined precisely enough to determine whether the stated bound follows under the listed baseline ADMM assumptions.

children.title: Nonergodic ADMM Rates
children.top_down_role: Rate guarantees attached to individual iterates, residuals, or best-iterate quantities.

assumptions_latex: The ADMM iteration admits an averaged fixed-point representation \(w^{k+1}=Tw^k\) on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.
\(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\), and the fixed penalty and relaxation parameters lie in a convergent regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{0\leq k<N}\|r^k\|=O(N^{-1/2})\), and under residual monotonicity \(\|r^k\|=o(k^{-1/2})\).

notation.meaning: fixed-point state associated with ADMM or its Douglas-Rachford representation

review_flags: A precise source is needed for the little-o last-iterate statement and its residual-monotonicity hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual rates for unaveraged ADMM fixed-point iterates, not objective values of their averages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Averagedness and existence of a fixed point imply asymptotic regularity and square summability, \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|r^k\|^2<\infty.\] Consequently, among the first \(N\) iterates, \[\min_{0\leq k<N}\|r^k\|\leq \frac{C}{\sqrt N}\] for some \(C<\infty\). If the fixed-point residual norms are nonincreasing, as in the standard firmly nonexpansive representation, square summability further yields \(\|r^k\|=o(k^{-1/2})\). These bounds concern the actual iteration residual; they do not by themselves give an \(O(1/k)\) last-iterate objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without averaging, ADMM generally guarantees a best residual of order one over square-root iterations; a monotone residual is little-o of that rate.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonergodic ADMM Rates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the leaf, but the square-summability, best-iterate rate, residual monotonicity, and little-o last-iterate rate require a specific averaged-operator or ADMM theorem with locator.

children.title: Averaging-to-Iterate Rate Gap
children.top_down_role: Distinctions between guarantees for averaged outputs and guarantees for actual iteration sequences.

assumptions_latex: Only convexity, saddle-point existence, and the standard averaged-operator properties of two-block ADMM are assumed.
No strong convexity, error bound, metric subregularity, or spectral contraction is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An \(O(N^{-1})\) ergodic certificate does not imply an \(O(k^{-1})\) certificate for the last iterate.

notation.meaning: Cesaro average of the first N iterates

review_flags: A source giving a sharp ADMM example or lower bound for the averaging-to-iterate gap is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical separation between averaged and last-iterate guarantees in baseline convex ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The estimate \(R(\bar w^N)\leq C/N\) controls the Cesaro average \(\bar w^N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^Nw^k\), not any particular \(w^k\). Convexity permits cancellation in the averaged variational inequality, whereas the fixed-point energy estimate generally supplies only \(\sum_k\|w^{k+1}-w^k\|^2<\infty\). Therefore one cannot infer \(R(w^N)=O(N^{-1})\) from the ergodic bound alone. A comparable last-iterate rate requires additional structure, such as strong curvature and smoothness, an error bound, metric subregularity, or a strict spectral contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-one-over-N bound for averaged ADMM iterates does not transfer to the last iterate unless additional regularity creates a contraction or error bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Averaging-to-Iterate Rate Gap

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but the claimed nonimplication requires a cited counterexample, lower bound, or theorem establishing that baseline convex ADMM does not generally inherit the ergodic O(1/N) rate at its last iterate.

children.title: Strong-Curvature Regime
children.top_down_role: Linear-convergence coverage associated with strong convexity or positive curvature on relevant subspaces.

assumptions_latex: The quadratic block objective is \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), with symmetric \(Q\).
The relevant feasible or coupling subspace is \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) has curvature modulus \(\mu\) on \(S\), providing the lower spectral bound used in linear-rate estimates.
review_flags: The exact ADMM rank and subspace hypotheses connecting restricted curvature to contraction need a dedicated source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted strong curvature for a convex QP block participating in ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The strong-curvature regime holds when there is \(\mu>0\) such that \[d^{\mathsf T}Qd\geq \mu\|d\|^2\qquad\text{for every }d\in S.\] Equivalently, the smallest eigenvalue of the restriction \(Q|_S\) is at least \(\mu\). Hence for all \(x\) and all \(d\in S\), \[f(x+d)\geq f(x)+\langle Qx+q,d\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\|d\|^2.\] For \(S=\mathbb R^n\), this reduces to \(Q\succeq\mu I\). In ADMM rate analysis, the subspace must contain all primal displacements left unconstrained by the coupling equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A QP block is in the strong-curvature regime when its Hessian has a positive lower eigenvalue on every displacement relevant to the ADMM coupling.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Curvature Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restricted-curvature formulas are standard and the condition role fits. However, the final ADMM-specific displacement-subspace assertion lacks precise coupling/rank hypotheses and an inspectable source.

children.title: Smoothness Regime
children.top_down_role: Linear-convergence coverage associated with Lipschitz gradient or bounded quadratic curvature.

assumptions_latex: The quadratic block objective is \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
Norms are Euclidean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f\) is globally \(L\)-Lipschitz, with the least such constant \(L=\lambda_{\max}(Q)\).
review_flags: The elementary quadratic identity is standard, but a source locator specific to smooth convex quadratics was not supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global Euclidean smoothness of a convex quadratic ADMM block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because \(
abla f(x)=Qx+q\), for every \(x,y\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|=\|Q(x-y)\|\leq L\|x-y\|\] with \(L=\|Q\|_2=\lambda_{\max}(Q)\). Equivalently, \[f(y)\leq f(x)+\langle
abla f(x),y-xangle+ rac{L}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\] Thus every finite-dimensional convex quadratic has a Lipschitz gradient; unlike strong curvature, this upper spectral bound may hold when \(Q\) is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic is smooth with gradient Lipschitz constant equal to the largest eigenvalue of its Hessian, even when the Hessian is singular.
knowledge_statements.title: Smoothness Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic smoothness statement is mathematically standard and the property role is suitable, but no source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Curvature-Smoothness Conditioning
children.top_down_role: How the balance between lower curvature and upper smoothness affects linear-rate quality.

assumptions_latex: On a subspace \(S\), the quadratic Hessian satisfies \(\mu I_S\preceq Q|_S\preceq LI_S\) for finite \(0<\mu\leq L\).
The ADMM splitting and constraint maps satisfy the rank conditions needed to transfer these bounds to its fixed-point metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relevant curvature condition number is \(\kappa_S=L/\mu\), and linear-rate factors deteriorate as \(\kappa_S\) grows.
review_flags: No supplied source specifies an ADMM contraction factor for this conditioning regime; the claim is intentionally qualitative.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning parameter formed from restricted lower and upper quadratic curvature bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The two-sided spectral inequality \[\mu\|d\|^2\leq d^{\mathsf T}Qd\leq L\|d\|^2\qquad(d\in S)\] defines the restricted condition number \(\kappa_S=L/\mu\). After scaling, ADMM linear-rate estimates depend on this ratio together with singular values of the constraint maps and the penalty-induced metric. Small \(\kappa_S\) means comparable curvature in all relevant directions; large \(\kappa_S\) produces an anisotropic fixed-point map and a contraction factor closer to one. The numerical rate is therefore not determined by \(Q\) alone, but by curvature, coupling, penalty, and metric jointly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ratio of largest to smallest relevant quadratic curvature measures conditioning, but the actual ADMM rate also depends on constraints, penalty, and metric.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Smoothness Conditioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restricted condition number is well defined, but the claim that larger kappa_S produces an ADMM contraction factor closer to one is not universal without fixing the splitting, constraint maps, metric, and tuning rule. A precise sourced theorem is required.

assumptions_latex: The ADMM fixed-point operator \(T\) is averaged and has nonempty fixed-point set \(F\).
On a neighborhood \(U\) containing the tail of the iterates, \(\operatorname{dist}(w,F)\leq\kappa\|w-Tw\|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The distance to \(F\) decreases Q-linearly and the iterates converge R-linearly.
review_flags: A precise polyhedral multifunction theorem and the resulting contraction constant require source support.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local linear convergence induced by a polyhedral residual error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the QP objectives and constraints make the ADMM residual mapping \(R=I-T\) polyhedral, then near any solution component it admits a local error bound \[\operatorname{dist}(w,F)\leq\kappa\|R(w)\|.\] Combining this bound with the descent inequality for an averaged operator gives a constant \(q\in[0,1)\) such that, once \(w^k\in U\), \[\operatorname{dist}(w^{k+1},F)\leq q\operatorname{dist}(w^k,F).\] Hence solution-set distance is Q-linear; asymptotic regularity and Fejer monotonicity then give R-linear convergence of \(w^k\) to a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the QP ADMM residual is polyhedral, its local error bound combines with averaged-operator descent to yield local linear convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Error-Bound Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the regime, but no source establishes that the stated QP residual mapping is polyhedral, supplies the local error bound, or justifies the asserted Q-linear and R-linear consequences under the exact hypotheses.

assumptions_latex: The ADMM fixed-point mapping \(T\) is averaged, and \(F=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
The residual \(R=I-T\) is metrically subregular at \((w^\star,0)\) for every relevant cluster point \(w^\star\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Metric subregularity converts residual decrease into local Q-linear decrease of \(\operatorname{dist}(w^k,F)\).
review_flags: A source is needed for the exact averagedness parameter and contraction factor in the metric-subregularity theorem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-theoretic local linear convergence under metric subregularity of the ADMM residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Metric subregularity at \((w^\star,0)\) means that some neighborhood \(U\) of \(w^\star\) and \(\kappa<\infty\) satisfy \[\operatorname{dist}(w,F)\leq\kappa\|R(w)\|\qquad(w\in U).\] If averagedness supplies \(\operatorname{dist}(Tw,F)^2\leq\operatorname{dist}(w,F)^2-c\|R(w)\|^2\) with \(c>0\), then within \(U\), \[\operatorname{dist}(Tw,F)^2\leq\left(1-\frac{c}{\kappa^2}\right)\operatorname{dist}(w,F)^2.\] Whenever the displayed coefficient is nonnegative, this is a strict local contraction in solution-set distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity bounds distance to the ADMM fixed-point set by the residual, turning averaged-operator descent into a local linear contraction.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Subregularity Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The metric-subregularity condition and contraction calculation are plausible, but the averagedness constant, neighborhood invariance, and precise local linear-convergence theorem are not sourced.

assumptions_latex: After elimination or active-set stabilization, the ADMM state satisfies an affine recurrence \(w^{k+1}=Mw^k+b\).
A fixed point \(w^\star\) exists, and eigenvalue \(1\) directions represent only motion within the fixed-point set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Transverse linear convergence holds exactly when the spectral radius of the induced error map is less than one.

notation.meaning: error relative to a fixed point
spectral radius on the transverse error space

review_flags: A QP-specific derivation of the iteration matrix and treatment of nonnormal Jordan blocks require a source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral characterization after ADMM becomes an affine stationary iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Subtracting \(w^\star=Mw^\star+b\) gives \(e^{k+1}=Me^k\) and hence \(e^k=M^ke^0\). Let \(M_\perp\) be the induced map on a complementary space to fixed-point directions. If \(\rho(M_\perp)<1\), then for every \(q\in(\rho(M_\perp),1)\) there is \(C_q<\infty\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(w^k,F)\leq C_qq^k\operatorname{dist}(w^0,F).\] Conversely, an eigenvalue of \(M_\perp\) with modulus at least one prevents uniform linear decay of all transverse errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once QP ADMM is affine, its asymptotic rate is governed by the spectral radius of the iteration matrix away from fixed-point directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Linear-Iteration Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits, but a complementary space need not be M-invariant, so M_perp must be defined on an invariant complement or quotient. A source is also needed for the QP-specific affine reduction and spectral characterization.

assumptions_latex: The nonsmooth terms are partly smooth relative to active manifolds at a primal-dual solution.
A nondegeneracy condition holds, and the ADMM iterates converge to that solution.
The derivative of the identified local fixed-point map is strictly contractive transverse to its fixed-point manifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active manifolds are identified finitely, after which ADMM converges locally linearly.

notation.meaning: active manifolds of the two primal blocks
derivative of the local fixed-point map at the limit

review_flags: The precise partial-smoothness, nondegeneracy, and spectral hypotheses vary by theorem and need an authoritative source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite activity identification followed by a smooth or affine local ADMM model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists \(K<\infty\) such that for all \(k\geq K\), the primal iterates lie on the active manifolds: \[x^k\in\mathcal M_f,
\qquad z^k\in\mathcal M_g.\] After identification, the proximal mappings restrict to smooth mappings on these manifolds, so the ADMM state has the local expansion \[w^{k+1}-w^\star=DT(w^\star)(w^k-w^\star)+o(\|w^k-w^\star\|).\] If the derivative has transverse spectral radius below one, then for some \(q<1\) and \(C<\infty\), \(\operatorname{dist}(w^k,F)\leq Cq^{k-K}\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under partial smoothness and nondegeneracy, ADMM identifies the active manifolds finitely; a contractive local linearization then gives local linear convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Identified Active-Manifold Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is appropriately presented as a theorem, but partial smoothness, nondegeneracy, identification, differentiability, and transverse contraction have theorem-specific formulations. Without an authoritative citation, the hypotheses and conclusion cannot be validated.

assumptions_latex: Two-block ADMM is applied to \(\min\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\}\) with exact subproblem solutions.
The penalty \(\rho>0\) and any weighting metric remain constant throughout the iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method is a stationary fixed-point iteration whose convergence and asymptotic rate are governed by one fixed penalty-induced metric.
review_flags: A standard ADMM algorithm citation and convergence theorem locator were not supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical scaled two-block ADMM with one positive penalty used at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\rho>0\) and initialize \((z^0,u^0)\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \[x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2,\] \[z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_z g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2,\qquad u^{k+1}=u^k+r^{k+1}.\] Stop when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances are met, and return \((x^{k+1},z^{k+1},\rho u^{k+1})\). Because \(\rho\) is fixed, the associated Douglas-Rachford or fixed-point operator is stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-penalty ADMM repeatedly solves both proximal subproblems and updates the scaled dual variable using one unchanged positive penalty.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Penalty Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role is defensible for this parameter regime, and the displayed scaled ADMM updates are standard. Nevertheless, the dual stopping residual is not defined, and no located source supports the stationary-operator and convergence claims.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), both ADMM subproblems use the same penalty \(\rho_k>0\).
Penalty changes are bounded, preserve positive lower and upper bounds, and satisfy conditions ensuring the resulting variable-metric iteration remains convergent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adaptive penalties define a nonstationary ADMM iteration; convergence requires explicit control of metric variation, not merely positivity of each \(\rho_k\).

notation.meaning: primal and dual residuals used by the update rule

review_flags: Residual balancing is heuristic without additional safeguards; a source is required for a precise convergent variable-penalty theorem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-driven penalty adaptation with safeguards for variable-metric convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run the two ADMM primal updates with \(\rho_k\), form primal and dual residuals \(r^{k+1}\) and \(s^{k+1}\), and set \[\rho_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\gamma\rho_k,&\|r^{k+1}\|>\tau\|s^{k+1}\|,\\ \rho_k/\gamma,&\|s^{k+1}\|>\tau\|r^{k+1}\|,\\ \rho_k,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\] followed by projection onto a prescribed interval \([\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\). Rescale the scaled dual variable so the unscaled multiplier is unchanged when \(\rho_k\) changes. Stop at joint residual tolerances. For a convergence guarantee, additionally require controlled metric variation, such as summable relative penalty changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive ADMM changes its penalty using primal-dual residual imbalance, rescales the dual state, and needs bounded, controlled variation for convergence guarantees.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Penalty Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but r and s are not defined, the dual rescaling must be stated explicitly, and bounded projected residual balancing alone does not establish convergence. A precise variable-penalty theorem with controlled-variation hypotheses is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Parameter Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard over-relaxed ADMM regime for a closed proper convex two-block splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), with a saddle point and exactly solved ADMM subproblems. Replace the new affine image in the second-block and multiplier updates by \(\alpha Ax^{k+1}+(1-\alpha)(c-Bz^k)\). The standard convergence regime is \[0<\alpha<2.\] At \(\alpha=1\) the ordinary ADMM iteration is recovered. Values \(\alpha\notin(0,2)\) are outside the general averaged-operator guarantee and may produce divergence even for convex quadratic instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over-relaxed convex ADMM has its standard convergence guarantee for relaxation strictly between zero and two; one gives ordinary ADMM.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are closed, proper, and convex.
The constraint system admits a primal-dual saddle point.
Both ADMM subproblems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0<\alpha<2\) is the standard relaxation-parameter regime.
review_flags: No relevant ADMM source was supplied for the exact relaxation convention and endpoint exclusions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but no source verifies this relaxation convention, the endpoint exclusions, or the claimed quadratic divergence outside the interval.

children.title: ADMM Metric Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of scalar, diagonal, or structured metrics for ADMM QP subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: ADMM Metric Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection rule for a positive-definite residual metric in finite-dimensional ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For residual \(r=Ax+Bz-c\), replace the scalar quadratic penalty by \(\tfrac{\rho}{2}\lVert r\rVert_M^2\), where \(\lVert r\rVert_M^2=r^\top Mr\) and \(M\succ0\). Choose \(M\) so that \[mI\preceq M\preceq LI\qquad(0<m\le L<\infty),\] while reducing the condition numbers of the resulting primal linear systems and scaled constraint operators. Uniform spectral bounds preserve equivalence with the Euclidean residual norm; singular or extremely ill-conditioned choices can destroy this equivalence or make subproblem solves unstable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a uniformly positive-definite residual metric that improves the scaled linear systems without losing norm equivalence or numerical stability.
assumptions_latex: The ADMM residual lies in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
The chosen metric is symmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A suitable metric satisfies \(mI\preceq M\preceq LI\) and improves relevant spectral conditioning.
review_flags: The supplied metric-method locator is unrelated to ADMM residual metrics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits metric selection, but no relevant source supports the proposed ADMM metric rule or its numerical-stability claims.

children.title: ADMM Spectral Tuning
children.top_down_role: Parameter selection informed by spectral characteristics of the QP splitting.

knowledge_statements.title: ADMM Spectral Tuning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Offline tuning for a linear ADMM iteration arising from a quadratic problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the error iteration for fixed metric \(M\), penalty \(\rho>0\), and relaxation \(\alpha\in(0,2)\) be \(e^{k+1}=T(M,\rho,\alpha)e^k\). Given compact search sets \(R\subset(0,\infty)\) and \(D\subset(0,2)\), estimate the nontrivial spectral radius \(\widehat\varrho(T)\) at candidate pairs and select \[(\rho_*,\alpha_*)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(\rho,\alpha)\in R\times D}\widehat\varrho\bigl(T(M,\rho,\alpha)\bigr).\] Run ADMM with the selected pair and stop when prescribed primal- and dual-residual tolerances hold. Modes fixed by solution nonuniqueness are excluded from the radius estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate the linear ADMM iteration spectrum over admissible penalty and relaxation values, then choose the pair with the smallest nontrivial spectral radius.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic ADMM iteration is affine with a well-defined error matrix.
The tuning domains are compact and exclude inadmissible endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is \((\rho_*,\alpha_*)\) minimizing the estimated asymptotic contraction factor.
review_flags: A source is needed for the selected spectral-tuning formulation and treatment of invariant modes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the spectral-radius estimator, exclusion of invariant modes, and existence of the stated minimizer require a formulation-specific source and hypotheses.

children.title: Metric-Induced Spectral Conditioning
children.top_down_role: How metric choices reshape the spectrum relevant to ADMM behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Induced Spectral Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Congruence-based conditioning effect of a positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\succ0\) be the quadratic operator governing an ADMM subproblem or reduced linear mode, and let \(M\succ0\) define the computational metric. In metric coordinates, the relevant operator is \(\widetilde H=M^{-1/2}HM^{-1/2}\), with spectral condition number \[\kappa_M(H)=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(M^{-1/2}HM^{-1/2})}{\lambda_{\min}(M^{-1/2}HM^{-1/2})}.\] Thus metric selection changes the spectrum by congruence. If \(aM\preceq H\preceq bM\) for \(0<a\le b\), then \(\kappa_M(H)\le b/a\); the idealized choice \(M=H\) gives condition number one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A metric preconditions the quadratic operator by congruence; spectral equivalence between the metric and operator bounds the resulting condition number.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(M\) are symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(aM\preceq H\preceq bM\) implies \(\kappa_M(H)\le b/a\).
review_flags: The linear-algebra claim is standard, but no relevant source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The congruence-conditioning statement is mathematically standard and fits the property leaf, but no inspectable source locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Controlled Inner-Solve Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summable-error regime for inexact convex ADMM subproblem solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_*^{k+1}\) and \(z_*^{k+1}\) denote the exact ADMM subproblem minimizers, and let the computed iterates satisfy \[\lVert x^{k+1}-x_*^{k+1}\rVert\le\varepsilon_k^x,\qquad \lVert z^{k+1}-z_*^{k+1}\rVert\le\varepsilon_k^z.\] A standard controlled-error regime requires \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(\varepsilon_k^x+\varepsilon_k^z)<\infty.\] Under the ordinary convex ADMM solvability hypotheses, this makes the cumulative perturbation finite and preserves convergence to a primal-dual solution. Merely requiring bounded, nonvanishing errors does not generally imply exact convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact ADMM retains its standard convergence behavior when the distances from exact subproblem solutions form a summable sequence.
assumptions_latex: The exact convex ADMM iteration has a primal-dual solution.
Subproblem errors are measured in fixed finite-dimensional norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Summability of \(\varepsilon_k^x+\varepsilon_k^z\) preserves convergence to a solution.
review_flags: A precise inexact-ADMM theorem source is required for this distance-error criterion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but convergence from summable distances to selected exact minimizers depends on precise inexact-ADMM hypotheses, including possible nonuniqueness, that are not sourced.

children.title: Changing-Metric ADMM Regimes
children.top_down_role: ADMM behavior under iteration-dependent proximal or scaling metrics.

knowledge_statements.title: Changing-Metric ADMM Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformly coercive, summably varying metric regime for variable-metric ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k\succ0\) be the residual or proximal metric at iteration \(k\). A controlled changing-metric regime is specified by constants \(0<m\le L<\infty\) and a nonnegative summable sequence \((\eta_k)\) such that \[mI\preceq M_k\preceq LI,\qquad M_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)M_k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty.\] These conditions prevent metric degeneracy and ensure finite accumulated relative expansion. With compatible convex ADMM hypotheses, they form a standard sufficient regime for quasi-Fejér convergence analyses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing ADMM metrics should remain uniformly positive definite and bounded, with summable relative variation.
assumptions_latex: Every \(M_k\) is symmetric.
The underlying fixed-metric convex splitting admits a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform spectral bounds and summable relative metric change define a controlled variable-metric regime.
review_flags: Exact variable-metric ADMM hypotheses differ by formulation; no relevant source was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated regime is plausible and correctly typed as a condition, but its sufficiency for the intended ADMM formulation is source-dependent and unsupported.

children.title: Changing-Penalty ADMM Regimes
children.top_down_role: ADMM behavior under iteration-dependent penalty parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Changing-Penalty ADMM Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded, summably varying scalar-penalty regime for convex ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_k>0\) be the ADMM penalty at iteration \(k\). A controlled changing-penalty regime requires constants \(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_{\max}<\infty\) and finite cumulative multiplicative variation, for example \[\rho_{\min}\le\rho_k\le\rho_{\max},\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\left|\log\frac{\rho_{k+1}}{\rho_k}\right|<\infty.\] Consequently \((\rho_k)\) converges to a positive finite limit and cannot oscillate indefinitely by fixed factors. Together with the corresponding variable-metric ADMM convergence hypotheses, this controls the perturbation caused by penalty adaptation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safe variable-penalty regime keeps penalties positive and bounded while making their cumulative multiplicative change finite.
assumptions_latex: Each penalty \(\rho_k\) is strictly positive.
The ADMM multiplier is rescaled consistently when \(\rho_k\) changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Boundedness and summable logarithmic variation imply \(\rho_k\to\rho_\infty\in(0,\infty)\).
review_flags: A variable-penalty ADMM source is needed to connect this sufficient variation condition to a specific convergence theorem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Summable logarithmic variation does imply convergence of the positive penalty sequence, but its connection to ADMM convergence requires a specific sourced theorem.

children.title: Joint Parameter-Variation Control
children.top_down_role: Compatibility requirements when metric variation and penalty variation occur together.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Parameter-Variation Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified finite-variation condition for simultaneous metric, penalty, and relaxation updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iteration parameters \(M_k\succ0\), \(\rho_k>0\), and \(\alpha_k\in(0,2)\), impose uniform bounds \[mI\preceq M_k\preceq LI,\quad \rho_k\in[\rho_-,\rho_+],\quad \alpha_k\in[\alpha_-,\alpha_+]\subset(0,2),\] and joint finite variation \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\left(\lVert M_{k+1}-M_k\rVert+|\log(\rho_{k+1}/\rho_k)|+|\alpha_{k+1}-\alpha_k|\right)<\infty.\] Then all three sequences converge to admissible limits, and their cumulative change can be treated as a summable perturbation in a compatible variable-parameter ADMM analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous metric, penalty, and relaxation updates are controlled by uniform admissibility bounds and summable total variation.
assumptions_latex: All matrices act on one fixed finite-dimensional space.
The norm on metric differences is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parameter sequences converge to admissible limits and have finite cumulative variation.
review_flags: The joint condition is mathematically sufficient for parameter convergence, but its ADMM convergence consequence needs formulation-specific sourcing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-variation conditions imply parameter convergence, but treating all changes as a summable ADMM perturbation is formulation-specific and has no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between vanishing or summable perturbations and persistent numerical error in a uniformly contractive fixed-point model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Model a computed ADMM fixed-point iteration as \(w^{k+1}=F_k(w^k)+e_k\), where every exact map has the common fixed point \(F_k(w^*)=w^*\) and satisfies \(\lVert F_k(u)-F_k(v)\rVert\le q\lVert u-v\rVert\) for all \(u,v\), with \(0\le q<1\). If \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert e_k\rVert<\infty\), then \(w^k\to w^*\). If only \(\lVert e_k\rVert\le\epsilon\), then \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert w^k-w^*\rVert\le\frac{\epsilon}{1-q},\] while exact convergence need not occur. Thus persistent finite-precision perturbations can produce an accuracy floor amplified by weak contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For exact maps sharing one uniformly contractive fixed point, summable perturbations permit convergence to that fixed point, whereas persistent bounded perturbations can leave an error floor of epsilon divided by one minus the contraction factor.
assumptions_latex: \(F_k(w^*)=w^*\) for every \(k\).
\(\lVert F_k(u)-F_k(v)\rVert\le q\lVert u-v\rVert\) in one common norm, where \(0\le q<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\lVert e_k\rVert\le\epsilon\), then \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert w^k-w^*\rVert\le\epsilon/(1-q)\), and exact convergence is not guaranteed.

notation.meaning: exact iteration map at step k

review_flags: A source connecting the uniformly contractive perturbation model specifically to finite-precision ADMM is required.

children.title: Inconsistent QP Behavior
children.top_down_role: Splitting behavior when the QP constraint system has no feasible point.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent QP Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate for infeasibility of box-constrained linear QP constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex QP constraints \(l\le Ax\le u\), allowing infinite one-sided bounds. If there exists \(y\ne0\) such that \[A^\top y=0,\qquad u^\top y_+ + l^\top y_-<0,\] with terms involving infinite bounds required to have zero corresponding coefficients, then the constraint system is inconsistent. Indeed, the displayed vector is a directly checkable primal-infeasibility certificate. Consequently no ADMM sequence can converge to a primal feasible QP solution, although algorithm-dependent normalized difference sequences may converge toward such a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero dual vector annihilating the constraint matrix and strictly separating the interval bounds certifies that the QP constraints are inconsistent.
assumptions_latex: \(l_i\le u_i\) for every component.
Infinite-bound products are interpreted only when the associated signed coefficient is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed \(y\) certifies \(\{x:l\le Ax\le u\}=\varnothing\).
review_flags: A precise alternative theorem and an ADMM-specific certificate-convergence source are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the leaf and the sign convention is plausible, but an authoritative alternative-theorem locator and support for the ADMM difference-sequence claim are absent.

children.title: Unbounded QP Behavior
children.top_down_role: Splitting behavior when feasible recession permits objective decrease without a finite optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded QP Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession-direction certificate for a convex QP with interval constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x \tfrac12x^\top Px+q^\top x\) subject to \(l\le Ax\le u\), assume \(P\succeq0\) and the feasible set is nonempty. A vector \(d\ne0\) certifies unboundedness below when \[Pd=0,\qquad q^\top d<0,\qquad d\in\operatorname{rec}\{x:l\le Ax\le u\}.\] Equivalently, \((Ad)_i=0\) for two-sided finite bounds, \((Ad)_i\le0\) for upper-only bounds, and \((Ad)_i\ge0\) for lower-only bounds. For any feasible \(x\), the ray \(x+td\) remains feasible and its objective tends to \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible recession direction in the quadratic nullspace with negative linear cost certifies that a convex QP is unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.
The interval-constrained feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed direction implies \(\inf\{\tfrac12x^\top Px+q^\top x:l\le Ax\le u\}=-\infty\).

notation.meaning: recession cone of the feasible set

review_flags: No supplied locator supports the convex-QP recession certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate fits the leaf and is mathematically plausible for a feasible convex interval-constrained QP, but no source supports the exact recession characterization.

children.title: Infeasibility-Unboundedness Distinction
children.top_down_role: Observable and certificate-level distinctions between inconsistency and unboundedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility-Unboundedness Distinction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between empty feasibility and objective recession in convex interval-constrained QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex QP \(\min\{\tfrac12x^\top Px+q^\top x:l\le Ax\le u\}\) with \(P\succeq0\), primal infeasibility is certified by a separator \(y\ne0\) satisfying \[A^\top y=0,\qquad u^\top y_+ + l^\top y_-<0.\] Unboundedness below instead requires a nonempty feasible set and is certified by a recession direction \(d\ne0\) satisfying \[Pd=0,\qquad q^\top d<0,\qquad d\in\operatorname{rec}\{x:l\le Ax\le u\}.\] The first certificate concerns inconsistency of the constraints; the second concerns objective decrease along feasible rays, so the two failure modes are distinct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infeasibility uses a separating vector for an empty constraint set, whereas unboundedness uses a decreasing recession direction from a nonempty feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.
Infinite-bound terms use the signed-support convention under which their corresponding incompatible signed coefficients vanish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The separator \(y\) and recession direction \(d\) describe distinct QP failure boundaries.

notation.meaning: recession cone of a set C

review_flags: An authoritative source with specific locators for both interval-constraint certificates is required.

assumptions_latex: The problem has three variable blocks and a linear coupling constraint.
Each block objective is closed, proper, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convergence of the direct three-block Gauss--Seidel ADMM extension is not guaranteed without additional structural assumptions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct Gauss--Seidel extension of two-block ADMM to three convex blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x_1,x_2,x_3}\sum_{i=1}^3 f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(A_1x_1+A_2x_2+A_3x_3=b\). The naive multi-block ADMM successively minimizes the augmented Lagrangian over \(x_1,x_2,x_3\), using newly updated preceding blocks, and then updates the multiplier with penalty \(\rho>0\). There exist finite-dimensional instances with quadratic convex \(f_i\), a feasible constraint, and an attained solution for which the resulting linear iteration has spectral radius greater than one. Consequently, the iterates and residuals can diverge. Two-block ADMM convergence theory therefore does not extend to this scheme without conditions such as sufficient block strong convexity, proximal regularization, or a convergent regrouping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct cyclic three-block ADMM can diverge on a feasible convex quadratic problem; two-block convergence does not automatically extend without added structure or regularization.
knowledge_statements.title: Naive Multi-Block ADMM Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and mathematical claim are appropriate, but the asserted finite-dimensional convex quadratic divergence example and spectral-radius conclusion require a specific inspectable source.

assumptions_latex: The QP objective is \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\), with symmetric \(P\).
The splitting uses an unconstrained quadratic \(x\)-update with penalty \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Negative curvature can invalidate both convex convergence theory and well-posedness of the ADMM subproblem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between convex QPs and indefinite nonconvex QPs for standard ADMM analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the QP \(\min_x \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to splitting constraints involving \(Ax\), the standard convex ADMM guarantee requires \(P\succeq0\). If \(P\not\succeq0\), the objective is nonconvex and its subdifferential is not monotone. Moreover, an unconstrained ADMM \(x\)-subproblem has Hessian \(H_\rho=P+\rho A^{\mathsf T}A\). If \(H_\rho\) has a negative eigenvalue, that subproblem is unbounded below, so the ADMM step is undefined. Even when \(H_\rho\succeq0\), convex ADMM convergence conclusions do not follow merely from solvability of each update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indefinite QP lies outside convex ADMM theory; if the augmented x-update retains negative curvature, the subproblem is unbounded and the iteration is undefined.
knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite-QP Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The negative-curvature calculation is coherent and fits the failure-boundary container, but no source supports the claimed boundary of standard ADMM theory or the nonconvex update conclusions.

children.title: Poorly Scaled QP Regimes
children.top_down_role: QP instances with disparate coefficient, variable, or constraint scales.

assumptions_latex: A linear system \(Kz=d\) is solved during each first-order QP iteration.
A norm and a threshold \(\kappa_{\max}>1\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is poorly scaled when the effective linear system exceeds the prescribed conditioning threshold.

notation.meaning: Condition number in the selected norm.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational conditioning criterion for linear algebra inside a first-order QP solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(K\) is nonsingular and define \(\kappa(K)=\|K\|\,\|K^{-1}\|\). Relative to a fixed solver, norm, arithmetic precision, and threshold \(\kappa_{\max}\), a QP instance is in a poorly scaled regime when \(\kappa(K)>\kappa_{\max}\) for the system actually used by the iteration. If \(K\) is singular, set \(\kappa(K)=+\infty\). This definition concerns the implemented formulation: diagonal row or variable scaling can change \(K\) and hence can move the same mathematical QP into or out of the regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A QP is operationally poorly scaled when the linear system used by its solver is singular or exceeds a specified condition-number threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Poorly Scaled QP Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent operational condition, but the condition-number threshold is solver- and policy-dependent and has no cited source establishing it as the intended meaning of this leaf.

children.title: Residual Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Solver regimes in which residual improvement slows or stops above requested tolerances.

assumptions_latex: A nonnegative residual sequence \((R_k)\) and window length \(m\ge1\) are fixed.
A required contraction factor \(\eta\in(0,1)\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stagnation at iteration \(k\) is the failure of the residual to contract by \(\eta\) over the preceding window.

notation.meaning: Aggregate optimality residual at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window operational definition, distinct from asymptotic nonconvergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_k\ge0\) be an aggregate residual, for example the maximum of normalized primal and dual residuals. For \(k\ge m\), residual stagnation over the window ending at \(k\) occurs when \(R_k>\eta R_{k-m}\), where \(m\ge1\) and \(\eta\in(0,1)\) specify the monitoring policy. Persistent stagnation means that this inequality holds for every endpoint in a prescribed sequence of consecutive windows while \(R_k\) remains above the termination tolerance. This predicate diagnoses inadequate observed progress; it does not by itself establish divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residuals stagnate when they fail to achieve a prescribed contraction over a fixed window while remaining above the stopping tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Stagnation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-window predicate is precise and correctly distinguished from divergence, but its parameters define a local monitoring policy for which no supporting source is supplied.

children.title: Scaling-Induced Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms by which poor scaling contributes to imbalanced or stalled residual progress.

assumptions_latex: The original and diagonally scaled formulations represent the same QP.
Stopping and penalty-update decisions are computed from formulation-dependent residual norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Non-invariant residual tests can make scaling alone produce an observed stagnation regime.

notation.meaning: Positive diagonal row and variable scalings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observed stagnation caused by formulation-dependent residual magnitudes or penalty adaptation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the change of variables \(x=D\bar x\) and row scaling by a positive diagonal \(E\), the corresponding residuals satisfy \(\bar r_p=Er_p\) and \(\bar r_d=D^{\mathsf T}r_d\). Hence raw residual norms and their ratio are generally not invariant. If a solver applies unchanged absolute tolerances or updates \(\rho\) from \(\|\bar r_p\|/\|\bar r_d\|\), sufficiently unbalanced \(D\) or \(E\) can trigger different penalty sequences and fail the finite-window contraction test although the represented QP is unchanged. This mechanism is scaling-induced stagnation; invariantly rescaled tests exclude this particular cause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal reformulation can distort raw residuals and penalty updates enough to trigger stagnation, even though the underlying QP is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Induced Stagnation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate-scaling formulas are plausible, but the stronger claim that scaling can alter penalty sequences and cause the specified stagnation behavior requires solver-specific evidence.

children.title: QP Residual-Certificate-Termination System
children.top_down_role: Approximate optimality evidence is separated from infeasibility evidence and from operational stopping policy.

assumptions_latex: The QP constraints are \(l\le Ax\le u\), componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal feasibility is equivalent to \(r_p(x)=0\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the constraint box.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection residual for box-form linear constraints, including equality constraints when bounds coincide.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the componentwise constraints \(l\le Ax\le u\), define the primal feasibility residual by \[r_p(x)=Ax-\Pi_{[l,u]}(Ax).\] Equivalently, its components are \((r_p(x))_i=(Ax)_i-u_i\) when \((Ax)_i>u_i\), \((r_p(x))_i=(Ax)_i-l_i\) when \((Ax)_i<l_i\), and zero otherwise. Thus \(r_p(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\) is primal feasible. A scalar residual is obtained as \(\|r_p(x)\|\) in the solver's declared norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal residual is the displacement of Ax from its projection onto the bound box; it vanishes exactly at primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Feasibility Residual

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153
source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

assumptions_latex: The QP objective is \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\), with \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\).
The multiplier \(y\) corresponds to the linear image \(Ax\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stationarity holds exactly when \(r_d(x,y)=0\).

notation.meaning: Dual multiplier for the constraint image.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity residual for a differentiable box-constrained convex QP.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\) and Lagrangian coupling \(y^{\mathsf T}Ax\), define \[r_d(x,y)=Px+q+A^{\mathsf T}y.\] The vector \(r_d(x,y)\) is the dual stationarity residual. It vanishes exactly when the first-order stationarity equation for \(x\) holds. Its norm is meaningful as a stopping quantity only together with primal feasibility and the requirement that \(y\) satisfy the appropriate normal-cone or sign conditions for the bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual stationarity residual is Px+q+A-transpose y; its vanishing enforces the stationarity part of the QP KKT system.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Stationarity Residual

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153
source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

assumptions_latex: The constraint image \(z=Ax\) satisfies finite bounds \(l\le z\le u\).
The normal-cone convention makes upper-bound multipliers nonnegative and lower-bound multipliers nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bound complementarity and multiplier sign conditions hold exactly when \(r_c(z,y)=0\).

notation.meaning: Positive and negative parts of y.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise residual for two-sided finite bounds using a single signed multiplier.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible \(z\in[l,u]\), let \(y_+=\max(y,0)\) and \(y_-=\min(y,0)\), componentwise. Define \[r_c(z,y)=\begin{pmatrix}y_+\odot(u-z)\\(-y_-)\odot(z-l)\end{pmatrix}.\] Then \(r_c(z,y)=0\) precisely when every positive component of \(y\) is complementary to its upper-bound slack and every negative component is complementary to its lower-bound slack. Together with feasibility, this is equivalent to \(y\in N_{[l,u]}(z)\) under the stated normal-cone convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complementarity residual multiplies signed multiplier parts by their associated bound slacks and vanishes exactly under bound complementarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Residual

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153
source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

assumptions_latex: The primal QP is convex and has finite bounds \(l\le Ax\le u\).
The pair \((x,y)\) is primal and dual feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The gap is nonnegative and vanishes at a primal-dual optimum under strong duality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value gap for feasible primal and dual points of a convex QP.

source_refs.locator: 2.12.2 Saddle Point of a Function p. 75
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Global Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\) be the primal objective and let \(d(y)\) be the value of the corresponding Lagrange dual objective under the same multiplier-sign convention. For primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \(y\), define \[G(x,y)=p(x)-d(y).\] Weak duality gives \(G(x,y)\ge0\). If strong duality holds and both optima are attained, then \(G(x,y)=0\) if and only if \(x\) and \(y\) attain the primal and dual optimal values, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For feasible primal and dual points, the primal-dual gap is primal objective minus dual objective; it is nonnegative and is zero at optimality under strong duality.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Gap

source_witnesses.locator: 2.12.2 Saddle Point of a Function p. 75
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Global Optimization

assumptions_latex: A splitting iteration is represented by a map \(T:\mathcal W\to\mathcal W\).
Fixed points of \(T\) correspond to solutions of the encoded QP inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fixed-point residual vanishes exactly at an encoded solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact zero-residual semantics for a solver represented as a fixed-point iteration.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 Fixed Point and Equilibrium p. 91
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Global Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an iteration \(w^{k+1}=T(w^k)\), define the fixed-point residual by \[r_{\mathrm{fp}}(w)=w-T(w).\] Then \(r_{\mathrm{fp}}(w)=0\) if and only if \(w\in\operatorname{Fix}(T)\). When the splitting construction establishes \(\operatorname{Fix}(T)=S^{-1}(\mathcal Z_\star)\) for a recovery map \(S\) and QP solution set \(\mathcal Z_\star\), a zero fixed-point residual certifies that \(S(w)\) solves the encoded optimality inclusion. A small residual alone implies a small solution error only if an additional error bound is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual w minus T(w) vanishes exactly at a fixed point, which certifies a QP solution when the splitting map has the stated correspondence.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Residual Interpretation

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 Fixed Point and Equilibrium p. 91
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Global Optimization

assumptions_latex: The QP is convex, and the stated constraint qualification makes its KKT conditions sufficient.
Primal, stationarity, and complementarity residuals use consistent multiplier conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Simultaneous vanishing of the residual blocks is equivalent to KKT optimality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual decomposition of KKT conditions for a convex bound-form QP.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z=Ax\), form the stacked residual \[R_{\mathrm{KKT}}(x,z,y)=\begin{pmatrix}Ax-z\\Px+q+A^{\mathsf T}y\\r_c(z,y)\end{pmatrix},\] while separately requiring \(l\le z\le u\) and the multiplier sign convention encoded by \(r_c\). Then \(R_{\mathrm{KKT}}(x,z,y)=0\) is equivalent to primal consistency, stationarity, and bound complementarity. Under convexity and a constraint qualification ensuring KKT sufficiency, these conditions are equivalent to primal-dual optimality. Thus splitting residuals are KKT certificates only after their variables and signs are mapped to these blocks consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consistently mapped splitting residuals certify KKT optimality when their primal, stationarity, and complementarity blocks all vanish for a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Residual Interpretation
