children.title: Symbolic Factorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of ordering, elimination-tree, and fill-pattern analysis across related systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic Factorization Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse criterion for ordering, elimination tree, and factor-storage pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_1\) and \(K_2\) be symmetric matrices with identical structural sparsity patterns. If both use the same permutation and the same symbolic elimination rule determined only by that pattern, then they have the same elimination tree and symbolic factor pattern. Consequently, the ordering, elimination tree, and factor-storage allocation computed for \(K_1\) may be reused for \(K_2\). This conclusion excludes value-dependent pivoting that changes the pivot sequence or symbolic structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrices with the same structural pattern can share ordering, elimination-tree, and factor-storage analysis when the symbolic rule is pattern-determined; value-dependent pivoting can invalidate that reuse.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{pattern}(K_1)=\operatorname{pattern}(K_2)\).
The same permutation and pattern-determined symbolic elimination rule are used.
No value-dependent pivot decision changes the symbolic structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{pattern}(L_1)=\operatorname{pattern}(L_2).\]

notation.meaning: symbolic triangular factor for matrix i

children.title: Numeric Factorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of numeric factors when coefficient values or solver parameters remain compatible.

knowledge_statements.title: Numeric Factorization Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reuse of numerical factors across multiple right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a fixed nonsingular matrix \(K\) has numerical factorization \(\Pi K\Pi^{\mathsf T}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\). For every new right-hand side \(b_j\), the same numerical factors yield
\[x_j=\Pi^{\mathsf T}L^{-\mathsf T}D^{-1}L^{-1}\Pi b_j\]
without repeating numerical factorization. Exact numeric reuse therefore requires the coefficient matrix, permutation, scaling, and pivot sequence to remain unchanged. If any numerical entry of \(K\) changes, the old factors are not an exact factorization of the new matrix unless a separately validated factorization update is performed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unchanged coefficient matrix can use one numerical factorization for every right-hand side; changed coefficients require refactorization or a validated update.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{S}^{N}\) is nonsingular and identical for all solves.
Permutation, scaling, and pivot choices remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Kx_j=b_j\quad\text{using the same }(\Pi,L,D)\text{ for every }j.\]

children.title: Pattern-Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural changes that invalidate symbolic or numeric reuse.

knowledge_statements.title: Pattern-Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which previously computed symbolic factorization data cease to be guaranteed applicable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a permutation and a pattern-determined elimination rule, and let \(S_{\mathrm{ref}}\) be the symbolic factor-storage pattern computed from \(\operatorname{pattern}(K_{\mathrm{ref}})\). If
\[\operatorname{pattern}(K_{\mathrm{new}})\subseteq\operatorname{pattern}(K_{\mathrm{ref}}),\]
then symbolic elimination of \(K_{\mathrm{new}}\) under the same rule produces a factor pattern contained in \(S_{\mathrm{ref}}\), so the existing storage remains structurally safe. If the containment fails, reuse is not guaranteed and the symbolic pattern must be verified or recomputed. Independently, value-dependent pivoting can change the pivot sequence and factor pattern even when the input pattern is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An updated pattern contained in the analyzed reference pattern can safely use the existing symbolic storage under the same pattern-only rule. Outside that envelope reuse requires verification or reanalysis, and value-dependent pivoting can still break it.
assumptions_latex: A symbolic factor-storage pattern \(S_{\mathrm{ref}}\) was computed for \(K_{\mathrm{ref}}\) using a fixed permutation and pattern-determined elimination rule.
The stated containment guarantee excludes value-dependent changes to the pivot sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{pattern}(K_{\mathrm{new}})\subseteq\operatorname{pattern}(K_{\mathrm{ref}})\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{pattern}(L_{\mathrm{new}})\subseteq S_{\mathrm{ref}}.\]

notation.meaning: matrix pattern used for reference symbolic analysis

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Factorization Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Woodbury representation underlying low-rank modifications of QP system solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}\) be nonsingular and let \(U,V\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times r}\), \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\) be nonsingular. If \(C^{-1}+V^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}U\) is nonsingular, then the rank-at-most-\(r\) modification \(\widetilde K=K+UCV^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies
\[\widetilde K^{-1}=K^{-1}-K^{-1}U(C^{-1}+V^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}U)^{-1}V^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}.\]
Thus solves with \(\widetilde K\) can reuse solves with the factors of \(K\), together with an \(r\times r\) dense solve. Numerical stability still requires monitoring the small matrix and the accumulated updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank matrix change can reuse the original factors through the Woodbury formula and one small dense solve, subject to nonsingularity and stability checks.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) and \(C\) are nonsingular.
\(U,V\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times r}\).
\(C^{-1}+V^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}U\) is nonsingular.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Woodbury representation is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but no source is supplied for either the identity or the factor-update and stability interpretation.

children.title: Update Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditioning and fill regimes where updating loses reliability or efficiency.

knowledge_statements.title: Update Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic and numerical boundaries for low-rank modifications of a nonsingular factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonsingular \(K\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) and \(U,V\in\mathbb R^{N\times p}\), define \(K_+=K+UV^T\) and \(S=I_p+V^TK^{-1}U\). The updated matrix is nonsingular if and only if \(S\) is nonsingular, in which case
\[K_+^{-1}=K^{-1}-K^{-1}US^{-1}V^TK^{-1}.\]
Consequently, singularity of \(S\) is the exact algebraic failure boundary. In floating-point computation, a very small \(\sigma_{\min}(S)\), large triangular-solve backward errors, or loss of an intended inertia makes the modification numerically unsafe and calls for refactorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank update is algebraically valid exactly when its small correction matrix is nonsingular; near singularity or inertia loss marks a numerical refactorization boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is nonsingular.
\(U\) and \(V\) have the same number \(p\) of columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_+\) is nonsingular if and only if \(I_p+V^TK^{-1}U\) is nonsingular.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic Woodbury boundary is precise, but the numerical warnings concerning small singular values, backward errors, inertia loss, and refactorization lack a source and quantitative interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate-Gradient Inner Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned conjugate gradients for symmetric positive-definite inner systems in a QP iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given symmetric positive-definite \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), right-hand side \(b\in\mathbb R^n\), symmetric positive-definite preconditioner \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), initial iterate \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), and tolerance \(0<\eta<1\), set \(r_0=b-Ax_0\), solve \(Mz_0=r_0\), and set \(p_0=z_0\). For \(j=0,1,\ldots\), return \(x_j\) if \(\|r_j\|_2\leq\eta\|r_0\|_2\); otherwise compute
\[\alpha_j=\frac{r_j^Tz_j}{p_j^TAp_j},\qquad x_{j+1}=x_j+\alpha_jp_j,\qquad r_{j+1}=r_j-\alpha_jAp_j,\]
solve \(Mz_{j+1}=r_{j+1}\), set \(\beta_j=(r_{j+1}^Tz_{j+1})/(r_j^Tz_j)\), and set \(p_{j+1}=z_{j+1}+\beta_jp_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioned conjugate gradients solves a symmetric positive-definite inner system using matrix-vector products and preconditioner solves, and stops when the Euclidean residual meets the prescribed relative tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^T\succ0\) with \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
\(M=M^T\succ0\) with \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
\(b,x_0\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned iterate \(x_j\) satisfies \(\|b-Ax_j\|_2\leq\eta\|b-Ax_0\|_2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric-Indefinite Krylov Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MINRES characterization for symmetric, possibly indefinite, KKT systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=K^T\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^N\), and \(x_0\) be given. With \(r_0=b-Kx_0\), Lanczos iteration constructs an orthonormal basis \(V_j\) of \(\mathcal K_j(K,r_0)=\operatorname{span}\{r_0,Kr_0,\ldots,K^{j-1}r_0\}\) and a tridiagonal relation \(KV_j=V_{j+1}\underline T_j\). MINRES chooses
\[y_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb R^j}\|\|r_0\|e_1-\underline T_jy\|_2,\qquad x_j=x_0+V_jy_j.\]
It returns the first \(x_j\) with \(\|b-Kx_j\|_2\leq\eta\|r_0\|_2\), without requiring \(K\) to be positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MINRES uses a Lanczos basis and a small least-squares problem to minimize residuals for symmetric indefinite KKT systems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_j\in x_0+\mathcal K_j(K,r_0)\) minimizes \(\|b-Kx\|_2\) over that affine Krylov space.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Operator Application
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free action of the equality-constrained QP KKT operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a QP Hessian \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), constraint Jacobian \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and regularizations \(R_p\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(R_d\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\), the KKT operator
\[K=\begin{bmatrix}H+R_p&A^T\\A&-R_d\end{bmatrix}\]
may be applied without assembling \(K\). For every \((v,w)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\), compute
\[K\binom{v}{w}=\binom{Hv+R_pv+A^Tw}{Av-R_dw}.\]
Thus a Krylov iteration requires only routines for \(Hv\), \(Av\), \(A^Tw\), and the regularization actions, while preserving exactly the assembled operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KKT matrix-vector product can be evaluated from Hessian, Jacobian, adjoint-Jacobian, and regularization actions without assembling the block matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(H\), \(A\), \(R_p\), and \(R_d\) define linear operator actions of compatible dimensions.
The routines for \(A\) and \(A^T\) are algebraic adjoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The matrix-free block action equals multiplication by the assembled KKT matrix \(K\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block operator action is dimensionally correct and representation is the appropriate kind, but the matrix-free KKT claim has no cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Inner Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual forcing condition for inexact inner linear solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At outer iteration \(k\), let \(K_ks=d_k\) be the required inner system and let \(\widetilde s_k\) be its approximate solution. Define the linear residual \(r_k=d_k-K_k\widetilde s_k\). An adaptive relative-accuracy rule accepts \(\widetilde s_k\) when
\[\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|d_k\|,\qquad 0\leq\eta_k\leq\eta_{\max}<1.\]
For asymptotically vanishing inner perturbations, additionally require \(\eta_k\to0\); a sufficient cumulative-error condition used in perturbed fixed-point analyses is \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k\|d_k\|<\infty\). The forcing sequence may be tightened as the outer residual decreases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner solve is accepted when its relative residual meets a bounded forcing tolerance; vanishing or summable forcing controls asymptotic perturbations.
assumptions_latex: Each \(K_k\widetilde s_k\) and residual norm can be evaluated.
\(0\leq\eta_k\leq\eta_{\max}<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted inner errors satisfy \(\|d_k-K_k\widetilde s_k\|\leq\eta_k\|d_k\|\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual acceptance test is well defined, but the vanishing and summability conditions are convergence-framework dependent. No outer method or source establishes when either condition is sufficient.

children.title: Diagonal Variable Scaling
children.top_down_role: Diagonal transformations applied to primal or dual variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Variable Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible diagonal change of primal variables for a convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^TPx+q^Tx\quad\text{subject to}\quad l\leq Ax\leq u,\]
where \(P=P^T\succeq0\). For any positive diagonal \(D\), substitute \(x=D\widehat x\). The equivalent scaled QP is
\[\min_{\widehat x}\ \tfrac12\widehat x^T(DPD)\widehat x+(Dq)^T\widehat x\quad\text{subject to}\quad l\leq(AD)\widehat x\leq u.\]
The map \(\widehat x\mapsto D\widehat x\) is bijective, preserves feasibility and objective values, and maps scaled minimizers to minimizers of the original QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal variable scaling transforms the Hessian, linear term, and constraint matrix while preserving feasibility, objective values, and minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(P=P^T\succeq0\).
\(D\) is diagonal with strictly positive entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x^\star\) solves the scaled QP if and only if \(x^\star=D\widehat x^\star\) solves the original QP.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagonal change of variables and transformed QP are mathematically consistent and fit a representation leaf, but no inspectable QP-scaling source is cited.

children.title: Matrix Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Row, column, or block balancing for QP linear systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative diagonal row-and-column equilibration of a QP data matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), a norm index \(p\in[1,\infty]\), tolerance \(\tau>0\), and positive diagonal \(R_0,C_0\), repeat for \(t=0,1,\ldots\): form \(M_t=R_tMC_t\), compute nonzero row norms \(\rho_i=\|(M_t)_{i,:}\|_p\) and column norms \(\gamma_j=\|(M_t)_{:,j}\|_p\), and update
\[R_{t+1}=\operatorname{diag}(\rho_i^{-1/2})R_t,\qquad C_{t+1}=C_t\operatorname{diag}(\gamma_j^{-1/2}).\]
Stop when the spreads of nonzero row and column norms are at most \(1+\tau\), or at a prescribed iteration limit; return \(R_t,C_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equilibration alternately rescales rows and columns toward equal norms, stopping when their norm spreads meet a tolerance or an iteration limit.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) has no identically zero row or column, or such rows and columns are excluded from updates.
Initial diagonal scalings have strictly positive entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a diagonally scaled matrix \(R_tMC_t\) whose measured row and column norm spreads satisfy the stopping test when convergence occurs.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected simultaneous square-root row/column update is a particular equilibration variant whose convergence and stopping behavior require a specific source.

children.title: Scaling Quality Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators of imbalance, coefficient spread, and ineffective equilibration.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Quality Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable diagnostics for the quality and safety of diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a scaled matrix \(\widehat M=RMC\), define nonzero row norms \(\rho_i=\|\widehat M_{i,:}\|_p\), column norms \(\gamma_j=\|\widehat M_{:,j}\|_p\), spreads
\[s_r=\frac{\max_i\rho_i}{\min_i\rho_i},\qquad s_c=\frac{\max_j\gamma_j}{\min_j\gamma_j},\]
and scaling dynamic range \(d=\max\{\max_iR_{ii}/\min_iR_{ii},\max_jC_{jj}/\min_jC_{jj}\}\). The inequalities \(s_r,s_c\leq1+\tau\) certify norm equilibration to tolerance \(\tau\). A large \(d\), nonfinite scaled entry, or substantial residual growth after unscaling is a verifiable warning that scaling may amplify roundoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row and column norm spreads certify equilibration, while extreme scaling range, nonfinite entries, or unscaled residual growth warn of numerical harm.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) and \(C\) are positive diagonal matrices.
Zero rows and columns are omitted from spread ratios.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_r,s_c\leq1+\tau\) certifies the stated norm-equilibration tolerance for \(\widehat M\).

notation.meaning: dynamic range of diagonal scaling factors

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spread inequalities certify the stated diagnostic by definition, but the roundoff-warning claims and the meaning of a large scaling range lack a source or threshold.

children.title: Block Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Preconditioners organized around variable, stage, scenario, or matrix blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-diagonal preconditioner for an equality-constrained QP KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\]
choose symmetric positive-definite approximations \(\widehat H\) to \(H\) on the primal space and \(\widehat S\) to the positive Schur complement \(A\widehat H^{-1}A^T\). The block-diagonal preconditioner is
\[P_{\mathrm{BD}}=\begin{bmatrix}\widehat H&0\\0&\widehat S\end{bmatrix},\qquad P_{\mathrm{BD}}^{-1}\binom{r_x}{r_y}=\binom{\widehat H^{-1}r_x}{\widehat S^{-1}r_y}.\]
It preserves symmetry under symmetric preconditioning and separates each application into independent approximate primal and Schur-complement solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-diagonal KKT preconditioner independently approximates the primal block and positive Schur complement, enabling symmetric preconditioned Krylov iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank.
\(\widehat H=\widehat H^T\succ0\) and \(\widehat S=\widehat S^T\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Applying \(P_{\mathrm{BD}}^{-1}\) requires one solve with \(\widehat H\) and one solve with \(\widehat S\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-diagonal construction fits the preconditioner leaf and is internally consistent, but no KKT-preconditioning source supports the formulation or symmetry claim.

children.title: Constraint Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Preconditioners organized around constraint Jacobians or Schur complements.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint preconditioner retaining the exact KKT off-diagonal blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the saddle-point matrix
\[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\]
a constraint preconditioner replaces only the primal block:
\[P_C=\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}.\]
Here \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and \(G=G^T\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), so \(P_C\) is nonsingular. Its application solves a system satisfying the same linearized constraint equation as the original KKT system. If \(G=H\), then \(P_C=K\) and exact preconditioning is obtained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint preconditioner keeps the exact constraint blocks and approximates only the primal block, thereby retaining the original linearized constraint equation.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank.
\(z^TGz>0\) for every nonzero \(z\in\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_C\) is nonsingular and its second block equation is the exact constraint equation \(A\Delta x=r_y\).

notation.meaning: approximation to the primal KKT block
null space of the constraint Jacobian

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The null-space definiteness condition is appropriate for nonsingularity and the representation fits the leaf, but the constraint-preconditioner characterization lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Coupled KKT Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Designs retaining selected primal-dual coupling in saddle-point systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled KKT Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled triangular preconditioner derived from the KKT block factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\]
with nonsingular \(H\), let \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\). The exact block factorization is
\[K=\begin{bmatrix}I&0\\AH^{-1}&I\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}H&0\\0&-S\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}I&H^{-1}A^T\\0&I\end{bmatrix}.\]
Replacing \(H\) and \(S\) by readily invertible approximations \(\widehat H\) and \(\widehat S\) yields coupled lower-, upper-, or full-factor KKT preconditioners. Unlike a block-diagonal choice, their application retains an approximate primal-dual coupling through multiplication by \(A\) or \(A^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupled KKT preconditioners approximate the block LDU factors, retaining primal-dual coupling while replacing expensive Hessian and Schur solves.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is nonsingular.
\(A\) has full row rank, so \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\) is nonsingular when the stated factorization is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Substitution of invertible \(\widehat H\) and \(\widehat S\) in the displayed factors defines an invertible coupled KKT preconditioner.

notation.meaning: KKT Schur complement without its negative sign

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed block factorization is algebraically correct when H and S are nonsingular. However, nonsingular indefinite H together with full-row-rank A does not by itself imply that S=AH^{-1}A^T is nonsingular; corrected hypotheses and an authoritative source are required.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Structure-Aware Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible variable and constraint transformations that retain exploitable QP sparsity or block structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the QP \(\min_x \tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), choose nonsingular structured matrices \(S\) and \(R\), set \(x=Sz\), and scale the equations by \(R\). The equivalent transformed QP has data \[\widehat Q=S^{\mathsf T}QS,\qquad \widehat q=S^{\mathsf T}q,\qquad \widehat A=RAS,\qquad \widehat b=Rb.\] A structure-aware preconditioner selects \(R,S\) so that applying them and solving systems involving the transformed operator preserve a designated sparsity, banded, block, or decomposition pattern while reducing a specified spectral condition measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structured invertible scaling yields an equivalent QP and is chosen to improve conditioning without destroying the sparsity or decomposition used by the solver.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
\(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star=Sz^\star\), and the original and transformed QPs have corresponding feasible points and equal objective values under this substitution.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invertible congruence and equation scaling are standard QP transformations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transformation formulas and equivalence claim are standard, and the representation fits the leaf. However, no inspectable citation supports the structure-preservation and conditioning claim, and the transformed operator and spectral condition measure are not specified.

children.title: Banded QP Kernels
children.top_down_role: Linear-algebra kernels exploiting bounded scalar or block bandwidth.

knowledge_statements.title: Banded QP Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct linear-algebra kernels for symmetric positive-definite banded QP systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite with half-bandwidth \(w\), meaning \(H_{ij}=0\) whenever \(|i-j|>w\). Banded Cholesky factorization computes \(H=LL^{\mathsf T}\) without entries outside the same lower half-band, using \(O(nw^2)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(nw)\) storage. Each subsequent solution of \(Hx=r\) by banded forward and backward substitution uses \(O(nw)\) operations. Thus a QP iteration whose fixed structured kernel is such a solve can reuse the factorization across right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite banded QP system factors in linear complexity for fixed bandwidth, and each reused solve is cheaper still.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
The variable ordering gives \(H\) half-bandwidth \(w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The factorization cost is \(O(nw^2)\), its storage is \(O(nw)\), and each triangular solve costs \(O(nw)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The banded Cholesky storage and arithmetic bounds are mathematically standard and complexity_bound fits the leaf, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Block-Tridiagonal QP Kernels
children.top_down_role: Stagewise kernels for block-tridiagonal systems arising in structured QPs.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Tridiagonal QP Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block elimination for positive-definite block-tridiagonal systems arising in staged QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric block-tridiagonal matrix with diagonal blocks \(D_k\) and lower off-diagonal blocks \(E_k\), initialize \(S_1=D_1\). For \(k=2,\ldots,N\), compute \[L_k=E_kS_{k-1}^{-1},\qquad S_k=D_k-L_kE_k^{\mathsf T}.\] Solve the resulting block lower-triangular system forward and its transpose backward. If every \(S_k\) is positive definite, these recurrences give a block \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization. With block dimension at most \(p\), factorization costs \(O(Np^3)\), storage costs \(O(Np^2)\), and one solve costs \(O(Np^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential block Schur complements factor a positive-definite block-tridiagonal QP system with work linear in the number of stages for fixed block size.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient matrix is symmetric positive definite and block tridiagonal.
Every block has dimension at most \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recurrence produces a valid block \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) solve with factorization complexity \(O(Np^3)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: block LDL recurrence for block-tridiagonal positive-definite matrices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block elimination recurrence and stated complexities are consistent with an SPD block-tridiagonal system, and algorithm is an appropriate kind. An authoritative structured-factorization citation with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Structure-Breaking Fill
children.top_down_role: Couplings and reorderings that erode banded or block-tridiagonal efficiency.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Breaking Fill
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of banded or block-local complexity under nonlocal couplings or unsuitable elimination orderings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the path-structured positive-definite matrix \(H_0\) whose graph has edges \((i,i+1)\). Its natural-order Cholesky factor has fixed bandwidth. Add couplings from vertex \(1\) to every vertex \(j\ge3\), obtaining \(H=H_0+U\) with symmetric star-patterned \(U\), and eliminate vertex \(1\) first. The Schur update \(H_{2:n,2:n}-H_{2:n,1}H_{11}^{-1}H_{1,2:n}\) couples every pair of neighbors of vertex \(1\); hence its trailing graph contains a clique and may require \(\Theta(n^2)\) factor storage. Fixed-band complexity therefore fails when nonlocal couplings or the ordering create large elimination fronts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlocal coupling eliminated early can turn a banded path into a dense Schur complement, destroying linear-storage structured solves.
assumptions_latex: \(H\succ0\) and vertex \(1\) is adjacent to \(\Theta(n)\) remaining vertices.
Vertex \(1\) is eliminated before those neighbors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The first Schur complement can contain \(\Theta(n^2)\) nonzeros, so fixed-band storage and arithmetic bounds no longer apply.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sparse elimination makes every eliminated vertex's remaining neighbors a clique

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon is appropriate for this leaf, but the clique statement should be supported as symbolic fill; actual numerical nonzeros can depend on cancellation. No inspectable sparse-elimination source is cited.

children.title: Arrowhead QP Kernels
children.top_down_role: Kernels exploiting a shared core coupled to otherwise separable blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Arrowhead QP Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block elimination for locally separable systems coupled through a small global block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[K=\begin{pmatrix}D&B^{\mathsf T}\\B&C\end{pmatrix},\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(D_1,\ldots,D_s),\] where every \(D_i\) is nonsingular. For \(K(x,z)^{\mathsf T}=(r_x,r_z)^{\mathsf T}\), eliminate the local variables in parallel: \(x=D^{-1}(r_x-B^{\mathsf T}z)\). The coupling variable satisfies \[Sz=r_z-BD^{-1}r_x,\qquad S=C-BD^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}.\] After solving this reduced system, recover each local block independently. The arrowhead kernel therefore reduces the globally coupled computation to local block solves plus one Schur-complement solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arrowhead QP system separates into parallel local solves and one reduced global Schur-complement solve.
assumptions_latex: Every local block \(D_i\) is square and nonsingular.
The Schur complement \(S=C-BD^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed elimination gives the unique solution of \(K(x,z)^{\mathsf T}=(r_x,r_z)^{\mathsf T}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact block Gaussian elimination for arrowhead matrices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The arrowhead block elimination formulas are correct under the stated nonsingularity assumptions, and representation fits the container. No authoritative block-linear-algebra citation is supplied.

children.title: Consensus QP Kernels
children.top_down_role: Kernels exploiting replicated local variables linked through consensus constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus QP Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable quadratic subproblems linked by equality of local and shared variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A consensus QP has local variables \(x_i\in\mathbb R^p\), a shared variable \(z\in\mathbb R^p\), and form \[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_s,z}\ \sum_{i=1}^s\left(\tfrac12x_i^{\mathsf T}Q_ix_i+q_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\right)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i=z\ \ (i=1,\ldots,s).\] For penalty \(\rho>0\), the augmented local Hessians are \(Q_i+\rho I\), so local primal updates separate across \(i\). The shared-variable update aggregates the local quantities, and dual updates enforce the residuals \(x_i-z\). At any feasible limit, every local copy equals the common decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus splitting duplicates a shared decision, producing independent local quadratic solves followed by aggregation and equality-residual updates.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_i=Q_i^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) for every \(i\).
\(\rho>0\), and the consensus constraints are jointly feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented quadratic minimization separates by agent, while feasibility is exactly \(x_1=\cdots=x_s=z\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard consensus reformulation and augmented-Lagrangian separability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The consensus formulation and local augmented Hessians are standard, but the aggregation and dual-update statements implicitly invoke an unspecified augmented-Lagrangian or ADMM variant. A source is needed to identify and support the intended kernel.

children.title: Schur-Complement Coupling
children.top_down_role: Reduced-system organization shared by arrowhead and consensus structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduction of partitioned QP linear systems to their coupling variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}\) with nonsingular \(A\), and consider \(K(u,v)^{\mathsf T}=(f,g)^{\mathsf T}\). Eliminating \(u=A^{-1}(f-Bv)\) yields the reduced coupling equation \[Sv=g-CA^{-1}f,\qquad S=D-CA^{-1}B.\] If \(S\) is nonsingular, solve this equation for \(v\) and recover \(u\). Moreover, \(K\) is nonsingular if and only if \(S\) is nonsingular. In structured QP kernels, applications of \(A^{-1}\) can be performed independently whenever \(A\) is block diagonal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating local variables produces an exact reduced system on coupling variables, with the Schur complement determining nonsingularity.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is square and nonsingular.
All block dimensions are conformable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is nonsingular exactly when \(S=D-CA^{-1}B\) is nonsingular, and the displayed elimination recovers its solution.

notation.meaning: Schur complement of the block A

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Schur-complement reduction and nonsingularity equivalence are correct, and representation fits the leaf. No authoritative matrix-analysis citation with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Decomposed QP Kernels
children.top_down_role: Local kernels induced by variable, constraint, scenario, or temporal decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposed QP Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic solves coordinated through a low-dimensional coupling constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_s}\sum_i(\tfrac12x_i^{\mathsf T}Q_ix_i+q_i^{\mathsf T}x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\), with \(Q_i\succ0\). Given a multiplier \(y^k\), compute in parallel \[x_i^{k}=\arg\min_{x_i}\left\{\tfrac12x_i^{\mathsf T}Q_ix_i+q_i^{\mathsf T}x_i+(y^k)^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i\right\},\] form \(r^k=\sum_iA_ix_i^k-b\), and update \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_kr^k\). Stop when the coupling residual and an appropriate dual or iterate residual satisfy prescribed tolerances; return the local blocks and multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual decomposition solves independent local QPs, aggregates their coupling residual, and updates a shared multiplier until primal and dual tolerances hold.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_i=Q_i^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) for every local block.
The coupling constraint is feasible.
The step-size rule is chosen for convergence of dual gradient ascent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration consists of separable local QP kernels followed by one coupling-residual aggregation and multiplier update.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard dual-decomposition iteration for separable strongly convex QPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed iteration is a plausible dual-gradient decomposition kernel, but its convergence-relevant step-size rule and stopping residual are not defined. The intended algorithmic version requires an authoritative source.

children.title: Distributed QP Kernels
children.top_down_role: Kernels mapped across processors, devices, or networked compute nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed QP Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighbor-to-neighbor consensus iteration for a graph-coupled separable quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a connected undirected graph distribute convex quadratic functions \(f_i(x_i)=\tfrac12x_i^{\mathsf T}Q_ix_i+q_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\), and impose \(x_i=x_j\) on every edge. Orient the edges and let \(B\) be the incidence matrix, so consensus is \((B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I)x=0\). A distributed augmented-Lagrangian kernel alternates local minimization of the quadratic augmented Lagrangian, exchange of current boundary variables with neighbors, and multiplier updates \[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho(B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I)x^{k+1}.\] Stop when consensus and stationarity residuals meet prescribed tolerances; output the agreed primal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed QP kernel performs local quadratic updates, neighbor exchanges, and edge-multiplier updates until consensus and stationarity residuals are small.
assumptions_latex: The communication graph is connected and undirected.
\(Q_i=Q_i^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), the QP has a solution, and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupling residual is \((B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I)x\), and every zero-residual iterate has identical local variables on the connected graph.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: incidence-matrix consensus and augmented-Lagrangian multiplier update

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incidence-matrix consensus condition and multiplier update are standard. However, the augmented quadratic generally couples neighboring variables, so the claimed local minimization requires a precise splitting and update schedule supported by a source.

children.title: Coordination-Overhead Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where synchronization or data exchange offsets local computational savings.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordination-Overhead Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration cost model separating local QP work from communication and synchronization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(s\) workers execute local QP kernels with times \(T_i\), exchange \(M\) scalar words, perform \(R\) communication rounds, and incur synchronization time \(T_{\mathrm{sync}}\). Under a bulk-synchronous model with per-word time \(\beta\) and per-round latency \(\alpha\), the iteration time satisfies the model \[T_{\mathrm{iter}}=\max_{1\le i\le s}T_i+R\alpha+M\beta+T_{\mathrm{sync}}.\] The coordination-dominated regime is defined by \(R\alpha+M\beta+T_{\mathrm{sync}}\ge\max_iT_i\); the computation-dominated regime is defined by the reverse strict inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed QP iterations are coordination dominated when latency, data movement, and synchronization cost at least as much as the slowest local solve.
assumptions_latex: Workers follow a bulk-synchronous execution model.
\(\alpha,\beta,T_i,T_{\mathrm{sync}}\ge0\), and communication does not overlap computation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coordination dominates exactly under \(R\alpha+M\beta+T_{\mathrm{sync}}\ge\max_iT_i\) in the stated model.

notation.meaning: message-round latency and per-word transfer time
communication rounds and transferred scalar words

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed expression is an assumed bulk-synchronous performance model rather than a derived complexity bound; condition or representation may better fit this regime-defining leaf. Its additive latency, bandwidth, and synchronization model also lacks an authoritative citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Batched Dense QP Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel solution of many independent small dense QP linear-algebra subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a batch \(j=1,\ldots,B\) of independent dense systems \(H_jx_j=r_j\), initialize one output slot per instance. In parallel over \(j\), factor \(H_j=L_jL_j^{\mathsf T}\), solve \(L_jy_j=r_j\), and solve \(L_j^{\mathsf T}x_j=y_j\). Report failure for any instance whose factorization detects nonpositive curvature; otherwise return all \(x_j\). If every dimension is at most \(p\), the total arithmetic work is \(O(Bp^3)\), the critical-path arithmetic depth under ideal batch parallelism is \(O(p^3)\), and factor reuse reduces later right-hand sides to \(O(Bp^2)\) total work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent small dense QP systems can be factored concurrently, with cubic total work per instance and quadratic work for reused solves.
assumptions_latex: Each \(H_j=H_j^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and has dimension at most \(p\).
Batch instances share no algebraic coupling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The batch returns \(x_j=H_j^{-1}r_j\) with total factorization work \(O(Bp^3)\) and reusable factors.

notation.meaning: Cholesky factor for batch instance j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: independent batched Cholesky and triangular-solve complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The batched Cholesky algorithm and total-work estimates are standard, but the ideal-parallel critical-path claim depends on the execution model. No dense-linear-algebra or parallel-kernel source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Hessian Convexity Checks
children.top_down_role: Numerical and structural checks supporting convex-QP classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian Convexity Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and tolerance-aware validation of convexity for a quadratic objective, distinguished from symmetry validation of supplied Hessian data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+c\), define the symmetric Hessian \(H=(Q+Q^{\mathsf T})/2\). Then \(f\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(H\succeq0\), equivalently \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv\ge0\) for every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\). If an input contract requires \(Q\) itself to represent a symmetric Hessian, reject the data when \(\lVert Q-Q^{\mathsf T}\rVert\) exceeds the declared symmetry tolerance; this is an input-validation rule rather than a necessary condition for convexity of the represented quadratic. Numerically, the test \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge-\tau\), with \(\tau\ge0\), certifies \(H+\tau I\succeq0\), not exact positive semidefiniteness of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic is convex exactly when the symmetric part of its quadratic coefficient is positive semidefinite. Requiring symmetric input data is a separate validation rule, and tolerance-based acceptance certifies only the shifted symmetric Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R\), and \(\tau\ge0\).
Convexity is assessed on all of \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact convexity is equivalent to \(H=(Q+Q^{\mathsf T})/2\succeq0\), while \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge-\tau\) implies only \(H+\tau I\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: symmetric Hessian represented by the quadratic coefficient
smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convexity of a quadratic is characterized by positive semidefiniteness of its symmetric Hessian

children.title: Constraint Data Validation
children.top_down_role: Consistency, dimensions, bounds, and finite-value checks for constraint data.

assumptions_latex: The QP constraint model is \(l\leq Ax\leq u\), with \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(l,u\in(\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\})^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint data are structurally valid exactly when dimensions agree, no bound is NaN, and \(l_i\leq u_i\) for every \(i\).
review_flags: solver-specific acceptance of infinite or unconstrained rows needs an authoritative source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural validation for two-sided linear constraints before solver preprocessing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the constraint system \(l\leq Ax\leq u\), validation accepts the data if and only if \(A\) has \(m\) rows, \(l\) and \(u\) each have length \(m\), every stored entry of \(A\) is finite, neither bound vector contains NaN, and \(l_i\leq u_i\) for all \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Infinite endpoints are permitted only with their indicated sign. A row with \(l_i=-\infty\) and \(u_i=+\infty\) is valid but redundant and may be removed during presolve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint arrays must have compatible dimensions, finite matrix entries, non-NaN bounds, and componentwise lower bounds no greater than upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Data Validation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but no source supports the policies for infinities, finite matrix entries, or redundant unconstrained rows. The conclusion also omits some conditions stated in the main predicate.

children.title: Numerical Input Sanity Checks
children.top_down_role: Magnitude, symmetry, precision, and representation checks before solver execution.

assumptions_latex: The QP is represented by \(P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and bounds \(l,u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Passing the checks guarantees well-defined finite arithmetic at solver initialization, except for explicitly permitted bound infinities.
review_flags: numerical thresholds and symmetry tolerances are implementation-dependent and need a source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Machine-data checks preceding convexity tests, presolve, and scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Numerical input passes the sanity predicate when all dimensions are consistent; every stored entry of \(P\), \(q\), and \(A\) is a finite real number; no datum is NaN; bound entries are finite or correctly signed infinities; and sparse indices are in range. If only one triangle of \(P\) is supplied, that storage convention must be declared; otherwise the supplied matrix must satisfy \(\lVert P-P^{\mathsf T}\rVert\leq\tau_{\mathrm{sym}}\) for a documented tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{sym}}\geq0\). Empty dimensions are accepted only if the selected backend defines them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sanity checking rejects inconsistent dimensions, NaNs, illegal infinities, invalid sparse indices, and Hessian data that violate the declared symmetry convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Input Sanity Checks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits, but symmetry conventions, tolerance, empty-dimension handling, sparse-index validation, and permitted infinities are implementation-specific and uncited.

children.title: QP Presolve
children.top_down_role: Structural reductions, eliminations, and simplifications performed before numerical solution.

assumptions_latex: The original convex QP and every presolve transformation are represented in exact arithmetic.
Each transformation records sufficient information to reconstruct eliminated primal and dual variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Presolve either detects a valid infeasibility certificate or produces a reduced QP whose solutions lift to solutions of the original QP.
review_flags: the admissible presolve rule set and certificate conventions need an authoritative QP source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence-preserving reductions for a convex QP before numerical conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the working problem as \(\widehat{\mathcal Q}=\mathcal Q\) and the reconstruction map as \(R=I\). Repeatedly remove free constraint rows, substitute fixed variables, eliminate singleton equalities, tighten bounds implied by singleton rows, delete duplicate constraints, and remove identically zero coefficients. If a zero row or implied bound yields a contradiction, stop with the corresponding infeasibility certificate. Otherwise stop when no enabled rule changes \(\widehat{\mathcal Q}\), solve the reduced QP, and apply the recorded transformations in reverse order. Every enabled reduction must preserve feasibility and objective values under \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve repeatedly applies reversible reductions, reports certified contradictions, or returns a smaller equivalent QP together with a solution-reconstruction map.
knowledge_statements.title: QP Presolve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the reduction set and certificate claims require authoritative support. Fixed-variable substitution can introduce an objective constant, so literal preservation of objective values requires recording an offset or qualifying the claim.

children.title: Problem Scaling
children.top_down_role: Variable, constraint, and objective transformations controlling coefficient magnitude.

assumptions_latex: The QP is \(\min_x \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(l\leq Ax\leq u\).
The diagonal matrices \(D\) and \(E\), and scalar \(c\), have strictly positive diagonal entries or value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled and original QPs are equivalent under \(x=D\bar x\), with identical minimizers after inverse scaling.

notation.meaning: Positive variable and constraint scaling matrices

review_flags: a source is needed for the solver's exact scaling and dual recovery convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal scaling that preserves the QP solution correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the substitution \(x=D\bar x\), define \(\bar P=cD^{\mathsf T}PD\), \(\bar q=cD^{\mathsf T}q\), \(\bar A=EAD\), \(\bar l=El\), and \(\bar u=Eu\), with signed infinities unchanged by positive scaling. Then the scaled problem is \(\min_{\bar x}\tfrac12\bar x^{\mathsf T}\bar P\bar x+\bar q^{\mathsf T}\bar x\) subject to \(\bar l\leq\bar A\bar x\leq\bar u\). Its objective equals \(c\) times the original objective, so primal minimizers correspond bijectively through \(x=D\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal variable, constraint, and objective scalings produce an equivalent QP whose primal solutions recover by the inverse coordinate transformation.
knowledge_statements.title: Problem Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits and the primal scaling formulas are coherent, but the exact solver scaling and recovery conventions are uncited. The plain statement's phrase “inverse coordinate transformation” is ambiguous relative to the stated recovery map x=D bar x.

children.title: System Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Balancing of solver matrices or operator blocks before factorization or iteration.

assumptions_latex: The assembled linear-system matrix \(K\) has no structurally zero row or column among the indices being equilibrated.
All scaling factors are restricted to positive finite values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration returns diagonal scalings that reduce disparities among nonzero row and column norms without changing the represented linear system's solutions.
review_flags: the precise equilibration norm, clipping, and stopping thresholds need a solver source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative diagonal equilibration of the solver's linear-system matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(R=I\), \(C=I\), and \(K_0=K\). At iteration \(t\), compute positive row factors \(r_i=\lVert(K_t)_{i,:}\rVert_p^{-1/2}\) and column factors \(c_j=\lVert(K_t)_{:,j}\rVert_p^{-1/2}\), optionally clipped to fixed positive limits. Set \(K_{t+1}=\operatorname{diag}(r)K_t\operatorname{diag}(c)\), \(R\leftarrow\operatorname{diag}(r)R\), and \(C\leftarrow C\operatorname{diag}(c)\). Stop when the row and column norm spreads meet prescribed tolerances or an iteration limit is reached; output \(R,K_t,C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterative positive diagonal row and column scaling reduces norm imbalance in the solver matrix while preserving a recoverable linear-system equivalence.
knowledge_statements.title: System Equilibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the norm, exponent, clipping, and stopping rules lack a source. Preserving a recoverable linear-system equivalence also requires specifying right-hand-side scaling and solution recovery.

assumptions_latex: The convex-QP Hessian satisfies \(P\succeq0\).
The parameters satisfy \(\sigma>0\) and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized KKT matrix is symmetric quasi-definite and therefore nonsingular.
review_flags: needs an authoritative locator for the stated quasi-definite regularization convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric primal-dual regularization used in splitting-based QP linear solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the regularized saddle-point matrix by \[K_{\sigma,\rho}=\begin{pmatrix}P+\sigma I&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\rho^{-1}I\end{pmatrix}.\] Since \(P+\sigma I\succ0\) and \(-\rho^{-1}I\prec0\), the matrix \(K_{\sigma,\rho}\) is symmetric quasi-definite. Consequently it is nonsingular for every real matrix \(A\), including rank-deficient matrices. The positive primal block and negative dual block stabilize the linear solve; changing \(\sigma\) or \(\rho\) changes the regularized system and must remain consistent with the surrounding splitting iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive primal and dual regularization makes the symmetric QP saddle-point matrix quasi-definite and nonsingular even when the constraint matrix is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Regularization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind correctly fits this topic, and the stated block-sign conditions support the standard quasi-definite conclusion, but no inspectable source locator is supplied.

children.title: Sparsity-Pattern Analysis
children.top_down_role: Pattern, fill, ordering, and reusable-structure assessment for solver preparation.

assumptions_latex: The sparsity patterns of \(P\) and \(A\) are fixed during repeated numerical solves.
Structural nonzeros are distinguished from entries that happen to be numerically zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pattern of the assembled KKT matrix and its symbolic fill can be computed without using numerical coefficient values.
review_flags: symbolic-fill and ordering claims need a sparse-factorization source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic analysis of the regularized KKT system before backend selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{pmatrix}P+\sigma I&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\rho^{-1}I\end{pmatrix}\), its structural pattern is determined by \(\operatorname{supp}(P)\), \(\operatorname{supp}(A)\), and both diagonal blocks. A symmetric elimination ordering applied to the undirected graph of this pattern determines the symbolic factor pattern and an estimated fill count independently of the numerical nonzero values. Therefore the symbolic analysis may be reused while these supports remain unchanged; adding or deleting a structural nonzero invalidates that reuse, whereas changing only stored numerical values does not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The structural supports of the Hessian and constraints determine the KKT graph, symbolic fill, and whether symbolic factorization can be reused.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Pattern Analysis

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits, but the symbolic-fill and reuse claims require a sparse-factorization source. Reuse also presumes a fixed ordering and symbolic policy, which should be made explicit by that source.

children.title: Backend Compatibility Analysis

assumptions_latex: A backend declaration specifies accepted matrix format, scalar type, index width, symmetry convention, and definiteness requirements.
The prepared QP system has known dimensions and structural properties.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A complete compatibility predicate between prepared QP data and a linear-system backend.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a backend \(B\), define \(\mathcal C_B(K)\) as the conjunction of: supported scalar and index types; representable dimensions and nonzero count; accepted sparse layout or available lossless conversion; matching symmetry and triangle-storage conventions; satisfaction of the backend's definiteness or quasi-definiteness requirement; and availability of every operation required by the solver, including symbolic setup, numerical solve, and parameter updates. The prepared system \(K\) may be assigned to \(B\) if and only if \(\mathcal C_B(K)\) is true. Conversion cost may affect selection but not logical compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A backend is compatible only when the prepared system satisfies all declared type, size, storage, matrix-class, and required-operation capabilities.
knowledge_statements.title: Backend Compatibility Analysis

children.title: Backend Selection Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes where sparsity, memory, or conditioning changes the preferred backend.

assumptions_latex: Both candidate backends pass their logical compatibility predicates.
A direct backend materializes and factors the system, while an indirect backend uses matrix-vector products and an iterative stopping tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No sparsity-only threshold universally identifies the faster backend; selection boundaries depend on fill, memory, conditioning, tolerance, and reuse.
review_flags: quantitative selection boundaries require backend-specific benchmarks and documentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of universal rules for choosing direct versus indirect QP linear solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A direct backend is inadmissible when its estimated factor storage \(f\) exceeds available memory \(M\), while an indirect backend is inadmissible when it cannot meet the required linear-solve tolerance within its iteration budget. Between these boundaries, matrix dimension and input nonzero count alone do not determine the preferable backend: two matrices with identical dimensions and nonzero counts may have different elimination fill, spectra, preconditioner quality, and reuse opportunities. Hence any fixed rule based only on \(n\), \(m\), or \(\operatorname{nnz}(K)\) has instances on which its performance ordering reverses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct selection fails under excessive factor fill; indirect selection fails under poor convergence, and dimensions or nonzero counts alone cannot define a universal boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Backend Selection Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the universal reversal claim is stronger than the supplied rationale and needs evidence or a precisely delimited model. Memory and convergence boundaries also depend on backend-specific estimates and policies.

assumptions_latex: The regularized KKT matrix \(K\) is symmetric quasi-definite.
A sparse direct factorization backend supports the selected ordering and numerical scalar type.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each solve returns \(z\) satisfying \(Kz=b\) up to the backend's numerical tolerance, with reusable symbolic work while the pattern is fixed.

notation.meaning: Regularized KKT matrix and right-hand side

review_flags: factorization form, pivoting, and refinement policy require backend-specific sources
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse factorization backend for repeated regularized KKT solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(K\) and \(b\), compute a fill-reducing symmetric permutation \(\Pi\), perform symbolic analysis, and numerically factor \(\Pi K\Pi^{\mathsf T}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), using the backend's stable pivoting policy. Solve successively with \(L\), \(D\), and \(L^{\mathsf T}\), then unpermute to obtain \(z\). Optionally apply iterative refinement until \(\lVert Kz-b\rVert\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\lVert b\rVert\). Reuse symbolic analysis while the sparsity pattern is unchanged, and reuse the numerical factors while all entries of \(K\) are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct backend orders and factors the sparse KKT matrix, performs triangular solves, and reuses symbolic or numerical work when valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Direct Sparse Backend
