assumptions_latex: The reduced positive-definite operator \(H=P+\sigma I+\rho A^{\mathsf T}A\) is available through matrix-vector products.
A symmetric positive-definite preconditioner \(M\) can be applied without forming \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Preconditioned conjugate gradients returns an approximate reduced-system solution using only operator products and vector operations.
review_flags: the exact reduced system and inexact-solve policy need an operator-splitting QP source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free iterative solution of the positive-definite reduced QP system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To solve \(Hx=g\), initialize \(x_0\), \(r_0=g-Hx_0\), \(z_0=M^{-1}r_0\), and \(p_0=z_0\). Apply preconditioned conjugate-gradient recurrences using products \(Pv\), \(Av\), and \(A^{\mathsf T}v\), so neither \(H\) nor a KKT factorization is formed. Stop at the first iterate satisfying \(\lVert r_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\lVert g\rVert\), or report failure at the iteration limit. Recover any eliminated dual component from the defining block equation and return the combined approximate linear-system solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indirect backend applies preconditioned conjugate gradients to a positive-definite reduced operator using Hessian and constraint matrix-vector products only.
knowledge_statements.title: Indirect Matrix-Free Backend

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, and PCG is appropriate under the stated positive-definiteness assumptions, but the particular reduced operator and its relationship to the surrounding splitting system need a source. The eliminated dual component and defining block equation are not introduced explicitly.

children.title: Penalty-Parameter Management
children.top_down_role: Selection and adaptation regimes for penalty parameters in splitting-based QP solvers.

assumptions_latex: At update index \(k\), primal and dual residual norms \(r_{\mathrm p}^k,r_{\mathrm d}^k\geq0\) are computed in mutually consistent scaling.
Parameters satisfy \(\mu>1\), \(\tau>1\), and \(0<\rho_{\min}\leq\rho_{max}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update keeps \(\rho_k\) positive and bounded while increasing it for primal-dominated residuals and decreasing it for dual-dominated residuals.

notation.meaning: Imbalance threshold and multiplicative update factor

review_flags: exact residual definitions, update cadence, and dual rescaling convention need a solver source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-balancing control of the splitting penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\rho_0\in[\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\). At each scheduled update, set \[\rho_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\min\{\tau\rho_k,\rho_{\max}\},&r_{\mathrm p}^k>\mu r_{\mathrm d}^k,\\\max\{\rho_k/\tau,\rho_{\min}\},&r_{\mathrm d}^k>\mu r_{\mathrm p}^k,\\\rho_k,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}\] If the algorithm stores a scaled dual variable, rescale it so that the corresponding unscaled multiplier is unchanged. Update or refactor the linear-system operator whenever its dependence on \(\rho\) changes. Stop adapting after convergence or after a prescribed number of unsuccessful updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual balancing raises the penalty when primal progress lags, lowers it when dual progress lags, and preserves bounds and dual-variable consistency.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Parameter Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but residual definitions, update cadence, stopping policy, and scaled-dual rescaling are solver-specific and uncited. An authoritative solver source is required before fixing this version.

children.title: Relaxation-Parameter Management
children.top_down_role: Selection and safeguarding regimes for under-relaxation or over-relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Parameter Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded relaxation control for an ADMM-style convex QP iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For relaxation parameter \(\alpha_k\), choose safeguards \(0<\alpha_{\min}\leq 1\leq\alpha_{\max}<2\), initialize \(\alpha_0\in[\alpha_{\min},\alpha_{\max}]\), and form the relaxed quantity \(\hat z^{k+1}=\alpha_k A x^{k+1}+(1-\alpha_k)z^k\). Use \(\hat z^{k+1}\), rather than \(Ax^{k+1}\), in the projection and dual updates. A proposed controller value \(\tilde\alpha_{k+1}\) is accepted only after clipping: \(\alpha_{k+1}=\min\{\alpha_{\max},\max\{\alpha_{\min},\tilde\alpha_{k+1}\}\}\). If a monitored residual merit increases by more than a prescribed factor, reject the proposal and reset \(\alpha_{k+1}=1\). Output the latest iterate satisfying the solver stopping test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep ADMM relaxation strictly between zero and two, clip every adaptive proposal, and reset to one when the monitored residual deteriorates excessively.
assumptions_latex: \(P\succeq0\) and the QP constraint set is closed and convex.
The underlying unrelaxed splitting iteration is well defined.
\(0<\alpha_{\min}\leq1\leq\alpha_{\max}<2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k\in[\alpha_{\min},\alpha_{\max}]\subset(0,2)\) for every accepted iteration.

notation.meaning: relaxed affine image used by the splitting updates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the relaxation-management leaf, but no cited source supports the particular relaxed update, clipping controller, deterioration test, or reset policy. The QP data and controller merit are also not fully introduced, so the solver-specific mathematical version cannot be validated.

children.title: Penalty–Relaxation Interaction Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Convergence and stability effects caused by coupled parameter choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty–Relaxation Interaction Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint diagnostic for penalty and relaxation changes in operator-splitting QP iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_p^k=Ax^k-z^k\), \(r_d^k=Px^k+q+A^Ty^k\), and \(M_k=\max\{\|r_p^k\|/\varepsilon_p,\|r_d^k\|/\varepsilon_d\}\). After changing the penalty and relaxation pair from \((\rho_k,\alpha_k)\) to \((\rho_{k+1},\alpha_{k+1})\), declare the interaction adverse when \(M_{k+1}>\gamma M_k\), where \(\gamma>1\), or when the dominant residual alternates for at least \(s\) consecutive control checks without decreasing \(M_k\). An adverse diagnosis requires suppressing simultaneous further changes: retain one parameter, revert the other to its last accepted value, and reassess after a fixed observation window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flag adverse coupling when a joint penalty-relaxation change enlarges normalized KKT residuals or causes persistent alternation without net progress.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_p>0\), \(\varepsilon_d>0\), \(\gamma>1\), and \(s\geq2\).
Residuals are evaluated using one consistent scaling during the observation window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An adverse diagnosis prevents another simultaneous change of \(\rho\) and \(\alpha\) until reassessment.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the interaction-diagnostics leaf, but the adverse-coupling thresholds, alternation rule, observation window, and prescribed response are implementation-specific and uncited. Dimensions and domains for the QP data and the integer control parameter are not fully specified.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Optimality Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based approximate KKT status for a convex box-constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TPx+q^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\in C=[l,u]\), with \(P\succeq0\). For candidate \((x,y)\), set \(z=\Pi_C(Ax)\), \(r_p=Ax-z\), \(r_d=Px+q+A^Ty\), and \(r_n=y-\Pi_{N_C(z)}(y)\). Given positive absolute and relative tolerances defining \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_n\), report approximate optimality only if \(\|r_p\|\leq\varepsilon_p\), \(\|r_d\|\leq\varepsilon_d\), and \(\|r_n\|\leq\varepsilon_n\), all computed in the original problem coordinates. These inequalities form a directly verifiable approximate KKT certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate optimality requires small primal feasibility, stationarity, and normal-cone consistency residuals in the original QP coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(P\succeq0\) and \(C=[l,u]\) is nonempty and closed.
All status tolerances are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y)\) satisfies the prescribed approximate KKT tests for the original convex QP.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the constraint box
normal cone of C at z

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the status leaf and the residual construction is plausible, but there is no source for this three-residual status definition, its normal-cone sign convention, or the unspecified absolute-relative tolerance normalization.

children.title: Infeasibility Status
children.top_down_role: Solver classifications supported by approximate primal or dual infeasibility evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-type primal-infeasibility certificate for box-constrained convex QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(l\leq Ax\leq u\), a vector \(v\neq0\) certifies primal infeasibility when \(A^Tv=0\) and \(u^T v_+ + l^T v_-<0\), where \(v_+=\max\{v,0\}\) and \(v_-=\min\{v,0\}\) componentwise. Terms involving an infinite bound are admissible only when their multiplier component is zero. With tolerances, report approximate infeasibility when \(\|A^Tv\|\leq\varepsilon_A\|v\|\) and \(u^Tv_+ + l^Tv_-\leq-\varepsilon_I\|v\|\), using \(\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_I>0\). The strict exact inequalities exclude every point satisfying the constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero null-space vector whose signed bound support is negative certifies that the QP constraints cannot be satisfied.
assumptions_latex: The bound set \([l,u]\) is closed, with infinite-bound terms handled by the stated convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:l\leq Ax\leq u\}=\varnothing\) in the exact case.

notation.meaning: componentwise positive and negative parts of the certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact Farkas-type certificate is standard and fits the leaf, but no citation with an inspectable locator is supplied. The approximate normalization and treatment of infinite bounds are solver-specific enough that the full status statement requires a source.

children.title: Unboundedness Status
children.top_down_role: Solver classifications supported by improving-ray or recession evidence.

assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
The box \(C=\{z\in\mathbb R^m:l\leq z\leq u\}\) is nonempty, where \(l_i\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\), \(u_i\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and \(l_i\leq u_i\).
A feasible point \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) exists, and \(d\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf\left\{\tfrac12x^TPx+q^Tx:Ax\in C\right\}=-\infty.\]

notation.meaning: recession cone of the constraint box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession-direction certificate for unboundedness of a feasible convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(C=\{z\in\mathbb R^m:l\leq z\leq u\}\). Suppose \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(Ax_0\in C\). A direction \(d\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\) certifies unboundedness below if \(Pd=0\), \(q^Td<0\), and \(Ad\in\operatorname{rec}(C)\). Componentwise, \((Ad)_i=0\) when both bounds are finite, \((Ad)_i\geq0\) when only the lower bound is finite, \((Ad)_i\leq0\) when only the upper bound is finite, and \((Ad)_i\) is unrestricted when both bounds are infinite. Then \(x_0+td\) is feasible for every \(t\geq0\), and its objective tends to \(-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible convex QP, a nonzero recession direction with zero quadratic curvature and negative linear slope certifies that the objective is unbounded below; its constraint-image direction must point upward at a lower-only bound and downward at an upper-only bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Status

children.title: Ambiguous Certificate Status
children.top_down_role: Cases where numerical evidence does not reliably distinguish infeasibility from unbounded behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous Certificate Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative status when approximate solvability certificates conflict or remain inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_O\), \(T_I\), and \(T_U\) denote the Boolean acceptance tests for approximate optimality, primal infeasibility, and unboundedness, respectively, after unscaling and independent residual verification. Report an ambiguous certificate status if either \(T_I\wedge T_U\) holds, or if a candidate certificate lies inside a prescribed uncertainty band around its acceptance threshold and no mutually exclusive status has been verified. Do not report ambiguity merely because all three tests fail; that case remains an undetermined or iteration-limit status. The ambiguous status carries every candidate certificate and its normalized residuals for later review but asserts none of the corresponding mathematical conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use ambiguity only for conflicting accepted failure certificates or a certificate inside an explicit uncertainty band; it certifies no final solvability conclusion.
assumptions_latex: All tests use original-coordinate quantities and fixed positive tolerances.
The optimality, infeasibility, and unboundedness tests are evaluated independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solver withholds each of the mutually exclusive conclusions represented by \(T_O\), \(T_I\), and \(T_U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role is suitable for an ambiguous-status leaf, but this ambiguity policy is not a standard mathematical certificate and is entirely solver-specific. No source defines the uncertainty band, conflict handling, or distinction from inaccurate and undetermined statuses.

children.title: Solution Unscaling
children.top_down_role: Recovery of primal variables, dual variables, and certificates in original problem units.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Unscaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of original primal and dual variables from diagonal QP scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\succ0\) and \(E\succ0\) be diagonal, and let \(c>0\). Under the scaled data \(\bar P=cDPD\), \(\bar q=cDq\), \(\bar A=EAD\), \(\bar l=El\), and \(\bar u=Eu\), a scaled primal-dual pair \((\bar x,\bar y)\) represents the original pair
\[x=D\bar x,\qquad y=c^{-1}E\bar y.\]
The scaled constraint image \(\bar z=\bar A\bar x\) unscales as \(z=E^{-1}\bar z=Ax\). Any reported solution or certificate must be transformed by these relations before original-coordinate residuals and stopping tolerances are evaluated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Undo diagonal variable, constraint, and objective scaling before reporting primal variables, dual variables, constraint images, or solver status.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) and \(E\) are positive diagonal matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y)=(D\bar x,c^{-1}E\bar y)\) is the original-coordinate primal-dual representation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits solution unscaling, and the formulas are internally consistent for the stated scaling convention. However, no source establishes that this is the convention used by the intended solver or supports the requirement applied to solutions and certificates.

children.title: Residual Reverification
children.top_down_role: Reassessment of reported residuals against the original unscaled QP data.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Reverification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent acceptance testing after transforming a candidate back to original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given scaled output \((\bar x,\bar y)\), first recover \((x,y)\) by the solver's inverse scaling map. Recompute from the original stored data \(z=\Pi_{[l,u]}(Ax)\), \(r_p=Ax-z\), \(r_d=Px+q+A^Ty\), and \(r_n=y-\Pi_{N_{[l,u]}(z)}(y)\). Recompute any infeasibility or recession certificate using original \(A,l,u,P,q\), without reusing scaled residual norms. Accept the proposed status only when every defining original-coordinate inequality meets its prescribed absolute-relative tolerance; otherwise downgrade it to the applicable inaccurate, ambiguous, or undetermined status and retain the recomputed residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After unscaling, recompute every status residual from the original QP data and accept only if the original-coordinate tests pass.
assumptions_latex: The original QP data remain available without scaling overwrite.
The inverse scaling map is nonsingular.
Status tolerances are defined in original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted status satisfies its defining residual tests for the original QP data.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits residual reverification, but its acceptance and downgrade behavior is solver-specific and uncited. The statement also refers generically to recomputing infeasibility and recession certificates without specifying their defining inequalities in this record or through sourced prerequisites.

children.title: Scaling-Induced Status Changes
children.top_down_role: Cases where unscaled accuracy no longer supports the status assigned in scaled coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Induced Status Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status acceptance need not be invariant under finite scaled-coordinate tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Nonsingular diagonal scaling preserves exact feasibility, exact KKT conditions, and exact infeasibility or recession certificates under the corresponding inverse transformations. Finite numerical tests are not generally invariant: for residual transformation \(r=Sr_{\mathrm{sc}}\), a scaled test \(\|r_{\mathrm{sc}}\|\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sc}}\) need not imply \(\|r\|\leq\varepsilon\) unless \(\|S\|\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sc}}\leq\varepsilon\). Consequently, a scaled-coordinate status may change after unscaling and reverification. The final status must be the result of the original-coordinate tests; a disagreement is recorded as scaling-induced rather than silently retaining the scaled status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact statuses survive invertible scaling, but finite-tolerance statuses may change; the original-coordinate reverification determines the reported result.
assumptions_latex: The scaling maps are nonsingular.
Exact objects are transformed consistently.
Numerical statuses use finite tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaled acceptance alone is insufficient whenever \(\|S\|\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sc}}>\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the leaf and correctly distinguishes exact invariance from finite-tolerance acceptance. A source is still required for the residual transformation, chosen norms and tolerances, and the policy that original-coordinate testing determines the final status.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Polishing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained polishing inferred from an approximate box-constrained QP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_x\tfrac12x^TPx+q^Tx\) subject to \(l\leq Ax\leq u\), infer an active index set \(I\) and active values \(b_I\in\{l_I,u_I\}\) from a candidate \((x,y)\) using fixed proximity and multiplier-sign thresholds. Solve the reduced KKT system
\[\begin{pmatrix}P&A_I^T\\A_I&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x^+\\y_I^+\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-q\\b_I\end{pmatrix},\]
set inactive multipliers to zero, and verify all original inequalities, multiplier signs, stationarity, and complementarity. Accept \((x^+,y^+)\) only if verification passes and a prescribed KKT residual merit is smaller than that of \((x,y)\); otherwise retain the original pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infer active bounds, solve the resulting equality-constrained KKT system, and accept the polished point only when feasibility and KKT residuals improve.
assumptions_latex: \(P\succeq0\).
The active-set thresholds are fixed before polishing.
The reduced KKT system is solved or its failure is detected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a verified improved polished pair or the unchanged input pair.

notation.meaning: active constraint rows and selected bound values

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is correct for active-set polishing, but the active-set inference thresholds, multiplier-sign convention, reduced-system construction, and improvement test are implementation-specific and have no cited source.

assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular, \(b\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(w_0\in\mathbb R^n\).
Residuals can be evaluated reliably in precision at least as high as that used for the correction solves.
\(\tau>0\) and \(J\in\mathbb N\) with \(J\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned iterate has minimum recorded residual norm among all iterates actually generated by the refinement procedure.

notation.meaning: linear residual at refinement step j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-correction refinement for a computed QP linear-system solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonsingular matrix \(K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), a right-hand side \(b\in\mathbb R^n\), an initial computed solution \(w_0\in\mathbb R^n\), a tolerance \(\tau>0\), and an iteration limit \(J\in\mathbb N\) with \(J\geq1\), perform at most \(J\) refinement steps. At generated step \(j\), compute \(r_j=b-Kw_j\) in precision at least as high as that used for the solve; stop successfully if \(\|r_j\|\leq\tau(\|b\|+\|K\|\|w_j\|)\); otherwise approximately solve \(K\delta_j=r_j\) using the existing factorization and set \(w_{j+1}=w_j+\delta_j\). Stop without accepting a new correction if a residual is nonfinite, a correction solve fails, or the residual fails the prescribed decrease test. Return the generated iterate having the smallest recorded residual norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve for a residual correction, update the linear-system solution, and return the actually generated iterate with the smallest recorded residual, stopping on convergence or a detected numerical failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-System Iterative Refinement

children.title: Polishing Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Singularity, inconsistent active sets, instability, and accuracy loss during polishing.

knowledge_statements.title: Polishing Failure Modes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural and numerical conditions under which active-set polishing must be rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inferred active matrix \(A_I\), polishing fails if the reduced KKT matrix \(K_I=\begin{psmallmatrix}P&A_I^T\\A_I&0\end{psmallmatrix}\) is singular or numerically unusable, if its solve produces nonfinite values, or if the candidate violates any inactive bound or active-multiplier sign condition. It also fails when the verified original-coordinate KKT residual is not smaller than the pre-polishing residual. Singular failure can arise from dependent active rows together with insufficient curvature of \(P\) on \(\ker A_I\); verification failure can arise from an incorrectly inferred active set. In every case, the polishing candidate is discarded rather than replacing a valid unpolished iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject polishing for singular or ill-conditioned reduced systems, nonfinite solves, incorrect active sets, feasibility violations, or failure to improve verified KKT residuals.
assumptions_latex: An unpolished candidate and inferred active set \(I\) are available.
Candidate acceptance is checked using original QP data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A failed polishing candidate cannot replace the stored unpolished solution.

notation.meaning: null space of the active constraint matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind exactly fits the leaf, and the listed structural failures are plausible. No source supports this complete failure taxonomy, the numerical-usability threshold, the multiplier-sign convention, or the mandatory residual-improvement and fallback policy.

children.title: Unpolished-Solution Fallback
children.top_down_role: Acceptance and reporting policies that retain the base solver solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Unpolished-Solution Fallback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance policy when a polishing step fails or degrades an operator-splitting QP iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex QP \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TPx+q^Tx\) subject to \(l\le Ax\le u\), retain the pre-polishing iterate \((x^k,z^k,y^k)\). Attempt polishing to obtain \((\widehat x,\widehat z,\widehat y)\). Accept the polished point only if the polishing solve succeeds and its normalized primal-dual residual measure \(R(\widehat x,\widehat z,\widehat y)\) is finite and no larger than \(R(x^k,z^k,y^k)\). Otherwise return the retained iterate. Report it as solved only when \(R(x^k,z^k,y^k)\le\varepsilon\); otherwise return the applicable inaccurate or iteration-limit status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain the original iterate, accept polishing only when it succeeds without worsening residuals, and preserve the original termination status otherwise.
assumptions_latex: \(P=P^T\succeq0\) and \(l\le u\) componentwise.
\(R\) is the solver's finite normalized KKT-residual measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polishing failure cannot replace the retained iterate by a point having a larger measured residual.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits this fallback-policy leaf, but no citation supports the proposed residual-comparison acceptance rule or status handling. The plain statement also says to preserve the original termination status, whereas the LaTeX statement assigns solved, inaccurate, or iteration-limit status from the retained iterate and tolerance. A solver-specific authoritative source is required to determine the intended policy.

children.title: Alternate Refinement Fallback
children.top_down_role: Recovery through iterative refinement, regularized polishing, or backend substitution.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternate Refinement Fallback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized iterative refinement after failure of an active-set polishing system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the polishing equations be \(Kw=b\), and suppose their direct solution fails, is nonfinite, or does not reduce \(\|Kw-b\|\). Choose \(\delta>0\), form a nonsingular regularization \(K_\delta\), initialize \(w^0\) with the unpolished primal-dual iterate, and repeat \(K_\delta d^j=b-Kw^j\), \(w^{j+1}=w^j+d^j\) for at most \(J\) steps. Accept the first \(w^{j+1}\) satisfying the solver's feasibility and stationarity tolerances and decreasing the original residual; if none exists, return the unpolished iterate unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On polishing failure, try bounded regularized iterative refinement; accept only a residual-reducing KKT point, otherwise keep the unpolished solution.
assumptions_latex: \(K_\delta\) is nonsingular for the selected \(\delta>0\).
Each correction equation is solved to finite numerical accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fallback returns either an acceptable refined point or the unchanged pre-polishing iterate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the alternate-refinement fallback leaf, but the construction of the nonsingular regularization, the correction-solve accuracy, and the feasibility and stationarity acceptance tests are not specified sufficiently to identify a standard method. No cited source supports this particular refinement variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm initialization for a sequence of related box-form convex QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a new QP \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TPx+q^Tx\) subject to \(l\le Ax\le u\), take a previous solution estimate \((x^-,z^-,y^-)\). Initialize \(x^0=x^-\), \(z^0=\Pi_{[l,u]}(z^-)\), and \(y^0=y^-\), converting \(y^-\) if the new solve uses different dual scaling. Start the ordinary primal-dual iteration from this triple and apply its usual stopping test. If no compatible previous estimate exists, use the solver's cold-start initialization. Warm starting changes only initialization, not the QP or its termination criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize a related QP from the prior primal, projected constraint, and compatibly scaled dual estimates, while retaining normal stopping tests.
assumptions_latex: The new and previous problems have compatible primal and constraint dimensions.
The underlying iteration permits arbitrary finite initial iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The warm-started run solves the new QP under the same convergence and stopping conditions as a cold start.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the componentwise interval box.
Previous primal, constraint, and dual estimates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate for a warm-start procedure, but no source supports the particular projection and dual-conversion policy. The phrase converting the dual estimate when scaling differs does not define the scaling map, so the mathematically intended initialization cannot be verified without a solver-specific citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Caching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of a direct linear-system factorization across repeated splitting iterations or QP solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every required linear solve has coefficient matrix \(K\) and varying right-hand side \(b^j\). Compute a permutation and factorization of \(K\) once, store the factors, and obtain each solution \(w^j\) by triangular substitutions satisfying \(Kw^j=b^j\). Reuse is valid while all entries and solver parameters determining \(K\) remain unchanged. If any such quantity changes, invalidate and recompute the numeric factors; if only \(b^j\) changes, retain them. Thus one factorization serves all compatible solves without changing their exact-arithmetic solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor a fixed system matrix once and reuse its factors for changing right-hand sides, invalidating the cache whenever matrix-defining data change.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is nonsingular and the stored factorization is numerically usable.
Repeated solves share exactly the same coefficient matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each cached solve has the same exact-arithmetic solution as refactorizing \(K\) for that right-hand side.

notation.meaning: Fixed linear-system or KKT coefficient matrix.
Right-hand side for solve index j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits this implementation procedure, and the fixed-matrix exact-arithmetic equivalence is mathematically standard. However, the record has no citation with an inspectable locator supporting the QP-solver caching and invalidation policy, so it cannot be accepted under the evidence contract.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Structure Numeric Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Updating QP numerical values while preserving dimensions and sparsity patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the dimensions and stored sparsity patterns of \(P\) and \(A\). For each new instance, overwrite only the permitted numerical entries of \(P,A,q,l,u\). Reuse index maps, permutations, symbolic factorization, and allocated workspaces. If \(P\), \(A\), or a matrix-defining algorithm parameter changes numerically, recompute the affected numeric factorization before solving; changes confined to \(q,l,u\) require only right-hand-side and bound updates. Reject an update that introduces a nonzero outside the declared patterns or changes dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse symbolic structure and memory across value updates, but refresh numeric factors when matrix coefficients change and reject structural changes.
assumptions_latex: The declared sparsity patterns and dimensions remain fixed.
Updated data continue to define an admissible convex QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Structural preprocessing remains reusable, whereas numeric factors are reused only when their defining matrix is unchanged.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits a numeric-update interface, but no source supports the asserted reuse and invalidation rules. The matrix-defining algorithm parameters and the meaning of an affected numeric factorization are solver dependent and must be established by a specific implementation or method reference.

knowledge_statements.title: Batched Solve Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Columnwise equivalence of batched and individual solves sharing one coefficient matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}\) be nonsingular and let \(B=[b^1\ \cdots\ b^s]\in\mathbb R^{d\times s}\). A batched interface returns \(W=[w^1\ \cdots\ w^s]\) from the block equation \(KW=B\), using one cached factorization or one common matrix-operator setup. This equation is equivalent columnwise to \(Kw^i=b^i\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,s\}\). Per-instance residuals and statuses must be computed separately, so failure of one column need not alter the mathematical result for another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve several right-hand sides against one shared matrix; each output column equals its corresponding independent solve and receives its own status.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is nonsingular and common to all batch members.
Batch members have compatible dimensions and numerical scaling conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(KW=B\) if and only if \(Kw^i=b^i\) for every batch column \(i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is a reasonable kind for the block equation and its columnwise interpretation. The algebraic equivalence is standard, but the separate residual and status semantics are interface claims not implied by the equation and have no supporting citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Matrix-Vector Workloads
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration arithmetic and storage for matrix-free sparse first-order QP iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a first-order iteration for \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TPx+q^Tx\) subject to \(l\le Ax\le u\) that evaluates \(Px\), \(Ax\), \(A^Ty\), vector updates, and componentwise box projections, without factorization or matrix fill-in. With sparse compressed storage, one iteration uses \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(P)+\operatorname{nnz}(A)+n+m)\) arithmetic operations and the same asymptotic storage, including vectors. The bound excludes preprocessing and stopping checks requiring additional global operations, and assumes each stored matrix entry is accessed only a constant number of times.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free sparse QP iteration costs linear work and storage in the stored nonzeros plus primal and constraint dimensions.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) use sparse compressed storage.
The iteration performs only a constant number of listed products and vector kernels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The per-iteration work and storage are \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(P)+\operatorname{nnz}(A)+n+m)\).

notation.meaning: Number of explicitly stored nonzeros of matrix M.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind exactly fits the leaf. The arithmetic bound follows under the stated constant-kernel access model, but no cited source supports the workload model, and the phrase the same asymptotic storage is ambiguous about whether immutable matrix storage and all working vectors are both included. A specific matrix-free QP reference is required.

knowledge_statements.title: GPU First-Order QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: GPU-oriented primal-dual iteration for a convex QP with box-form constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[l,u]\), choose \(\tau,\sigma>0\) and \(\theta\in[0,1]\), and initialize finite \(x^0,y^0\) with \(\bar x^0=x^0\). On the device compute \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\sigma A\bar x^k-\sigma\Pi_C(\sigma^{-1}y^k+A\bar x^k)\), \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\tau(Px^k+q+A^Ty^{k+1})\), and \(\bar x^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\theta(x^{k+1}-x^k)\). Implement matrix products as sparse or dense GPU kernels and projections as componentwise kernels. Stop at a residual tolerance or iteration cap and return \((x^k,y^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Execute a primal-dual QP iteration through GPU matrix-vector and projection kernels, stopping by residual tolerance or a fixed iteration cap.
assumptions_latex: \(P=P^T\succeq0\), \(C=[l,u]\neq\varnothing\), and a saddle point exists.
The step sizes satisfy a convergence condition appropriate to the chosen primal-dual scheme.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed updates expose the iteration as matrix-vector, vector, and componentwise projection kernels suitable for GPU execution.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is suitable for this GPU-method leaf, but the displayed explicit primal step with the quadratic gradient requires a precise convergence condition involving the smooth term and the operator. Saying only that an appropriate condition holds is not independently checkable, and no source identifies or validates this exact primal-dual variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed First-Order QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-partitioned distributed primal-dual solution of a convex box-constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(A=[A_1^T\ \cdots\ A_p^T]^T\), \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_p\), and \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_p)\) across \(p\) workers. Worker \(i\) updates \(y_i^{k+1}=y_i^k+\sigma A_i\bar x^k-\sigma\Pi_{C_i}(\sigma^{-1}y_i^k+A_i\bar x^k)\). An all-reduce forms \(g^k=\sum_{i=1}^pA_i^Ty_i^{k+1}\), after which each replica computes \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\tau(Px^k+q+g^k)\) and extrapolates \(\bar x^{k+1}\). Stop when aggregated residuals meet tolerance or the iteration cap is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distribute constraint blocks and dual updates, aggregate their transpose products, and update a shared primal vector until convergence or an iteration cap.
assumptions_latex: The constraint set is block separable as \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_p\).
Collective reductions return the exact sum in the idealized arithmetic model.
Step sizes satisfy the selected primal-dual method's convergence condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The distributed aggregate \(g^k\) equals \(A^Ty^{k+1}\), so the primal update matches the centralized iteration.

notation.meaning: Constraint matrix, feasible-set, and dual block on worker i.
All-reduced dual contribution to the primal gradient.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the distributed-solver leaf, and the block identity for the all-reduced transpose products is correct under the stated partition. Nevertheless, the underlying primal-dual method and its step-size condition remain unspecified, and no citation supports the exact distributed update and stopping policy.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Memory Deployment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static memory bound for embedded first-order QP execution with fixed structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(n,m\), the sparsity patterns of \(P,A\), and the maximum iteration count. Store matrix data, scaling data, iterates, residuals, and all temporary vectors in statically allocated arrays whose sizes are determined before execution. A matrix-free implementation using a constant number of primal and constraint vectors then requires \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(P)+\operatorname{nnz}(A)+n+m)\) words of persistent and working memory. Because iterations overwrite these arrays and create no dimension-dependent objects, runtime allocation is unnecessary and memory consumption is independent of the number of iterations executed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preallocate all fixed-structure matrix and vector storage; execution then uses linear memory in nonzeros and dimensions, independent of iteration count.
assumptions_latex: Problem dimensions and sparsity patterns are fixed before deployment.
The iteration uses a constant number of work vectors and performs no factorization fill-in.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Runtime memory is \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(P)+\operatorname{nnz}(A)+n+m)\) and does not grow with the iteration count.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind is appropriate. The bound is plausible for the explicitly restricted matrix-free implementation, but no source supports the embedded deployment model, and the wording does not distinguish persistent input storage from transient working memory. A cited implementation or complexity analysis is required.
