knowledge_statements.title: Division-Free Post-Factorization Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replacing runtime divisions by precomputed reciprocals in fixed linear solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a fixed nonsingular triangular factorization, precompute the reciprocal of every nonunit diagonal entry during setup and store it with the factors. In each forward or backward substitution, replace division by a diagonal value \(d_i\) with multiplication by its stored reciprocal \(r_i=d_i^{-1}\); apply any diagonal factor similarly. All remaining solve operations are additions and multiplications. Consequently, after factorization and reciprocal setup, repeated linear solves contain no arithmetic division, provided no pivot, scaling, or matrix coefficient changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precompute factor-diagonal reciprocals so repeated triangular solves use only additions and multiplications while the factorization remains unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Every diagonal divisor \(d_i\) is nonzero.
Factors, pivots, and scaling remain fixed after setup.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing each \(v/d_i\) by \(v r_i\), where \(r_i=d_i^{-1}\), yields the same exact-arithmetic substitution without runtime division.

notation.meaning: Nonzero diagonal divisor in a triangular or diagonal solve.
Precomputed reciprocal of the diagonal divisor.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits this execution transformation, and the exact-arithmetic substitution identity is correctly limited to fixed nonzero divisors. No source supports the deployment claim, however, and multiplication by a stored rounded reciprocal is generally not floating-point equivalent to division; an authoritative source must establish the intended arithmetic and implementation scope.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Latency Solve Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic latency cap obtained from bounded setup, iteration, and output work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a fixed iteration cap \(N_{\max}\). Suppose setup takes at most \(T_{\mathrm{set}}\), every iteration—including scheduled residual checks—takes at most \(T_{\mathrm{iter}}\), and output handling takes at most \(T_{\mathrm{out}}\). Execute no more than \(N_{\max}\) iterations and return immediately upon meeting the tolerance; otherwise return the final or best retained iterate with an iteration-limit status. The solve latency is bounded by \(T_{\mathrm{set}}+N_{\max}T_{\mathrm{iter}}+T_{\mathrm{out}}\). This deadline guarantee certifies execution time, not attainment of the requested optimization accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cap iterations and bound every execution phase to obtain deterministic latency; if tolerance is missed, return an explicitly limited-status iterate.
assumptions_latex: Setup, each iteration, and output handling have valid worst-case execution-time bounds.
The implementation performs no unbounded retries, allocation, or data-dependent refinement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{solve}}\le T_{\mathrm{set}}+N_{\max}T_{\mathrm{iter}}+T_{\mathrm{out}}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits this terminal container, and the displayed latency inequality follows from the stated worst-case execution-time assumptions. Those bounds and the absence of unbounded runtime behavior are implementation-specific premises, however, and no real-time solver or WCET source is cited to support them.

knowledge_statements.title: Code-Generated QP Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Offline synthesis and bounded online execution for parametric convex QPs with fixed sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the template \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TPx+q(\theta)^Tx\) subject to \(l(\theta)\le Ax\le u(\theta)\), offline synthesis fixes scaling, storage, arithmetic precision, stopping tolerances, and an iteration cap \(K_{\max}\); generates allocation-free linear-algebra and residual routines; and precomputes every parameter-independent factorization. Online, load \(\theta\), update parameter-dependent numerical data, execute the generated recurrence \(z^{k+1}=T_\theta(z^k)\), and stop at the first \(k\le K_{\max}\) satisfying the prescribed primal and dual residual tests. Return the associated primal-dual iterate and a status indicating convergence or iteration-cap termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate fixed-storage solver code and invariant factorizations offline; online, update parameters and run a capped recurrence until residual tolerances or the iteration limit is reached.
assumptions_latex: \(P=P^T\succeq0\) and the QP dimensions and sparsity pattern are fixed.
\(q(\theta),l(\theta),u(\theta)\) are available at runtime.
Generated arithmetic and workspace fit the deployment target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{output}(\theta)=(x^k,y^k,\mathrm{status})\) for some \(k\le K_{\max}\), without online dynamic allocation.

notation.meaning: combined solver state at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the code-generated solver container and is internally coherent, but it makes nontrivial claims about offline factorization, allocation-free execution, residual termination, and bounded online iterations without any inspectable citation. An authoritative code-generation or embedded-QP source with a specific section is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-to-Moderate Accuracy Large-Scale Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection condition for sparse or matrix-free first-order QP solution at moderate accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex QP, define the large-scale moderate-accuracy predicate by \[\mathcal R_{\mathrm{LM}}:=\bigl(M_{\mathrm{fac}}>M_{\mathrm{avail}}\ \lor\ F_{\mathrm{fac}}>F_{\max}\bigr)\ \land\ \epsilon_{\mathrm{tar}}\ge\epsilon_{\mathrm{mod}},\] where \(M_{\mathrm{fac}}\) and \(F_{\mathrm{fac}}\) estimate direct-factorization memory and fill, while \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{tar}}\) is the requested normalized residual tolerance. When \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{LM}}\) holds and matrix-vector products with the QP operators are available, select a first-order splitting or projected method whose iterations avoid dense factorizations and terminate using normalized primal and dual residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a sparse or matrix-free first-order method when direct factorization exceeds memory or fill budgets and only moderate normalized residual accuracy is required.
assumptions_latex: \(P=P^T\succeq0\).
\(M_{\mathrm{avail}},F_{\max},\epsilon_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) are deployment thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{LM}}\) identifies the low-to-moderate-accuracy large-scale selection regime.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: resource-budget and requested-accuracy predicates conventionally define solver-selection regimes
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the large-scale moderate-accuracy regime, but the proposed resource-and-accuracy predicate is an application-specific solver-selection rule rather than a source-independent mathematical fact. No citation supports the thresholds or the resulting method recommendation.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Accuracy Polished Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection condition for active-set polishing after a first-order QP solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\hat x,\hat y)\) be a first-order primal-dual iterate and let \(\widehat I\) be the constraints inferred active within threshold \(\tau_a\). The polished regime holds when \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{tar}}<\epsilon_{\mathrm{fo}}\), the residuals of \((\hat x,\hat y)\) are small enough to stabilize \(\widehat I\), and the KKT matrix \[K_{\widehat I}=\begin{bmatrix}P&A_{\widehat I}^T\\A_{\widehat I}&0\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular or admits a controlled regularized solve. Solve the equality-constrained KKT system on \(\widehat I\), then accept the polished point only if feasibility and the KKT residual both improve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polish a moderate first-order solution when higher accuracy is required, its active set is stable, and the reduced KKT system can be solved reliably.
assumptions_latex: \(P=P^T\succeq0\).
\(\epsilon_{\mathrm{tar}},\epsilon_{\mathrm{fo}},\tau_a>0\).
An active-set estimate \(\widehat I\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime permits KKT polishing, subject to an explicit residual-improvement acceptance test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition has the correct role for the polished regime, and the active-set KKT formulation is plausible. However, active-set stability, controlled regularization, and the residual-improvement acceptance rule require an authoritative polishing source with a precise locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Repeated Fixed-Structure Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Amortized selection condition for QP sequences sharing dimensions and sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(N\) convex QPs having fixed \(P\), \(A\), dimensions, sparsity, scaling, and solver settings, while \(q_j,l_j,u_j\) may vary. The repeated fixed-structure regime holds when reusable preprocessing exists and \[\frac{C_{\mathrm{setup}}}{N}+C_{\mathrm{update}}+C_{\mathrm{solve}}<C_{\mathrm{independent}},\] where the right side is the average cost of independently constructing and solving an instance. In this regime, perform symbolic analysis and parameter-independent factorization once, update only numerical vectors or permitted matrix entries, and warm-start each instance when an informative prior solution is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse preprocessing, invariant factors, and warm starts across QPs with fixed structure when their amortized per-instance cost beats independent solution.
assumptions_latex: \(P=P^T\succeq0\) and all instances share a fixed structural template.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed amortization inequality defines when fixed-structure reuse is computationally preferable.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: amortized setup-cost comparison is the conventional criterion for repeated fixed-structure computation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the repeated fixed-structure regime, but the amortized-cost inequality and the claimed reusable operations are not supported by an inspectable source. The reference to updating permitted matrix entries also extends beyond the stated case in which P and A are fixed and should be reconciled when sourced.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned or Degenerate Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral and active-constraint condition identifying numerically difficult convex QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a candidate active set \(I\), let \(Z\) span \(\ker A_I\), define \(H_I=Z^TPZ\), and let \(\sigma_{\min}(A_I)\) be the smallest singular value of the active-constraint matrix. For user-scaled thresholds \(\kappa_{\max}\) and \(\tau_{\mathrm{rank}}\), the QP is in the ill-conditioned or degenerate regime when \[\kappa_+(H_I)>\kappa_{\max}\quad\lor\quad\sigma_{\min}(A_I)\le\tau_{\mathrm{rank}},\] where \(\kappa_+\) is the ratio of largest to smallest positive eigenvalue. The regime calls for scaling, rank-revealing analysis, regularization, and guarded termination diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flag the difficult regime when reduced curvature has excessive positive-eigenvalue condition number or active constraints are numerically rank deficient.
assumptions_latex: \(P=P^T\succeq0\).
\(I\) is a candidate active set and \(Z\) has orthonormal columns.
\(\kappa_{\max}>1\) and \(\tau_{\mathrm{rank}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The spectral disjunction defines the ill-conditioned or degenerate solver-selection regime.

notation.meaning: reduced Hessian on active feasible directions

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reduced-Hessian conditioning and active-Jacobian rank are standard QP difficulty diagnostics
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Reduced-Hessian conditioning and active-constraint rank fit this regime, but the formula does not define kappa_+(H_I) when H_I has fewer than two positive eigenvalues, including a completely flat reduced Hessian. The intended treatment of such degenerate cases and the scale-dependent thresholds require a source before the mathematical condition can be fixed reliably.

children.title: Curvature Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators of weak, indefinite, or poorly scaled quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-Hessian spectral certificate for curvature along locally feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an active set \(I\), choose an orthonormal basis \(Z\) of \(\ker A_I\) and form the reduced Hessian \(H_I=Z^TPZ\). Certified spectral bounds \(\underline\lambda\le\lambda_{\min}(H_I)\) and \(\lambda_{\max}(H_I)\le\overline\lambda\) imply: positive curvature when \(\underline\lambda>0\); semidefinite curvature when \(\underline\lambda\ge0\); and a negative-curvature feasible direction when a computed \(d\ne0\) satisfies \(A_Id=0\) and \(d^TPd<0\). The interval \([\underline\lambda,\overline\lambda]\) is therefore a verifiable local curvature diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use certified eigenvalue bounds of the reduced Hessian to distinguish positive, semidefinite, and negative curvature along active feasible directions.
assumptions_latex: \(Z^TZ=I\) and \(A_IZ=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounds certify curvature of \(P\) restricted to \(\ker A_I\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Rayleigh quotients and reduced-Hessian eigenvalue bounds directly characterize restricted quadratic curvature
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the diagnostic container, and the reduced-Hessian curvature implications are mathematically standard. Nevertheless, the record supplies no cited source or inspectable locator for the certified spectral-bound formulation.

children.title: Flat-Direction Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators of objective directions with negligible curvature or weak constraint control.

knowledge_statements.title: Flat-Direction Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate of exact or numerical flatness on active feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker A_I\), and set \(H_I=Z^TPZ\). An exact flat direction is certified by a vector \(v\ne0\) satisfying \(H_Iv=0\); its full-space direction \(d=Zv\) obeys \(A_Id=0\) and \(d^TPd=0\). For scale \(s_H=\max\{1,\lVert H_I\rVert_2\}\), numerical flatness at tolerance \(\tau_f\) is indicated when \(\lVert H_Iv\rVert_2\le\tau_fs_H\lVert v\rVert_2\). The linear term \(q^Td\) then distinguishes locally neutral from linearly improving or worsening motion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null or near-null reduced-Hessian vector identifies a feasible flat direction; the linear term determines behavior along that direction.
assumptions_latex: \(P=P^T\succeq0\).
\(Z^TZ=I\) and \(A_IZ=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual test certifies exact flatness when zero and diagnoses numerical flatness when below the scaled threshold.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: null vectors and scaled residuals are standard exact and numerical singularity certificates
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact null-vector statement is a valid certificate and the numerical residual is a suitable diagnostic, but no source supports the scaled tolerance formulation or its interpretation. A numerical linear algebra or optimization reference with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Near-Semidefinite Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes where small curvature is difficult to distinguish from exact flatness.

assumptions_latex: \(P=P^T\succeq0\), \(Z^TZ=I\), and the columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker A_I\).
\(0<\tau_{\mathrm{psd}}<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled eigenvalue test defines the near-semidefinite diagnostic regime.

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis for the null space of the active-constraint matrix

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scale-relative minimum-eigenvalue tests conventionally diagnose nearly singular positive-semidefinite reduced curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware condition for nearly singular positive-semidefinite reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the reduced Hessian \(H_I=Z^TPZ\), let \(\lambda_{\min}^+(H_I)\) denote its smallest positive eigenvalue and define \(s_H=\max\{1,\lVert H_I\rVert_2\}\). Given \(0<\tau_{\mathrm{psd}}<1\), the near-semidefinite regime is \[0<\lambda_{\min}^+(H_I)\le\tau_{\mathrm{psd}}s_H,\] or, when computed eigenvalues are uncertain, a certified enclosure for \(\lambda_{\min}(H_I)\) intersects \([ -\tau_{\mathrm{psd}}s_H,\tau_{\mathrm{psd}}s_H]\). This condition separates resolvable positive curvature from curvature that is numerically indistinguishable from zero at the chosen scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced positive-semidefinite curvature is near singular when its smallest positive eigenvalue is tiny relative to scale or its certified minimum-eigenvalue interval intersects a scale-relative neighborhood of zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Semidefinite Regimes

children.title: Constraint-Dependence Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators of redundant, nearly dependent, or rank-deficient constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Dependence Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical certificate of linear dependence among candidate active constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the candidate active-constraint matrix \(A_I\), compute a nonzero vector \(w\) and the scaled dependence residual \[\delta_{\mathrm{dep}}=\frac{\lVert A_I^Tw\rVert_2}{\lVert A_I\rVert_2\lVert w\rVert_2}.\] Exact dependence is certified when \(A_I^Tw=0\). Numerical dependence at tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{dep}}\) is indicated when \(\delta_{\mathrm{dep}}\le\tau_{\mathrm{dep}}\), equivalently when the smallest singular value of \(A_I\) is small relative to \(\lVert A_I\rVert_2\). The coefficients in \(w\) identify the dependent combination of active constraint normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small normalized residual for a nonzero combination of active constraint normals diagnoses dependence and identifies the participating constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(w\ne0\) and \(\tau_{\mathrm{dep}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_I^Tw=0\) certifies exact dependence; \(\delta_{\mathrm{dep}}\le\tau_{\mathrm{dep}}\) diagnoses numerical dependence.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a nonzero left-null vector is an exact linear-dependence certificate, with its normalized residual giving the numerical analogue
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A nonzero left-null vector is an exact dependence certificate, so the selected knowledge kind fits. The normalized approximate-dependence threshold and its claimed equivalence to a small singular value need an inspectable numerical linear algebra source, particularly because an arbitrary computed w need not attain the smallest singular value.

children.title: Degeneracy Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators of nonunique multipliers, weak activity, or unstable active structures.

assumptions_latex: \((x,y)\) uses a specified primal-dual and multiplier-sign convention.
Each row \(a_i^T\) has finite lower and upper bounds \(l_i\) and \(u_i\).
\(\tau_a,\tau_r,\tau_y>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rank-deficiency or weak-activity disjunction defines the degeneracy diagnostic.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: LICQ failure and small active multipliers are conventional rank and weak-activity diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set condition detecting numerical linear-dependence or weakly active constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a primal-dual candidate \((x,y)\), define the numerical activity set by \[I=\left\{i:\min\left\{\lvert a_i^Tx-l_i\rvert,\lvert u_i-a_i^Tx\rvert\right\}\le\tau_a\right\}.\] The candidate is diagnostically degenerate when either \[\sigma_{\min}(A_I)\le\tau_r\lVert A_I\rVert_2\] or an index \(i\in I\) corresponding to an inequality bound has \(\lvert y_i\rvert\le\tau_y\). The first condition diagnoses numerical linear dependence among active normals; the second diagnoses weak activity and possible active-set ambiguity. Both tests must use the solver's row scaling and multiplier convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagnose degeneracy when the normals of constraints close to a bound are numerically dependent or a bound identified as active has a nearly zero multiplier, making the active set ambiguous.
knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy Diagnostics

children.title: Rank-Revealing Indicators
children.top_down_role: Numerical evidence used to separate structural dependence from conditioning artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealing Indicators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SVD and pivoted-QR indicators for numerical rank of active constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_I=U\Sigma V^T\) have singular values \(\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_p\ge0\). At relative threshold \(\tau_r\), its numerical rank is represented by \[r_{\tau}=\#\{j:\sigma_j>\tau_r\sigma_1\}.\] Alternatively, a column-pivoted QR factorization \(A_I^T\Pi=QR\) indicates rank \(r\) when \(|R_{rr}|>\tau_r|R_{11}|\) and \(|R_{r+1,r+1}|\le\tau_r|R_{11}|\). A large gap \(\sigma_r/\sigma_{r+1}\), or the analogous pivot gap, strengthens the separation between retained and dependent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thresholded singular values or pivoted-QR diagonals estimate active-constraint rank; a large adjacent gap strengthens the diagnosis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The threshold counts and adjacent gaps are rank-revealing indicators for \(A_I\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: thresholded SVD and pivoted-QR diagonals are standard numerical-rank representations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the rank-indicator container, and thresholded singular values are standard. The pivoted-QR diagonal test is an indicator rather than a general rank certificate and needs a numerical linear algebra citation with a specific section or theorem; none is supplied.

children.title: Stagnation Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators of persistent residual or objective plateaus.

assumptions_latex: \(w\ge1\), \(0<\eta<1\), \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}>0\), and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The windowed predicate diagnoses insufficient progress while the iterate remains outside the stopping tolerance.

notation.meaning: normalized optimality measure at iteration k
primal residual, dual residual, and nonnegative gap measure at iteration k
positive denominator floor used in the relative-progress test

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: rolling relative residual decrease is a conventional operational definition of iterative stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed residual condition detecting lack of meaningful iterative progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k=\max\{r_{p,k}/s_p,r_{d,k}/s_d,g_k/s_g\}\) be a nonnegative normalized optimality measure, with unavailable components omitted. For a window length \(w\ge1\), progress threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\), stopping floor \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}>0\), and denominator floor \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}>0\), declare stagnation at iteration \(k\ge w\) when \[m_k>\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}\quad\text{and}\quad\frac{m_{k-w}-m_k}{\max\{m_{k-w},\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}\}}<\eta.\] Requiring this predicate for several consecutive windows suppresses isolated nonmonotone steps; the diagnostic does not itself distinguish poor scaling, ill-conditioning, or an unsuitable parameter choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Declare stagnation when normalized optimality remains above tolerance yet improves by less than a prescribed fraction over a rolling iteration window.
knowledge_statements.title: Stagnation Diagnostics

children.title: Chattering Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators of rapid switching among active constraints or local solver states.

assumptions_latex: A first-order method generates iterates \(z^k\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and binary active-set indicators \(a^k\in\{0,1\}^m\).
A residual map \(R:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^q\) is fixed, and \(\|R(z^k)\|\) measures stationarity and feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conditions diagnose chattering rather than convergence.

notation.meaning: iterate and active-set indicator at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational asymptotic diagnostic for repeated active-set switching near an unresolved QP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Chattering is diagnosed when there exist \(\delta>0\), \(\varepsilon>0\), an index \(k_0\), and a constraint index \(i\) such that, for every \(N\ge k_0\), some \(k\ge N\) satisfies \(a_i^{k+1}\ne a_i^k\), while
\[
\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|\le\delta,\qquad \|R(z^k)\|\ge\varepsilon.
\]
Thus the same activity decision changes infinitely often despite small iterate motion, and the residual remains bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chattering occurs when an activity decision keeps switching despite small iterate changes, while a fixed optimality or feasibility residual does not approach zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Chattering Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the chattering leaf and is internally quantified, but the particular combination of infinite active-set switching, bounded step size, and nonvanishing residual is an operational diagnostic requiring a supporting source.

children.title: Oscillation Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators of recurring iterate, residual, or parameter cycles.

assumptions_latex: A first-order method generates iterates \(z^k\in\mathbb{R}^d\).
A fixed residual vector \(r^k=R(z^k)\in\mathbb{R}^q\) is used throughout the run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The repeated separated subsequences diagnose nonvanishing oscillation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subsequence-based diagnostic for persistent residual cycling, distinct from active-set chattering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Persistent oscillation is diagnosed when there exist increasing index sequences \(k_j\) and \(\ell_j\), vectors \(u,v\in\mathbb{R}^q\), and \(\eta>0\) such that
\[
r^{k_j}\to u,\qquad r^{\ell_j}\to v,\qquad \|u-v\|\ge\eta,
\]
and \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|r^k\|>0\). The residual trajectory therefore has at least two separated accumulation points and does not converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oscillation is present when residuals repeatedly approach two separated limiting states and remain bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Oscillation Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subsequence condition is mathematically coherent and distinct from active-set chattering, but no source supports adopting this particular residual-accumulation criterion as an oscillation diagnostic.

assumptions_latex: All solvers are evaluated on the same QP data and use residuals expressed in the original, unscaled variables.
Positive reference scales are chosen independently of the solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized residual pair is dimensionless and comparable across solvers and problem units.

notation.meaning: primal and dual residual vectors in original coordinates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionless comparison rule for primal and dual QP residuals after undoing internal solver scaling.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.2 Steepest Descent and Scaling p. 39
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Residual reports are scaling-comparable when each solver returns residuals to the original coordinates and applies the common normalization
\[
\widehat r_{\mathrm p}=\frac{\|r_{\mathrm p}\|}{s_{\mathrm p}},\qquad
\widehat r_{\mathrm d}=\frac{\|r_{\mathrm d}\|}{s_{\mathrm d}},
\]
where \(s_{\mathrm p}>0\) and \(s_{\mathrm d}>0\) depend only on the QP instance and declared norm. Stopping and ranking must use the same tolerances on \((\widehat r_{\mathrm p},\widehat r_{\mathrm d})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solver residuals are comparable only after conversion to original coordinates and normalization by common, positive, instance-dependent reference scales.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Scaling Comparability

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3.2 Steepest Descent and Scaling p. 39
source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited steepest-descent scaling section does not clearly support the proposed cross-solver QP benchmarking rule. The reference scales also must be specified to have the corresponding residual units before dimensionlessness follows.

children.title: Setup-Time Cost
children.top_down_role: Pre-solve analysis, factorization, compilation, and initialization time in solver comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Setup-Time Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock accounting definition for one QP solve, excluding model construction outside the solver boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a declared solver boundary, define
\[
T_{\mathrm{setup}}=t_{\mathrm{ready}}-t_{\mathrm{start}}.
\]
This cost includes solver-owned data conversion, equilibration, symbolic analysis, numerical factorization, preconditioner construction, and accelerator initialization performed before iteration one. It excludes iteration work and any model construction explicitly outside the boundary. A benchmark must state whether reusable setup artifacts are rebuilt or retrieved from cache.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Setup cost is elapsed time from entering solver preprocessing until iteration one can begin, under an explicitly declared cache policy.
assumptions_latex: A solver performs preprocessing before its first numerical iteration.
Elapsed time is measured with a fixed clock and synchronization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Setup-time cost is \(T_{\mathrm{setup}}=t_{\mathrm{ready}}-t_{\mathrm{start}}\).

notation.meaning: time when the first iteration can begin

children.title: Iteration-Time Cost
children.top_down_role: Steady-state time per iteration or per numerical kernel invocation.

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration-Time Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock accounting for repeated numerical updates after solver setup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\tau_k\ge0\) be the synchronized elapsed time of iteration \(k\). The iteration-time cost of a run is
\[
T_{\mathrm{iter}}(K)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\tau_k,
\]
reported together with \(K\) and either \(T_{\mathrm{iter}}(K)/K\) or a declared robust statistic of \(\{\tau_k\}_{k=1}^K\). Residual evaluation required by the stopping rule is included; preprocessing assigned to setup is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteration cost is the total synchronized duration of executed updates, including required stopping tests and excluding declared setup work.
assumptions_latex: A run executes \(K\ge1\) numerical iterations after setup.
Iteration timestamps use the same clock and synchronization convention as setup timing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Iteration cost is reported by total time and a declared per-iteration statistic.

children.title: Setup–Iteration Crossover Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem sizes and solve counts where setup investment changes comparative performance.

assumptions_latex: Solver \(A\) has setup cost \(S_A\) and constant marginal iteration cost \(c_A\); solver \(B\) has \(S_B\) and \(c_B\).
Both solvers require the same iteration count \(K\) to reach a fixed accuracy criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lower-latency solver changes, when it changes at all, at \(K_*=\frac{S_B-S_A}{c_A-c_B}\).

notation.meaning: setup costs of solvers A and B

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine latency model with equal accuracy-matched iteration counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the affine models \(T_A(K)=S_A+Kc_A\) and \(T_B(K)=S_B+Kc_B\), a positive crossover exists exactly when
\[
K_* = \frac{S_B-S_A}{c_A-c_B}>0,
\]
with \(c_A\ne c_B\). For integer iteration counts, comparison uses the sign of \(T_A(K)-T_B(K)\) on the two sides of \(K_*\). If \(c_A=c_B\), setup cost alone determines the ranking and no finite crossover occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In an affine timing model, setup and iteration costs exchange dominance at a positive crossover count; equal marginal costs preclude a finite crossover.
knowledge_statements.title: Setup–Iteration Crossover Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The crossover formula is algebraically correct under the stated affine equal-iteration model, and the condition kind fits the regime leaf. A source is still needed to justify this model as a QP solver-comparison diagnostic.

assumptions_latex: Every solver is run on the same QP instance and hardware environment.
A solver-independent residual normalization and target tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) are fixed before timing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only runs satisfying the common accuracy predicate are eligible for latency or resource ranking.

notation.meaning: common dimensionless primal and dual residuals at termination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver comparison at a common primal-dual residual threshold.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.1 First-Order Methods p. 232
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A run is accuracy-matched at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) precisely when its returned point satisfies
\[
\max\{\widehat r_{\mathrm p},\widehat r_{\mathrm d}\}\le\varepsilon,
\]
using the same residual definitions, norms, and original-coordinate scaling for every solver. Latency \(T\), iteration count, or energy may be ranked only among matched runs. A timeout or termination above \(\varepsilon\) is reported as failure or censoring, not as a faster matched solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Benchmark rankings compare only runs that satisfy the same normalized primal-dual accuracy target; premature termination is recorded separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy-Matched Benchmarking

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.1 First-Order Methods p. 232
source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the benchmarking leaf, but the cited first-order-methods section does not clearly support the specific accuracy-matched benchmarking and censoring protocol.

children.title: Warm-Start Bias
children.top_down_role: Comparison distortions caused by unequal initial iterates or solution proximity.

assumptions_latex: A benchmark contains an ordered sequence of related QP instances.
At least one solver receives state derived from a preceding instance while another starts from a fixed neutral state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The observed timing difference cannot be attributed solely to the compared solver algorithms.

notation.meaning: measured latency from a warm initial state
measured latency from the declared neutral state

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Confounding caused by unequal access to prior primal, dual, or active-set state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the warm-start advantage on a fixed instance by
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm w}=T_{\mathrm{cold}}-T_{\mathrm{warm}}.
\]
Warm-start bias is present when solver rankings use timings for which prior primal variables, multipliers, active sets, or adaptive parameters are supplied to only some runs, or are generated by unequal histories. Unless warm and cold regimes are stratified and identically applied, the ranking conflates algorithm performance with transferred state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm-start bias occurs when compared runs receive unequal prior solution state, so timing differences mix solver performance with transferred information.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Bias

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and statement match warm-start confounding, but the operational definition and required stratification have no cited support.

children.title: Factorization-Cache Bias
children.top_down_role: Comparison distortions caused by unequal reuse of symbolic or numeric factors.

assumptions_latex: Compared runs solve the same QP or QPs with the same sparsity pattern.
At least one run reuses solver-owned factorization or symbolic-analysis artifacts unavailable to another run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting end-to-end timing ranking is confounded by unequal preprocessing reuse.

notation.meaning: latency with reusable artifacts already cached
latency after required artifacts are cleared

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Confounding from unequal reuse of symbolic analysis, numerical factors, preconditioners, or compiled kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the cache advantage on a fixed instance by
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm c}=T_{\mathrm{rebuild}}-T_{\mathrm{cache}}.
\]
Factorization-cache bias is present when a reported comparison includes cached symbolic analysis, numerical factors, preconditioners, compiled kernels, or device-resident data for some runs but charges their construction to others. Such timings estimate different computational tasks unless cache state is equalized or cached and rebuild regimes are reported separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factorization-cache bias arises when some timings reuse preprocessing artifacts while others pay to construct them, making the measured tasks unequal.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Cache Bias

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind correctly captures unequal cache reuse, but the proposed taxonomy and reporting requirement require a source.

children.title: Benchmark Isolation Controls
children.top_down_role: Reporting boundaries that separate cold-start, warm-start, cached, and uncached performance.

assumptions_latex: Each solver is evaluated on the same declared instance set, hardware state, accuracy rule, and repetition schedule.
Cold and warm regimes are treated as distinct experimental conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting samples isolate declared solver costs sufficiently for accuracy-matched comparison.

notation.meaning: number of repetitions per controlled regime

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum controls for separating state reuse from solver latency and accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An isolated benchmark fixes \(\varepsilon\), residual scaling, hardware synchronization, thread count, and instance order; executes \(M\ge1\) repetitions under each declared regime; and records \(T_{\mathrm{setup}}\) separately from \(T_{\mathrm{iter}}\). Before every cold run it clears solver state and reusable artifacts within the declared boundary. Warm-start and cache-reuse runs are labeled separately and receive equivalent prior information. Only runs meeting the common accuracy predicate enter performance summaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Isolation controls equalize accuracy, hardware, ordering, repetitions, initial state, and caches while reporting setup and iteration timing separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Benchmark Isolation Controls

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the controls leaf and the protocol is internally coherent, but its asserted minimum isolation controls and sufficiency conclusion lack supporting evidence.
